USDtb is sensible collateral for a system that wants a quiet corner of traditional finance, with the caveat that each link in that chain is a separate point of failure.

zeusd-zoth.title: Zoth's Deprecated V1 Dollar
zeusd-zoth.text: ZeUSD is the token of Zoth's deprecated V1 stack, an RWA escrow receipt whose router is paused on-chain and whose backing has not been evidenced since the March 2025 exploits. The tracked V1 was never the continuing {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} it was labelled as: the router records collateral value and debt at mint and returns exactly what was recorded on burn, with no position-health checks and no liquidation path. The March 2025 exploits combined a liquidity-pool logic flaw with an admin-key compromise that let the attacker upgrade contracts and drain roughly $8.4M. Zoth still lists eligible {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral categories but publishes no current allocation, attestation, or proof of reserves, so the reserve is carried as a fully unresolved envelope and the backing pillar is scored on limited evidence. The exit and economic-control pillars sit at the floor: no comparable exit route is established, every admin and upgrade key resolves to a single Zoth EOA, and the token crosses chains only through a third-party LayerZero lockbox. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects all three. Pharos's June 2026 notice recorded market pricing far below par on thin public liquidity against a nominal supply in the tens of millions of units; the peg line on the card rests on a single price source, which says more about the absence of a market than about the token.

zchf-frankencoin.title: The Oracle-Free Franc
zchf-frankencoin.text:
A CHF-pegged CDP with auction-priced collateral, no oracle dependency, and no team tokens, carrying a single-name equity position that its purist design was never meant to hold.

Frankencoin remains the most ideologically committed stablecoin on the dashboard: no foundation, no team tokens, no VC money, and no price oracles. Its overall grade is {{grade}}, with exit quality near the top of the card. The asterisk still sits in the collateral pool: a single corporate equity, BOSS (Boss Info AG), remains roughly a third of the backing. It rivals wrapped BTC as the largest position, and that single-name concentration keeps the backing pillar below the exit pillar, while economic control is now the weakest of the three. Collateral is still valued through auction-based {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} that trades capital efficiency for oracle-manipulation resistance, a tradeoff most {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} protocols wouldn't dare make, with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} enforced through veto-governed minting limits. The peg has held near par with only a handful of shallow deviations in its history, notable for a CHF token priced against dollar reference rates on thin liquidity. On the regulatory front the pragmatism continues: the Frankencoin Association joined the MiCA Crypto Alliance in June 2026. The thing to watch is unchanged: the gap between Frankencoin's decentralization purity and its collateral discipline.

sources.label: MiCA Crypto Alliance welcomes Frankencoin Association (26 June 2026)

usn-noon.title: Yield Portfolio, Base Token
usn-noon.text: Noon's USN is the base dollar in a yield machine that would prefer you notice the par wrapper before the credit stack. The Accountable real-time feed Pharos reads puts most reserves in Fasanara private credit, with a material Treasury-bill sleeve and smaller CLO, HYPE funding-rate arbitrage, and Morpho and Euler lending positions behind it, and backing is the weakest of the three pillars on the card. Base USN does not itself accrue the yield; that job belongs to sUSN, while USN holders still rely on the same permissioned mint and redemption machinery. The setup is more transparent than many credit-backed dollars, but transparency does not ensure that private-credit liquidity arrives during stress. USN is stablecoin-shaped, yet the balance sheet underneath reads more like an institutional yield portfolio with a dollar label taped to the front.

honey-berachain.title: Proof of Liquidity's Dollar
honey-berachain.text: HONEY is Berachain's native dollar, minted 1:1 through the HoneyFactory against a governance-approved basket of USDC.e, USDT0, BYUSD, and USDe held in dedicated collateral vaults. The {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop with atomic settlement is the headline: HONEY can always be unwound into its constituent stablecoins, and Basket Mode works like a multi-asset {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}, which is more than most basket tokens offer. What the listing pages miss is the actual mix. At the July 2026 on-chain capture the registered vaults held USDe almost exclusively, with only trace balances of the three fiat-backed coins, so Pharos scores the backing as a single Ethena dependency rather than a diversified basket. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that: backing is the strongest pillar on architecture, exit is the weakest because on-chain depth is shallow relative to headline supply, and economic control sits between them because a 3-of-5 Berachain Safe can upgrade both the token and the factory immediately and can blacklist or pause holders. The peg record carries a long tail of brief early episodes, including one large upward spike, that pointed to thin two-sided liquidity rather than backing failure, and stress monitoring has not always sat at the calm end of the scale. It is a sound mechanism whose safety now rests on USDe and on its host chain.

sources.label: Berachain HONEY collateral and vault documentation

wusd-worldwide.title: The Exit Toll
wusd-worldwide.text:
A dollar token that lost every venue it traded on, then charged a hundred of itself to leave the one still standing.

WSPN's Worldwide USD shed roughly 94% of its circulating supply between 2026-07-21 and mid-August: 9.99M down to 0.61M, with two burns on 07-29 and 08-01 doing most of the work. No issuer statement has accompanied the contraction. The centralized exits closed in the same window: MEXC delisted on 07-25, Bitget dropped WUSD/USDT on 07-31, and Coins.ph, the flagship retail pair, left on 08-04 with the tidy explanation that WUSD was "no longer able to adhere to our listing standards." What remains is a single Viction pool that in mid-August quoted around $0.95 and whose ~$96k headline reserve absorbed roughly $490 before moving 2%, which is why Pharos now publishes no price rather than a number nothing trades at. Direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} still functions, but only through corporate accounts that qualified businesses must apply and be verified for. A holder without a WSPN relationship is routed to a secondary market that no longer exists. The detail worth pausing on sits on Viction, where the VRC25 deployment levies a flat 100 WUSD on token calls: amount-independent, verified on-chain, and charged on approve() as well as transfer(), meaning a wallet must hold $100 of a dollar token before it can authorise a swap of any size. Pharos had WUSD at the bottom of its scale before any of this happened; the reserve brochure was never the binding constraint.

sources.label: Bitget: notice of delisting 6 spot trading pairs, 2026-07-31
Viction VRC25 issuer registry entry for WUSD (100 WUSD fee)

frxusd-frax.title: Frax's Clean Slate
frxusd-frax.text: frxUSD is Frax's tokenized-{{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}}-backed dollar minted and redeemed 1:1 through governance-approved custodians, a {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} do-over without legacy FRAX's algorithmic baggage. The balance sheet is narrower than the custodian roster suggests: WisdomTree's WTGXX government money-market fund is the largest holding, Superstate USTB and BlackRock BUIDL sit behind it, and a small Bridge USDB position plus a segregated bank account round it out, while the enshrined-custodian design gives users a direct exit whenever the relevant collateral is available. Governance has approved more custodians than the reserve actually uses: Superstate USCC, Agora AUSD, and Centrifuge JTRSY each cleared a FIP without ever carrying a balance, a useful reminder that an approval is a permission, not a position. The sfrxUSD wrapper passes through reserve yield, which is modestly useful and mercifully not the whole pitch. The real trade-off is concentration in a small club of tokenized-money issuers, plus Frax DAO's power to approve who holds the money and to revoke that approval. It is institutional infrastructure arranged by a crypto protocol: much tidier than old FRAX, but not magically free of gatekeepers.

usyc-hashnote.title: Circle USYC Goes Multichain
usyc-hashnote.text: USYC is Hashnote's tokenized short-duration fund share now wearing Circle's distribution jacket. The reserve mix is the clean TradFi part: mostly U.S. Treasury bills with reverse repo agreements, redeemable at NAV rather than pretending every token is a static dollar bill. That NAV behavior matters because USYC is yield-bearing fund exposure, not a payment stablecoin, and Pharos treats the issuer controls accordingly. Circle's rebrand and multichain push make the wrapper easier to move around, but the legal and operational substance remains fund administration, eligible access, and issuer-operated minting. It is a very respectable money-market instrument cosplaying just enough as crypto to become collateral elsewhere.

eurr-stablr.title: Hacked, Frozen, Compliant
eurr-stablr.text: EURR was StablR's Malta-MFSA MiCA euro e-money token, with Grant Thornton {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, Tether's strategic backing, and the full compliance stack, until a May 24, 2026 cybersecurity incident ended the experiment mid-stride. An attacker compromised StablR's minting infrastructure and printed 4.5 million unbacked EURR alongside its dollar sibling USDR; minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} were frozen, and StablR disclosed that circulating supply was no longer fully backed at the 1:1 ratio MiCAR requires. Pharos no longer scores it at all; EURR sits in the archive as a frozen incident asset, because a report card presumes a functioning redemption promise and this one has been suspended since May. StablR's recovery-plan updates through June announced forensics and specialists, not restored minting, redemption, or full backing, so the token trades, where it trades at all, on hope of recovery rather than on a claim. The Tether connection that once framed the institutional-trust question now reads differently: distribution muscle is worthless when the mint key is the thing that broke. Whether Malta's MFSA carries the weight of France's ACPR in the MiCA hierarchy is being answered in an enforcement file, not a marketing deck.

usdr-stablr.title: One Key From Compliant
usdr-stablr.text: StablR's USDR holds a Malta MFSA EMI license under MiCA with 100% reserves in cash and short-term government bonds, reviewed quarterly by Grant Thornton. The regulatory stack includes formal {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} that checks every European compliance box while the market barely notices at single-digit-millions in supply. Then May 2026 rewrote the story: an attacker compromised StablR's 1-of-3 minting multisig and printed $13.5 million of unbacked USDR and EURR, the quote broke violently below par, and the issuer froze minting and redemption while disclosing to Malta's MFSA that circulating supply was no longer fully 1:1 backed. That violated MiCA's cardinal requirement, and it happened to a MiCA poster child. Weeks later the report card reads F with the primary market still suspended, and the thin single-pool Ethereum footprint that once merely embarrassed the liquidity score now defines the only exit anyone has. With liquidity that shallow, any meaningful exit runs through StablR's own issuer API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route rather than the order book. Europe's MiCA framework was supposed to be the catalyst for regulated stablecoins; USDR is now the test of what the framework does after the incident report is filed.

usdo-openeden.title: Treasury Yield, Repackaged
usdo-openeden.text: OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing dollar that distributes tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} yield by growing holder balances daily, backed mostly by OpenEden's own TBILL token with BUIDL, VBILL, and a thin stablecoin buffer beneath it. The trust chain is considerably longer than the $1 label implies. The {{grade}} overall grade rests on one finding: the Bermuda Monetary Authority's regulated-entities register was read directly and upholds OpenEden Digital's digital-asset business licence, so prudential supervision is evidenced rather than asserted. Be clear about what the rest of that grade rests on. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars. Reconciliation is graded periodic rather than continuous. No issuer artefact names a reconciliation series, the Chainlink feed that does exist covers only the Treasury sleeve and diverges from the issuer's own full-basket figure, and the documentation's transparency page has been future-tense about a public dashboard for more than half a year. Pharos's own proof-of-reserves record grades that identical endpoint as self-verification with partial liability coverage, which makes this the thinnest evidence supporting a passing grade anywhere in its class, and the grade should be read as provisional. The rebasing design also stays awkward for anything that cannot handle a moving balance, which is precisely why cUSDO exists.

usda-anzens.title: Reserves Described, Not Attested
usda-anzens.text: Anzens USDA claims clean backing on Cardano: USD cash, {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills, and Treasury money-market funds in segregated accounts under BitGo Trust {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, issued by a FinCEN-registered MSB. It nevertheless carries a very poor peg record, with hundreds of recorded episodes and a price feed Pharos rates low-confidence. The problem starts with the chain and ends with the paperwork. Cardano-only deployment leaves no arbitrage infrastructure to enforce the peg, and mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through KYC-verified bank transfers for users in eligible U.S. states only, so exit is the weakest of the three pillars. Backing cannot compensate: the issuer names the eligible reserve categories but publishes no current weights, and the reviewed homepage and terms carry no attestation, audit, or assets-and-liabilities reconciliation that a reader could check. Economic control is the one pillar that scores well, because the Cardano mint policy executes only on mint and burn and cannot freeze ordinary transfers. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects reserves that are described rather than demonstrated. Sound reserves are necessary but nowhere near sufficient; the system also needs a market that can trade the thing and an issuer willing to publish a document somebody can actually read.

sources.label: Anzens terms and conditions (reserve categories, no attestation)

usdf-falcon.title: Falcon's BTC-Heavy Synthetic Dollar
usdf-falcon.text: Falcon Finance's USDf is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar whose reserve, at the latest reviewed snapshot, was overwhelmingly BTC, with USDC, USDT, an insurance fund, ETH, and an aggregated long tail of altcoins and tokenized assets making up the small remainder. The altcoin-collateral pitch that set Falcon apart from Ethena survives as mintable collateral; it is barely visible in the reserve itself. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by economic control, the weakest of the three pillars. Falcon's terms make an internally calculated spot price, set at its sole discretion, the authority for minting, {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, and settlement, with no independent feed, heartbeat, or fallback published. The Ethereum proxy can also be upgraded through a zero-delay admin owned by a 4-of-6 Safe. Backing sits in the middle of the card: Falcon publishes a per-asset reserve breakdown and weekly self-reports, but no reconciled hedge notionals or net delta. The bulk of assets sit in Falcon-controlled multisig wallets rather than with a third-party custodian, and the independent assurance series from ht.digital has fallen behind the weekly reports. The peg mostly behaves, but a long tail of brief episodes suggests the hedging book stumbles under stress, and the exit pillar is only middling with a restriction list on the token. USDf is only as sound as the price Falcon chooses to publish.

europ-schuman.title: Credentials Without Scale
europ-schuman.text: EUROP is Schuman Financial's ACPR-licensed euro stablecoin, backed by euro cash and cash equivalents at Société Générale and Banking Circle, with quarterly KPMG reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} and direct 1:1 redemption through the issuer. Schuman stacks every credential the euro stablecoin market demands, yet its float remains small. The latest KPMG report, which describes itself as neither an audit nor a review, puts about a third of the reserve in bank cash and two thirds in cash equivalents whose instruments it does not name, with reserves a few percent above tokens in circulation. That undisclosed two thirds is the one soft spot in an otherwise strong backing pillar, which leads the card. The {{grade}} overall grade reads mid-table because exit is the weakest pillar and economic control sits only slightly higher: the sober arithmetic of a token whose paperwork cannot conjure market depth or dilute issuer control. The peg itself holds near the top of the scale, with dozens of brief blips that read as thin-market noise rather than structural instability. Distribution spans XRPL, Plasma and Solana alongside the usual EVM chains, all issuer-native. But distribution without depth just spreads the same thin float across more order books.

brz-transfero.title: Pegged to Volatility Itself
brz-transfero.text: BRZ is Transfero's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 by KYC'd users against BRL cash held in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at a Brazilian institution; its depeg history tracks the real against the dollar rather than any reserve failure. The long tail of recorded depeg episodes, including deep swings far below peg, is what happens when you peg a token to the Brazilian real and price it against dollar-denominated markets. The {{grade}} overall grade follows from that FX-driven peg record once the v9 peg multiplier gets involved. The backing pillar is the weakest of the three and cannot rescue the score because Pharos scores current reserve evidence rather than issuer claims: the only reachable reserve report is dated March 2024, is self-published, and names no custodian, so no current composition is on file. The exit story has improved from the basement but remains a standing constraint: a 1% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee through Transfero's offchain issuer path still means the cleanest way out of any sizable position is the issuer window, not the secondary market. Deployed across more than a dozen chains, BRZ serves a genuine need in Latin America's largest crypto market, but thin liquidity and the underlying FX exposure are a standing reminder that non-USD stablecoins carry risks no reserve structure can hedge away.

rlusd-ripple.title: Ripple's Settlement Dollar
rlusd-ripple.text: Ripple's NYDFS-supervised dollar is backed by a very-low-risk reserve split across {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}, and cash, examined monthly by Deloitte under a New York trust charter, with BNY as primary reserve custodian. That reserve is the kind of boring institutional machinery a settlement token should have, and RLUSD is very much a settlement token rather than a DeFi primitive. The {{grade}} overall grade rests on the exit pillar, the strongest line on the card, since issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is permissionless and 1:1; backing is the weakest of the three only by a narrow margin, because the depository institutions, money-market funds, and custodians beyond BNY are not named and bankruptcy remoteness rests on contract rather than statute. Brief depeg events from early price discovery are less a reserve indictment than a reminder that new tokens need time to build market plumbing. DEX liquidity remains concentrated in a handful of pools, consistent with a payments corridor product whose real exit is issuer redemption. Pharos records RLUSD as an e-money token that is not MiCA-compliant, and the two-chain footprint on Ethereum and XRPL is issuer-native with no third-party bridge. RLUSD looks sturdy, but it is sturdy in the way a bank product is sturdy: excellent paperwork, narrow on-chain spontaneity.

feusd-felix.title: Liquity Fork on Hyperliquid
feusd-felix.text: feUSD is a Liquity-v2-fork {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on Hyperliquid, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by HYPE ecosystem tokens: concentrated chain risk, sturdy redemption mechanics. Felix Protocol cloned Liquity V2 onto Hyperliquid's unproven L1 and loaded the CDPs with HYPE and its liquid-staking derivatives, an asset class Pharos rates very-high risk, alongside bridged Bitcoin. The v9 report card renders a cleaner verdict than any blended score could: backing and exit both grade well, thanks to zero-fee atomic collateral {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and an interest-rate-sorted queue, yet the {{grade}} overall grade is dragged down because economic control is the weakest pillar by a wide margin: a multisig still holds the admin keys, caps, and pause, the HyperCore representation's bridge controls remain unresolved, and v9 treats that kind of mint authority as a first-class risk. The peg score remains strong despite a long tail of brief episodes, and stress monitoring has not always sat at the calm end of the scale. The structural caveat remains: when your primary collateral is the native token of the chain you live on, a single ecosystem shock hits both your backing and your exit {{term:liquidation}}liquidity simultaneously{{/term}}: good pillar grades measure the machinery, not the correlation.

dusd-standx.title: The Quiet Basis Trader
dusd-standx.text: DUSD is StandX's {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar: an Ethena-style {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} through Ceffu {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with less theater and less public verification. The reserve model is mostly spot-long and {{term:perpetual}}perp-short{{/term}} exposure on BTC, ETH and SOL, plus a small stability buffer, so the product lives or dies by CEX operations and hedging discipline. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects exotic collateral, centralized custody, no published proof of reserves, and an issuer-API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path, none of which are small footnotes. The peg record has looked cleaner than the structure deserves, which suggests the desk knows what it is doing as long as the infrastructure beneath it behaves. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the card: the Solana mint and freeze authority sit with a StandX program that can freeze individual accounts, and the backend signer set behind settlement is undisclosed. Trusting a basis trader is one thing; verifying the basis trader is the part StandX still leaves mostly off-chain.

eurcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SG-FORGE's Single-Bank Euro
eurcv-societe-generale-forge.text: EURCV is SG-FORGE's MiCA euro stablecoin, issued by the digital-asset arm of Société Générale with reserves held entirely as euro cash at the parent bank, disclosed daily by the issuer and offered with 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through SG-FORGE. The {{grade}} overall grade is a story about concentration rather than quality. The exit pillar leads the card, and backing grades well on a fully cash reserve reconciled daily against circulation, but the reserve, the {{term:custody}}custodian{{/term}}, and the issuer are the same banking group, and the daily disclosure is self-verified rather than examined by an outside auditor. Economic control is the weakest pillar: Ethereum minting is restricted to one immutable registrar account, and upgrades run through a single technical account once the registrar approves them, so two externally owned keys stand between EURCV and its contract logic. The peg record is spotless across more than three years of tracking, with no depeg episode logged and stress readings that have stayed at the calm end of the scale. Deployment spans Ethereum, XRPL, Stellar and Solana as issuer-native lanes, with Stellar carrying a material share. Whether EURCV becomes tokenised money at scale depends on distribution, and until then its safety case is exactly as strong as Société Générale.

yusd-aegis.title: Real-Time Proof, Unmeasured Unwind
yusd-aegis.text: Aegis YUSD is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar built on BTC: spot held under institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Copper and Fireblocks, hedged with COIN-M {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts, with {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} income passed to holders. The Accountable dashboard publishes the reserve split in real time, and Pharos reads it directly. What it does not publish is the unwind: no position-level hedge size, market depth, or measured time-to-close for the spot and short book, so the custody buckets sit in the reserve envelope as an undisclosed mix of spot, hedge, and margin exposure. That gap is why backing is the weakest of the three pillars on the {{grade}} card, while the exit pillar leads it and economic control sits between. Issuance runs through a single trusted-signer path under a 3-of-5 Safe with no timelock and no active mint cap on Ethereum, and the same owner can blacklist holders. The peg score is strong, but the history carries a long tail of brief episodes and at least one deep excursion, the usual signature of a {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} priced by exchange availability. Real-time disclosure shows the positions; it does not establish how quickly they could be closed.

reusd-resupply.title: Leverage All the Way Down
reusd-resupply.text: Resupply's reUSD is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} coin minted against Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares, so its collateral is itself earning yield on other stablecoins, and a 1% communal {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee sets the price floor. The {{grade}} overall grade is low, with the exit pillar the weakest of the three, and hundreds of recorded depeg events tell the tale of exotic collateral doing exotic things. The live pair registry puts more than nine tenths of the collateral in crvUSD lending markets, with the rest in Fraxlend, so the coin inherits both peg keepers' failure domains. DEX liquidity remains thin and concentrated relative to supply, so any serious exit leans on the communal redemption floor rather than the order book. The June 2025 oracle-manipulation exploit created roughly $9.6M of bad debt, which was repaid through treasury funds, insurance-pool burns, and a Yearn DAO loan. This is the footnote explaining why the vault plumbing earns skepticism. The token itself has no freeze or blacklist path and is minted only under on-chain governance. reUSD has spent more of its life on the stressed side of Pharos's monitoring than the calm one, and the market prices it as a recursive instrument rather than a stable store of value. The design suits farming rather than parking.

tbill-openeden.title: T-Bills With a Token Wrapper
tbill-openeden.text: OpenEden's TBILL is a tokenized BVI professional fund holding short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills managed by BNY Investment Management under BNY custody, KYC-gated and drifting steadily above its original dollar as NAV accrues to holders rather than resetting to par. The structure functions as intended: professional investors collect on-chain Treasury yield through issuer-side mint and redemption at NAV, and everyone else can look but not touch. The paperwork is thinner than the institutional nameplates suggest. Daily NAV figures come from fund administrator Protege Fund Services, the annual auditor has published no report, and the only named controls work is a one-off Ernst & Young procedures review rather than a recurring {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. The gating has now reached its logical conclusion: since mid-July Pharos has held TBILL in quarantine because permitted market-data sources report no positive circulating supply, so the token currently carries no report card at all. The NAV oracle keeps ticking upward while the supply side of the ledger is simply invisible. A token with no DEX pools and no permissionless mint has limited market exposure, and that same construction makes TBILL unmeasurable. TBILL has become so private that even the public data can't find it.

a7a5-old-vector.title: Ruble Token Under Sanctions
a7a5-old-vector.text: A7A5 is Old Vector LLC's centralized ruble stablecoin, issued under a Kyrgyz VASP license for the Promsvyazbank-owned A7 network; issuer materials describe the backing only as an undisclosed basket of ruble deposits and short-term assets, and no reserve artefact has ever been published. The architecture is technically compliant at home while functionally untouchable by Western financial infrastructure, and since February 2026 the issuer has passed nearly all reserve income to holders as additional A7A5 at the CBR key rate minus one percentage point, making it one of the few {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoins whose holders directly capture a sanctioned banking system's deposit rate. The net keeps tightening: the EU's 21st sanctions package, adopted in July 2026, stopped sanctioning around the edges and designated the A7 payments network itself: A7 Agent, A71, and its African affiliates, alongside some fifteen crypto platforms including HTX, with the measures biting from late August. A7A5 has no on-chain RUB liquidity, so the USD price print follows RUB/USD spot rather than arbitrage, and the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} loop runs entirely through KYC'd off-chain partners. Pharos records a long tail of peg episodes on a single-source feed, and the durable constraint is that no reserve schedule, bank identity, or custody arrangement has been published, so the backing claim rests on the issuer's word inside a sanctioned banking perimeter.

sources.label: CoinGeek: EU 21st sanctions package designates A7 network and HTX (adopted 2026-07-23)

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: World Liberty Financial Dollar
usd1-world-liberty-financial.text: World Liberty Financial's USD1 is politically loud and structurally conventional. Under the Trump-affiliated wrapper sits a BitGo-issued dollar backed by a government money-market fund and bank deposits under an OCC national trust charter, with Crowe examinations and a Chainlink reserve feed. The product risk comes from centralized issuer control, role-gated minting, issuer-only {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, and uncertainty over whether the brand helps distribution or narrows the buyer pool to people already nodding. Exit is the weakest of the three pillars, because no comparable same-notional route out exists beyond the issuer, and that is what holds the {{grade}} overall grade down while the peg has held near par for over a year. Pharos therefore reads USD1 as a regulated stablecoin with a political brand attached rather than a new monetary primitive. The reserves are the least dramatic part of the product; the durable constraint is the single issuer route out.

sources.label: Crowe USD1 Reserve Attestation Report - May 2026

usdx-hex-trust.title: Claimed Treasuries, No Exit
usdx-hex-trust.text: Hex Trust's USDX advertises T-bill and cash reserves at global tier-1 banks under Hong Kong issuer disclosures, which makes its {{grade}} safety grade a case study in how clean-sounding reserves mean nothing without functional market infrastructure. Supply sits across Ethereum, Flare, and Songbird, but Pharos finds no viable exit path: the exit pillar sits at the floor of the scale, and a single thin DEX pool is no liquidity profile. The peg record shows a long tail of depeg episodes, with the worst excursions taking the token to a fraction of par despite the claim of Treasuries behind it. Claiming is the operative word, since the issuer page's reserve panel remains a placeholder, no dated independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} or reserve-to-liability reconciliation is linked, and no current reserve composition is on file for the backing pillar to score. Stress monitoring has at times registered elevated stress, since without a two-sided market price gaps persist rather than close. Economic control is the one strong pillar on the card. Hex Trust's {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} credentials have not translated into the on-chain arbitrage loops that keep prices honest, and issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for approved parties cannot substitute for the missing secondary market. Custodial credibility and stablecoin stability remain different problems, and USDX is priced on the second.

pusd-plume.title: USDC With a Detour
pusd-plume.text: Plume's pUSD takes USDC, routes it through a Nucleus BoringVault with OFAC compliance checks, and issues a wrapped token on Ethereum and Plume Chain, adding smart contract risk, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} abstraction, and a new trust layer to an asset that was already perfectly functional. The {{grade}} overall grade has recovered as exit liquidity moved from outright failing to merely thin, and the exit pillar is still the weakest of the three. Zero-fee same-day {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} suggests the wrapper functions, and the August 2026 reconciliation shows vault USDC and bridged USDC.e matching pUSD supply almost to the token, but the deviation history records more than a dozen blips capped by one catastrophic excursion far below par. The wrapper emphatically failed at least once. Supply remains small with on-chain depth to match, raising the question of whether the RWAfi ecosystem narrative generates enough demand to justify the wrapper's existence. The vault is immutable and Safe-governed, which is why economic control is the strongest line on the card, but the exit history is what a listing page would miss.

bold-liquity.title: Liquity V2's Immutable Dollar
bold-liquity.text: BOLD is Liquity V2's decentralized dollar stablecoin, minted from immutable {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults against WETH, wstETH, and rETH only: no governance keys, no admin functions, no RWA exposure. The {{grade}} report card shows what that discipline buys: exit and economic control are the two strongest pillars, with permissionless atomic collateral {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} providing one of DeFi's hardest peg floors, while user-set interest rates and Stability Pool yield create self-correcting incentives that keep BOLD close to par. The one concession is a backing pillar a notch below the rest: the volatility premium for holding ETH and its staking derivatives instead of T-bills, which is precisely the trade Liquity's users signed up for. What holds the overall grade back today is age: the binding cap on the card is a track-record limit for a design still short of two years of implementation history. Supply now spreads across a multichain footprint transported by Chainlink CCIP rather than native issuance, so the non-Ethereum balances carry that external validation assumption. The cap lifts with time; the CCIP dependency does not.

avusd-avant.title: Redeemable Receipt, Leveraged Book
avusd-avant.text: avUSD is Avant's centralized dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 for USDC and deployed into actively managed {{term:delta-neutral}}market-neutral{{/term}} strategies for yield: avUSD itself does not accrue yield, the staked savUSD does. USDC is the mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rail rather than the reserve itself: deposited capital is routed into a leveraged market-neutral book spanning basis trades, lending arbitrage, and private liquidity deals, with the avUSDx junior tranche and a separate reserve fund absorbing strategy losses first, which is why backing sits as the weakest pillar on the {{grade}} report card. Users stake avUSD into the separately tracked savUSD senior tranche when they want yield exposure, while avUSD remains the redeemable receipt for USDC exits at a 5-basis-point fee and a one-to-seven-day settlement window. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and BVI domicile mean trust runs through Avant's operational integrity rather than a regulatory framework, which is why the backstop redemption remains queue-based rather than a hard on-chain par floor. A string of recorded depegs, with the worst reading several hundred basis points from par, shows the market can still stress the wrapper even when the peg has mostly held.

ylds-figure.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
ylds-figure.text: YLDS is a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing stablecoin{{/term}} issued by Figure Certificate Company as a face-amount certificate registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Investment Company Act of 1940. It pays SOFR minus 35 basis points, accrued daily, and mints and redeems 1:1 through Figure with mandatory KYC. The audited FY2025 schedules show overnight {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} repo at UMB Bank as roughly three quarters of the qualified assets and short-dated Treasury bills as most of the remainder, with KPMG's audit opinion covering the schedules of investments. Native issuance sits on Provenance and Stellar; the Solana and Ethereum tokens are Hastra wYLDS bridge representations moving over Chainlink CCIP, which Pharos scores under bridge risk rather than Figure's own mint authority. The trade-off is the one the registration implies: the exit pillar is the weakest line on the {{grade}} card because transfers are restrictable, accounts can be frozen, and redemption is eligibility-gated, while backing and economic control both grade comfortably higher. The certificates remain unsecured obligations of FCC, and the filing establishes no statutory bankruptcy remoteness for the deposited assets.

sources.label: Figure Certificate Company FY2025 Form 10-K (KPMG audit opinion dated 2026-03-19)
Stellar press release: Figure launches YLDS on the Stellar network
YLDS official site (rate and network availability)

usdq-quantoz.title: The Dutch Compliance Standard
usdq-quantoz.text: Quantoz's USDQ is the DNB-supervised, MiCAR-authorized e-money token that treats compliance as the product. The peg record is the strongest line on the card. The reserves read impeccably on paper: roughly 70% Netherlands, German, and U.S. government bonds and 30% cash at Tier 1 European banks, held in segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts at a ratio just above full backing. The catch is that Pharos has to take Quantoz's word for it. The transparency page is a self-published snapshot refreshed ad hoc, already weeks stale by the time anyone reads it, with no named auditor, no named banks, and no disclosed bond maturities. That evidence gap is why backing is the weakest of the three pillars despite sovereign-grade assets, and why the overall grade sits at {{grade}} for an otherwise clean profile. Distribution remains an afterthought too, with a small circulating footprint spread across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL, and Algorand. The lesson for the MiCAR cohort is uncomfortable: a regulator's blessing does not substitute for an attestation, and Pharos grades the evidence rather than the license.

sources.label: DNB public register: Quantoz Payments B.V.

usdn-noble.title: Noble Rebasing T-Bill Dollar
usdn-noble.text: Noble's USDN is a rebasing dollar backed by M0's short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} structure, with collateral maintained by M0 minters and verified through on-chain {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}. That is a far more conventional reserve story than its Cosmos-native wrapper suggests: holders receive the accumulated T-bill yield while the protocol tracks their principal against M0's rebasing multiplier. The problem is USDN's need for demand, usable exits, and confidence in a layered bridge-and-minter arrangement, even though the collateral does not read like a casino chip. A stable peg can coexist with a very small market, because quiet is not the same thing as liquid. USDN is credible infrastructure looking for a reason not to be merely transit capital.

usdu-unitas.title: Unitas's Hedged-Book Dollar
usdu-unitas.text: Unitas's USDu is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar: on-chain collateral on Solana and BNB Smart Chain, including the long Jupiter LP leg Unitas documents, is paired with CEX {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts settled through Copper and Ceffu off-exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, so the entire reserve is an active {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} rather than idle assets. Accountable's live proof-of-solvency dashboard is a genuine upgrade over the 'trust us' school of yield products, and Pharos reads its venue split directly: on a recent capture roughly half the reserve sat on Solana, a third in Bitcoin collateral, and the remainder at Binance and on BSC, at a collateralization ratio a few points above par. What the dashboard does not itemize is what each venue holds, so hedge counterparties, margin, and per-venue instruments stay undisclosed and backing is graded on that partial view. Economic control is the strongest pillar by a wide margin, but exit is the weakest: direct mint and redeem against USDC is whitelist-restricted, leaving most holders dependent on secondary markets. The peg has held with only a short tail of brief episodes. Singapore-domiciled Unipay's terms reserve the right to freeze or burn USDu without notice, a legal control the permissionless token contracts do not show. The {{grade}} overall grade is what a working hedge earns when its primary exit is gated.

usdg-paxos.title: Paxos's Singapore Sequel
usdg-paxos.text: Paxos's USDG is its Singapore sequel: after BUSD wound down, Paxos relocated its stablecoin ambitions under a MAS Major Payment Institution licence, with a MiCA-authorized EU issuance through Paxos Issuance Europe OY layered on top. The reserve is textbook. At the latest KPMG examination, roughly half sat in a BNY Dreyfus government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}}, most of the rest in Treasury bills maturing within weeks, and a small cash sleeve at commercial banks in Singapore and Luxembourg, all in segregated accounts held for token holders. The report card reads accordingly: backing and economic control both sit at the top of the scale, the latter helped by a 24-hour timelock over supply control and upgrades. The exit pillar is the weakest of the three while still high. The gap between those pillars and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects a peg record that carries one severe early dislocation alongside a run of brief episodes, over a tracking history that only began in late 2024. Two structural facts deserve attention: bankruptcy remoteness rests on contract rather than a trust, since Paxos's explicit trust language covers only its Trust Company coins, and more than half of native supply sits on X Layer, a concentration Pharos measures as material. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Paxos Singapore for verified users is the core exit. The catch remains on-chain presence: a handful of chains and an institutional pedigree that still outpaces its DeFi footprint.

xsgd-straitsx.title: Southeast Asia's FX Shortcut
xsgd-straitsx.text: XSGD is the rare non-USD stablecoin that exists for a reason beyond novelty. It provides SGD-denominated on-chain liquidity for Southeast Asian payment flows where routing through dollar pairs adds pointless FX friction. The {{grade}} overall grade is earned: a MAS Major Payment Institution licence, segregated trust reserves explicitly excluded from the issuer's creditor estate, and twice-monthly independent examinations by KK Yap & Associates, most recently on the end-June position. The backing pillar carries a disclosure caveat: the reserve is no longer plain bank cash but close to an even split between cash and a short-dated MAS bill or eligible overnight repo category the report declines to break apart, with the safeguarding institution left unnamed. That is a rounding error in risk terms and a fair prompt for better disclosure, since half the backing is currently described by the bucket it is permitted to sit in rather than what it holds. Exit is the pillar trailing the rest of the card, even with direct par redemption through the licensed issuer. Past oracle-driven wobbles, the inherent hazard of pricing an SGD token against USD-denominated feeds on thin non-USD pairs, have mostly aged out, and genuine DEX depth spread across many pools rather than one fragile venue keeps XSGD tied to a working payment corridor.

sources.label: KK Yap & Associates XSGD SCS Reserve Account Report, 30 June 2026

xusd-straitsx.title: One Pool Holds Everything
xusd-straitsx.text:
Same MAS framework as XSGD, but a single dominant DEX pool makes XUSD institutional plumbing without an on-chain audience.

StraitsX's XUSD inherits the same MAS framework, DBS/StanChart/UOB {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and institutional-grade infrastructure as its XSGD sibling, with semi-monthly reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} still arriving on schedule. The most recent covered the end-June position, by which point the reserve had moved entirely to cash. The {{grade}} overall grade tells the real story: a near-flawless peg and top-grade backing dragged down by an exit pillar that is the weakest line on the card by a wide margin. One pool holds essentially everything, and the long tail of brief, mostly shallow depeg blips on record is exactly what thin markets produce. The circulating supply is respectable for a Singapore-issued dollar stablecoin, but it lives almost entirely off-chain. The on-chain footprint across its deployments is a ghost town. Stress signals have rarely strayed from the calm end of the scale and the backing and economic-control pillars both lead the card, confirming the institutional plumbing works fine; the problem is that nobody building in DeFi has a reason to choose it over USDC. The value proposition is regional FX corridors and StraitsX's banking relationships rather than DEX composability. The business is valid, but it does not show up in on-chain metrics.

sources.label: KK Yap & Associates XUSD SCS Reserve Account Report, 30 June 2026

vgbp-vnx.title: Twenty Pounds in Existence
vgbp-vnx.text: VNX's Liechtenstein-licensed pound was always a thin market; by the data's account it is now not a market at all. Pharos quarantined VGBP on 2026-07-19 after DefiLlama's supply feed reported zero circulating tokens, a condition no active listing can survive. The formal scaffolding that once flattered it reads differently in this light: the latest AREVA fiat-series report, dated end-2024 and never refreshed since, attested a grand total of 20.00 VGBP in existence, while issuance quietly migrated from VNX Commodities AG to a Bermuda-licensed VNX Global entity that report does not cover. Same-day issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and TVTG licensing remain on paper, but a sterling rail with no measurable supply and a stalled {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cycle is settlement infrastructure for settlements that are not happening. The UK regulatory wildcard now cuts the other way: if banks ever bring serious sterling liquidity on-chain, they will arrive to find the first mover already gone quiet. VGBP stays in quarantine until someone shows up holding it.

sources.label: AREVA VNX reserve report as of December 31, 2024

cusd-cap.title: Basket Wrapper, Mostly USDC
cusd-cap.text: cUSD is Cap's dollar minted against a governance-whitelisted vault of regulated stablecoins and tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}, with an EigenLayer AVS providing the economic security layer for the protocol's credit strategies. The pitch is diversification; the ledger is concentration. At Pharos's last fixed-block read the Ethereum vault held only two assets, roughly nine-tenths USDC and the rest WisdomTree's WTGXX fund shares, so the basket behaves as a USDC wrapper with an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} garnish. The mechanism is still the interesting part: dynamic fees on minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} keep utilisation below full so exits stay atomic, and redemptions return a proportional slice of every underlying asset, which socialises any single reserve depeg across all redeemers. That design earns the exit pillar the top line on the card, while backing is the weakest of the three pillars because one issuer dominates it. The {{grade}} overall grade also reflects a one-day timelock that can add assets, raise caps, or replace mint logic, and a protocol-wide transfer pause in the token itself. Native on Ethereum and Tempo with a LayerZero representation on MegaETH, cUSD is less an independent stablecoin than a wrapper whose safety is mostly Circle's, plus whatever the vault's credit strategies do with idle capital.

msusd-main-street.title: Redemption Target, Not A Clean Vault
msusd-main-street.text: msUSD is Main Street's dollar token with a USDC redemption target, but Pharos no longer treats it as a clean USDC reserve passthrough. Main Street documents 1:1 USDC minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for verified users, yet the redemption path is capacity-managed, cooldown-bound, and can require position unwinds, asset conversion, and strategy liquidity before settlement. The separate msY token still owns the explicit options-box {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} wrapper, but that split does not independently verify that unstaked msUSD is segregated from liquidity needed to support the strategy. The June 2026 depeg made that distinction material, so Pharos models msUSD with unresolved reserve-verification risk and very-high-risk reserve exposure rather than as fully backed idle USDC.

iusd-infinifi.title: Credit Book Behind a Redemption Queue
iusd-infinifi.text: InfiniFi's iUSD is a USDC-collateralized dollar with duration-matched private credit deployment: a liquid buffer available on demand, the rest in credit strategies with multi-week unwinds, and redemptions queued under stress. It routes USDC into institutional private credit from Fasanara, FalconX, Sentora, and Maple, behind a liquid DeFi buffer on Spark, Fluid, and Aave, with the siUSD savings wrapper passing through the yield. The structural tension the model was always going to face shows up exactly where the V9 report card says it should: the backing pillar earns respectable credit and the control surface passes, but the exit pillar fails outright and drags the overall grade to {{grade}} because most of the collateral cannot be pulled on demand, whatever the mint contract promises. The peg itself holds cleanly and stress monitoring has stayed at the calm end of the scale, but a flat stress reading is cold comfort when the real risk is a liquidity wall rather than a price wobble. The peg record is still clean, which either means the queue is doing exactly its job or that the redemption test that matters has not arrived. Functionally siUSD is a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper over private-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} positions, with the buffer-driven {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} queue acting as the gate when liquid reserves run thin. You are earning credit fund returns and bearing credit fund risks through a stablecoin interface.

pht-pht.title: Peso Stablecoin Pioneer
pht-pht.text: PHT is APACX's Philippine-peso stablecoin built like a Maker-style CDP system, but the beta reserve reality is narrower than the architecture brochure. APACX says all existing PHT was minted against custodial apcxUSDT backed 1:1 by USDT at one disclosed Tron wallet, yet live Ethereum reads show positive debt in five collateral branches, and no branch-level balances or reconciliation are published. That leaves holders with USDT dependency, custodial-wrapper risk, and unresolved privileged mint or admin risk sitting behind a familiar overcollateralized label. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped by the oracle design: the main live branches divide a Chainlink stablecoin/USD numerator by an owner-set APACX PHP/USD denominator with no contract-enforced freshness, so Pharos scores the pricing topology as opaque. Dutch-auction {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} make the mechanism legible, yet the exit pillar is the weakest of the three because no comparable redemption route is disclosed, and the Tron bridge representation runs unverified code. It is a useful experiment in peso-denominated DeFi rails, but the dashboard reads it as early machinery rather than mature monetary infrastructure.

hyusd-hylo.title: Volatility Sold Separately
hyusd-hylo.text: Hylo's HYUSD is the stable tranche of a dual-token design in which each pool's xASSET absorbs collateral-price swings before HYUSD holders take any. Leverage buyers do the unpleasant work, by construction. The disclosure gap that once separated Hylo's documented V2 from its deployed program has narrowed: V2 is live with isolated SOL-LST, cbBTC, HYPE, and USDC pools, and its xAsset Engine has already shipped a 3x bitcoin product, with leveraged equities still ambition rather than deployment. Pharos now measures the deployed pools directly, and the {{grade}} report card shows a solid backing pillar, with SOL-LST collateral making up the bulk of the book and pool liabilities reconciling to supply. Exit fails because on-chain liquidity for the stable tranche remains far thinner than the mechanism deserves. Economic control is the weakest pillar for a different reason: the token itself has no freeze authority, but the production oracle and liquidation topology of the recently upgraded programs is unresolved, and the 3-of-4 upgrade multisig can rewrite mint logic with no timelock. The peg record is nearly spotless. This is a reminder that {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} via volatility-absorbing tranches is only as sturdy as the leverage demand funding it. The pools now match their documentation; the order books and the oracle inventory have yet to match the design.

meusd-mezo.title: Liquity Mechanics, Off-Chain Admin Keys
meusd-mezo.text: Mezo's MUSD applies Liquity-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics to Bitcoin collateral at a 110% minimum ratio, with permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and atomic settlement on Mezo's Bitcoin L2, a chain Pharos classifies as unproven. The {{grade}} overall grade is lopsided: the exit pillar leads the card on those redemption mechanics, while backing is the weakest of the three because the collateral is a single BTC envelope whose native-versus-wrapped split is not published, and economic control sits between them. The Mezo token owner's 5-of-9 Safe administers the canonical mint list and can authorize additional minters, and the Ethereum and Base representations run through Wormhole NTT under that same Safe, so permissionless borrowing on Mezo coexists with very real admin keys off-chain. The owner can also grant arbitrary-account burn rights on every deployment. MUSD has logged a long tail of brief deviation episodes on both sides of par rather than a single break. A design this sturdy still depends on one concentrated owner key and a young chain.

usdu-usdu-finance.title: Undercollateralized by Design
usdu-usdu-finance.text: USDU Finance was refreshingly honest about what it was: an intentionally undercollateralized stablecoin at roughly 40% backing, minted through DAO-approved adapters connected to Curve, TermMax, and Morpho vault positions, designed explicitly for professional market participants who could price the risk. Apparently they priced it. Supply has since been all but wound down in a sharp, near-total contraction, and the issuer's transparency endpoint now reports backing roughly equal to the little that remains outstanding. The {{grade}} safety grade reflects v9's refusal to grade on a curve: a nearly empty book is easy to cover one-for-one, but three-quarters of what covers it is USDU-denominated Morpho and Curve positions rather than external collateral, so backing is the weakest of the three pillars, while unbounded mint authority and a supply too small to clear the peg floor cap the other two. The modular adapter architecture was genuinely interesting engineering: dynamic Curve liquidity management, fixed-rate TermMax lending, and Morpho vault integration. Building sophisticated infrastructure around a product that deliberately skipped the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} step is the kind of experiment that works until it doesn't. USDU's distinction is ending in the rare exit lane: wound down in orderly fashion before the market could write the depeg headline.

uty-xsy.title: Pristine Peg, Padlocked Exit
uty-xsy.text: XSY's UTY is an AVAX-hedged {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar minted 1:1 from USDC on Base, with Avalanche and Katana as LayerZero spokes and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} back to USDC only on Base after a 7-day unbonding period. It holds a {{grade}} overall grade, and the pillar spread tells the story. The peg record is the strongest line on the card: the {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} of long AVAX spot against short perps with a USDC buffer has held the dollar line, and its dozens of recorded deviations are shallow blips rather than crises. Backing is the best of the three pillars but still mid-table, because the Accountable feed itemizes reserves by location bucket (Ethereum, Base, Avalanche, a sliver at Copper) rather than by asset, leaving the strategy's actual positions, hedge notionals, and venue balances undisclosed. Economic control sits below it, and the card is currently capped by an opaque oracle topology: XSY does not publish how the strategy is priced, what freshness bounds apply, or what fails over. The exit pillar is the weakest: a 7-day unbonding period plus thin, fallback-class DEX coverage makes getting out an exercise in patience precisely when patience is most expensive. The peg mechanism evidently works whenever anyone tests it. The exit is where the grade and the risk actually live.

gusd-gate.title: Par Price, Opaque Ledger
gusd-gate.text: GUSD is Gate's account-linked yield certificate: users subscribe 1:1 with USDT, USDC, or USD1, receive daily GUSD rewards, and {{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} through Gate. Gate says tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}} and stablecoins back the product, but publishes no holdings schedule, named backing-asset custody structure, legal segregation, or independent reserve-to-token reconciliation. Its exchange proof-of-reserves now publishes customer and platform GUSD balances, which answers whether Gate holds customer GUSD but does not show what backs every token. The Ethereum control plane remains a single-EOA minter plus a separate no-delay EOA upgrader. GUSD also exists on GateLayer, although Pharos contract telemetry currently covers Ethereum only. The displayed market cap inherits DefiLlama's full Ethereum token-supply series and is materially above Gate subscription and CoinGecko circulating figures, so it should not be read as reconciled circulation. The peg has stayed close to par; the {{grade}} overall grade reflects the evidence and control plane behind that price.

usdcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen-FORGE USDCV Bank-Issued Dollar
usdcv-societe-generale-forge.text: SocGen-FORGE's USDCV is MiCA-regulated bank-issued plumbing: 100% USD cash in segregated accounts at BNY Mellon's Belgian entity and Societe Generale, an ACPR-regulated EMI licence, statutory segregation with a pro-rata holder claim, and a reserve page the issuer updates daily. That last point is the catch. The reserve could hardly be simpler, but the disclosure is self-reported rather than independently examined, and backing is the weakest of the three pillars on the report card. The exit pillar leads the card: direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through SG-FORGE, issuer-native deployments on Ethereum and Solana, and no third-party {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} in the path. The peg record is among the cleaner ones on the dashboard and stress monitoring has spent its history at the quiet end of the scale, which is what the cash-only design was built to deliver. The {{grade}} overall grade lands where the weakest pillar drags it, on an implementation still short of two years old with both chains resolving to SG-FORGE-held keys and no timelock on upgrades. The durable constraint is that the bank's own daily page is still the only check on the bank.

usdai-usd-ai.title: The Liquid Base Token
usdai-usd-ai.text: USDai is the non-yielding base token in USD.AI, and the important current detail is that Pharos metadata shows the base reserve as 100% PYUSD held by the USDai contract. USDC and USDT are deposit and exit currencies for users, not the assets currently sitting underneath the base token, which is exactly the kind of distinction stablecoin marketing tends to blur when nobody is watching. The GPU-backed loan book belongs to sUSDai, the separate staking sleeve, so base USDai holders are taking PYUSD dependency and platform-admin risk rather than AI-credit yield risk. The real-time proof-of-reserves API is a genuine transparency upgrade, especially for a young product spread across multiple chains. The catch is centralized mint and upgrade control through bridge/admin roles and a Safe-governed path, so the base token is liquid and observable, not permissionless.

susdai-usd-ai.title: The GPU-Credit Sleeve
susdai-usd-ai.text: sUSDai is where USD.AI moves from a PYUSD-backed base dollar into the actual AI-credit bet. The reserve stack currently combines a large PYUSD liquid sleeve with a smaller but meaningful GPU-backed infrastructure-loan sleeve, so the token behaves like a NAV-appreciating credit product rather than a clean payment stablecoin. USD.AI's on-chain reserve index separates the liquid assets from the loan book, and Pharos can reconstruct the PYUSD balance and loan principal from Arbitrum, but GPU identity, appraisal, insurance, and SPV enforceability remain issuer disclosures. Exits run through staking mechanics and a queued withdrawal flow with thirty-day processing windows rather than an always-on issuer redemption promise. Satellite tokens on Ethereum, Base, and Plasma sit behind a LayerZero adapter and a chain-local Safe that can burn holder balances. Exit and backing sit together as the weakest lines on the card, and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects a loan book whose collateral, appraisal, and enforceability rest on issuer disclosure.

usx-solstice.title: Synthetic Dollar, Aggregate Proof
usx-solstice.text: Solstice's USX is a Swiss-domiciled synthetic dollar on Solana, minted through KYC-gated institutional issuance against a reserve the issuer describes as audited cash, tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}, and {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} hedged positions, with Copper and Ceffu named as custodians. What Pharos can verify is narrower than that description. The Accountable attestation feed reports aggregate reserves slightly above supply, roughly 100.2% at the late-August 2026 read, with cryptographic proof material but no asset-level balances, so the current split among cash, Treasuries, and hedges is unpublished and the backing pillar is scored on limited evidence. Minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} validate collateral through Solstice's own oracle cross-checked against Pyth, and the issuer's program holds live mint and freeze authority. The exit pillar is the weakest of the three. Redemption is eligibility-gated, so retail holders depend on Solana secondary markets, and a December 2025 thin-liquidity episode took USX to a small fraction of par on a DEX before it recovered. The peg record has been quiet since, but the structure has not changed: an institutional redemption window in front, an aggregate-only solvency proof behind, and everyone else trading the gap.

hollar-hydrated.title: Aave Fork, Polkadot Address
hollar-hydrated.text: HOLLAR is Hydration's overcollateralized dollar, minted on an Aave V3 fork against DOT, ETH, BTC, and stablecoin collateral with a Stability Module that anchors the peg through direct stablecoin swaps. The core mechanics are a multi-collateral {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with per-block partial {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, and a Stability Module that behaves like a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}. That design earns structural credit, and economic control is the strongest pillar on the {{grade}} report card. The weaknesses are evidentiary and market-side. Hydration publishes no dated per-asset collateral weights, so the whole reserve is scored as an unsplit basket; the launch was less than two years ago; and the exit pillar is the weakest of the three because the route out has no stated same-notional dollar output. Governance reach is also wider than a fork label suggests: the admin role can repoint the token's delegated-allowance contract and move any holder's balance, and OpenGov's root track can replace runtime logic wholesale. The peg record carries a short tail of sharp episodes on thin DEX liquidity, with the worst excursions several percent below par. HOLLAR's viability ultimately tracks whether Polkadot DeFi expands or contracts, and the shallow order books around it are the durable constraint.

musd-metamask.title: Distribution as Moat
musd-metamask.text: MetaMask mUSD is what happens when crypto's default self-custody wallet decides to vertically integrate. It is issued by Stripe's Bridge on M0 protocol rails, backed by short-dated {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and cash in bankruptcy-remote custody and verified by real-time on-chain {{term:attestation}}validator attestations{{/term}}, although M0 no longer publishes the cash-versus-Treasury split. The {{grade}} overall grade is a split decision: a mid-card backing pillar and near-flawless peg behavior that has rarely left the calm end of the stress scale, dragged down by an exit pillar that is the weakest of the three. The secondary market hasn't caught up with primary-market confidence, and DEX liquidity stays spread wide and shallow. The reserve architecture reads like a compliance team's wishlist, but a modest tally of brief depeg blips, including a sharp positive spike, shows that arbitrage works in theory while depth stays thin in practice. The funnel switched on at the end of June: MetaMask's Money Account wires mUSD into yield routes and card spending directly inside the wallet, the first serious attempt to convert wallet distribution into float. The moat narrative is still more aspiration than balance sheet, but the infrastructure to realize it now exists.

cash-phantom.title: The Wallet's Dollar
cash-phantom.text: CASH is Phantom's wallet-native dollar on Solana, issued by Bridge Building Inc.: a distribution edge no DeFi protocol can replicate, putting a default stablecoin in front of the wallet's users. The distribution keeps compounding: World, the on-chain prediction market that replaced Phantom's Kalshi integration, settles winning positions automatically in CASH, the clearest sign Phantom wants CASH as the unit of account for everything the wallet touches. The report card is harsher than the peg: the peg record is the strongest line on the card, but Bridge discloses only an eligible-asset envelope: short-dated {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, Treasury repo, {{term:money-market-fund}}government money-market funds{{/term}}, and deposits in bankruptcy-remote {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at BlackRock and Fidelity, with no published category weights and no dated independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and its reserve APIs sit behind credentials. That leaves backing the weakest of the three pillars. Add exit depth that is modest for the supply, a HyperEVM representation carried by a LayerZero route whose validation set is unresolved, and issuer control as centralized as it gets, and the {{grade}} overall grade lands well below what the peg alone would suggest. A dollar can trade flawlessly and still be unverifiable, and until Bridge publishes weights and an attestation, that is where CASH stays.

sources.label: BeInCrypto: World prediction market goes live in Phantom, settling in CASH (July 2026)
Bridge Building Inc. stablecoin terms (reserve envelope)

tgbp-tokenised.title: Tokenised GBP Stablecoin
tgbp-tokenised.text: tGBP is BCP Technologies' pound stablecoin, issued under an FCA cryptoasset registration and redeemed through a direct off-chain GBP workflow. The issuer names the eligible reserve envelope, GBP bank deposits, money market funds, and short UK Treasury bills, but does not publish the current split, and Andersen's monthly agreed-upon-procedures report establishes aggregate sufficiency without an audit opinion or asset-class weights. Pharos therefore scores the reserve as one undisclosed basket, which is why the {{grade}} overall grade sits well below what the reserve envelope alone would suggest. Exit is the weakest of the three pillars; {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through the issuer's sterling rails. Economic control scores highest on the card: the LayerZero OFT mesh across eight chains is externally validated, even though a single owner key can mint and pause every EVM deployment and upgrade most of them. The peg has held near par with a tail of brief dips. The durable constraint is disclosure: until BCP publishes the allocation behind its attestation, the backing pillar stays capped.

sources.label: Andersen tGBP independent accountants report - June 2026

eurau-allunity.title: Licensed Reserves, Unnamed Banks
eurau-allunity.text: EURAU is AllUnity's MiCA-licensed euro stablecoin, issued by a BaFin-supervised EMI and backed one-for-one by euro reserves held in segregated accounts at EU credit institutions, with direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through AllUnity. The regulatory packaging is complete; the disclosure is not. The trust center still lists the reserve audit report as coming soon, and neither the white paper nor the site names the current banks, publishes allocations or a cash-versus-HQLA split, or defines what happens if a reserve bank fails, which is why backing grades in the middle of the card rather than at the top. The {{grade}} overall grade is dragged down by exit, the weakest pillar: redemption is eligibility-gated and secondary-market coverage is thin, with a single-source price feed and no depeg episode on record. Distribution now spans eight issuer-native deployments, including Solana, Tempo and BSC alongside the EVM majors, moved by AllUnity's own burn-and-mint mapping bridge; the announced Chainlink CCIP integration was not yet registered on any chain at the last check. On the EVM lanes the minter and admin are single externally owned accounts with no cap and no delay, so the reserve claim and the supply control both rest on AllUnity's backend. Until the audit report appears, backing is graded on the issuer's word.

usdh-native-markets.title: The Evacuated Beachhead
usdh-native-markets.text: Native Markets' USDH on HyperEVM is a Bridge-issued (Stripe) dollar with 40% short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} at JP Morgan plus tokenized treasuries. It was a bet on Hyperliquid traction that ended in a structured wind-down. USDH built to nine figures on HyperEVM with one of the more credible reserve compositions in the market: 40% short-term T-bills managed by BlackRock at JP Morgan, 20% tokenized {{term:treasury}}treasuries{{/term}} via BUIDL and USTB, and the rest in cash, repos, and {{term:money-market-fund}}treasury funds{{/term}}. All of it flowed through Bridge Building Inc., Stripe's stablecoin subsidiary. The 12 depeg events with swings as wide as 227 basis points tell the story of a young stablecoin on a single chain still building the arbitrage infrastructure to enforce its peg tightly. The bet did not get to play out: in late May Native Markets announced a structured wind-down as Coinbase took over as Hyperliquid's official USDC treasury deployer, the deployer liquidated its unlocked HYPE allocation, and by mid-June USDH's markets were settled and delisted. The validator vote that chose USDH over Paxos and Ethena was a bet on revenue redirection from Circle; the ecosystem re-voted with its treasury, and the beachhead is being evacuated in orderly fashion.

sbc-brale.title: Brale's Platform Stablecoin
sbc-brale.text: Brale's SBC is the house stablecoin of a stablecoin-as-a-service issuer, minted and redeemed through Brale's issuance APIs across eleven networks rather than sold as a consumer product. The peg record is the strongest line on the card: deviations have been brief blips rather than crises, and stress monitoring has stayed at the calm end of the scale. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three. An eleven-chain footprint spreads already-thin DEX liquidity thinner still, and Pharos has not been able to review a holder-facing primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route with published terms. Backing is the stronger story. MCCPA's examination as of July 31, 2026 records cash and cash equivalents plus a smaller sleeve of U.S. government-backed debt in segregated accounts, fully reconciled to issued SBC, although the examiner relied on company-provided records and the report names neither the banks nor the custodian. Brale is a FinCEN-registered money transmitter that describes direct 1:1 redemption, but the reserve custodian, provider allocations, and successor-custody mechanics remain undisclosed. Circulation is small, in the single-digit millions per the July attestation. The durable constraint is exit: eleven chains of distribution have not produced a deep secondary market or a disclosed primary one.

sources.label: MCCPA SBC Reserve Attestation Report - July 2026

euri-banking-circle.title: The Binance Distribution Play
euri-banking-circle.text: EURI is Banking Circle's MiCA-licensed euro stablecoin with fee-free 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}: a {{term:custody}}credit-institution{{/term}} wrapper engineered for Binance distribution. Eurite exists because Binance needed a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin and Banking Circle had the Luxembourg CSSF credit institution license to provide one. Holder funds sit in a segregated, bankruptcy-remote fiduciary estate of euro cash and low-risk cash equivalents, the regulatory structure arranged correctly on paper. Look for the receipts, though, and the evidence is thinner than it appears: the homepage's 'trusted attestation by a top tier auditor' links to no document, the only EY artefact on record is the bank's own financial-statements audit that mentions EURI once, and no dated reserve composition has ever been published, which is how a licensed bank's stablecoin ends up with backing near the bottom of its card. The peg itself behaves well: its score is near-perfect and only a couple of brief blips are on record. Exit grades just as poorly as backing, because Binance's endorsement has never translated into organic on-chain trading depth on either of its two chains, Ethereum and BSC. The {{grade}} overall grade tells the story: Eurite is less a standalone stablecoin than a compliance wrapper that lets Binance's European users stay in euros without leaving the exchange's orbit, and asks them to take the reserves on faith.

msusd-metronome.title: Latency Ate the Backing
msusd-metronome.text: Metronome's msUSD spent years as the durable niche synth, minted against USDC, DAI, ETH, WBTC, and Vesper yield tokens through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, with no direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and a peg defended by zero-slippage internal synth swaps. In late July 2026, the accounting failure surfaced: that same swap module had accumulated unbacked float because Chainlink price latency at swap execution was never covered by the fee design. Roughly 4.6 million msUSD had no debt positions behind them at disclosure. The market repriced the discovery: the token broke well below par, and Pharos now shows a {{grade}} overall grade with the peg score at the floor of the scale, on a coin once notable for quiet persistence. The remediation plan uses fee hikes, treasury-funded loops, and systematic buyback-and-burn to re-back the float faster than holders leave. The circularity was always the design: price support depends on insiders finding the balance-sheet trade worth taking. It turns out the balance sheet itself had been miscounted.

aznd-mu-digital.title: Asia Credit in a Token
aznd-mu-digital.text: AZND is Mu Digital's KYC-gated dollar token backed by a Singapore-regulated Asia credit fund, with yield routed through the loAZND vault and a muBOND junior tranche providing {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and absorbing first losses. It is structured credit dressed as a stablecoin. The last Accountable snapshot Pharos ingested showed the Asset Pool parked in short-term cash and liquid bonds, a notably more conservative posture than the published mandate that permits up to 20% illiquid private credit. The {{grade}} overall grade is earned where it matters most: the exit pillar is the weakest of the three, because thin Monad DEX liquidity plus weekly KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} settling on a fund calendar leave holders no fast path back to dollars, and backing is held down because no current allocation of the Asset Pool is published. The peg record is the strongest line on the card, but that is the faint praise of a peg too illiquid to be seriously tested. AZND targets a real gap in institutional Asian credit exposure on-chain. The question remains whether DeFi-native capital will accept fund-style lockups for single-digit yields.

nect-beraborrow.title: Below Redemption Scale on Berachain
nect-beraborrow.text: BeraBorrow's NECT runs Liquity-v2 {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics on Berachain's exotic collateral set: WBERA, wrapped BTC variants, ETH derivatives, and Kodiak LP tokens, mostly classified high-risk on an unproven chain. The {{grade}} overall grade is earned: NECT has logged hundreds of brief sub-peg blips with the worst episode several points below par, and while the acute episodes have cooled since the last one in March, the token has spent more time a point or two shy of a full dollar than parked at it. With circulating supply below the methodology's one-million-dollar floor and thin DEX liquidity, the coin sits below the threshold where the CDP {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism can function as designed only when arbitrageurs show up; the economics do not justify it at this scale. Backing is the strongest pillar on the card and exit the weakest.
