The collateral-redemption backstop and {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffer remain structurally sound on paper, but sound mechanisms need liquid markets to express themselves.

usp-pikudao.title: Turkish Carry Trade, Tokenized
usp-pikudao.text: PikuDAO's USP is a KYC-gated, NAV-appreciating token whose backing is deployed into a Turkish lira FX arbitrage strategy run by Balsa Technologies ({{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} TRY/USD trades capturing Turkey's inflation-driven {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} carry), allocations across DeFi protocols such as Giza, Almanak, USD.AI, Ethena, Aave, and Cap, and a USDC/USDT buffer. Piku publishes no dated allocation table, so Pharos carries the whole reserve as one unresolved strategy envelope; the only published weights, roughly half in the Turkish strategy and most of the rest across DeFi, come from third-party research rather than an issuer disclosure. KYC/KYB is required to mint or redeem, with a 24-hour FIFO settlement queue and a 0.2% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee. The very-high risk classification on the Turkish FX leg and the undisclosed weights show up in the exotic collateral quality rating, and backing and economic control are the two weakest pillars on the card, the latter dragged by a manual issuer price feed and an uncapped minter. It is a genuinely novel yield source for DeFi: Turkish carry trade returns are uncorrelated with crypto markets. It also concentrates geopolitical and counterparty risk in a single emerging market with a long record of currency depreciation. The NAV has climbed well above par, which proves the strategy works when it works; what happens when it doesn't is the question the disclosure gap leaves open.

pmusd-precious-metals.title: Gold-Backed pmUSD With Sky PSM
pmusd-precious-metals.text: Gold-backed supply paired with a sUSDS-funded {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} means pmUSD's peg defense depends on Sky Protocol staying healthy, which is a meaningful external dependency. The structure runs on two awkward logics: supply is backed by gold via RAAC's RWf(x) fork and ION.au tokenized claims, while dollar recovery relies on a PSM holding Sky's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} savings wrapper. Arbitrageurs can swap discounted pmUSD for sUSDS at a $1 internal valuation, but the flow is one-directional and halts if sUSDS reserves fall below the module's threshold. That ties pmUSD's dollar recovery to Sky stability, which is a strange dependency for a coin whose collateral narrative begins with precious metals. That failure mode is no longer hypothetical: pmUSD has traded far below the dollar through 2026, logging a long run of depeg episodes, and for as long as that depeg persists it pins the {{grade}} overall grade at the bottom of the scale, while the one-directional PSM does what it can from its side of the door. Real-time Chainlink Proof of Reserves and Instruxi {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} document I-ON's gold reserve, though not a pmUSD-specific reconciliation, and gold is not necessarily the right asset to stabilize with someone else's savings-dollar plumbing.

jupusd-jupiter.title: Three Layers to Treasuries
jupusd-jupiter.text: JupUSD is Jupiter's bid to own Solana's dollar layer, backed overwhelmingly by Ethena's USDtb, itself a wrapper around BlackRock's BUIDL, with a USDC buffer covering the rest. The dependency chain runs JupUSD to USDtb to BUIDL to actual government bonds: pristine collateral buried under three layers of operational and counterparty risk, custodied through Porto and Anchorage. It holds a {{grade}} overall grade, lifted by a real finding: reserves sit in named Solana token accounts any third party can read, so coverage is recomputable from chain state rather than taken on the issuer's word. The uplift arrives with a ceiling attached, though: reconciliation is credited on cadence alone, with no attestor, no attestation section, and no regulatory disclosure anywhere on the transparency surface, so the centralized-mint constraint survives and is now the binding cap on the card. A zero-delay 4-of-9 Squads multisig can replace the mint logic outright, and the monthly attestations that show up in press coverage belong to USDtb, the collateral issuer, not to JupUSD. Jupiter is betting BlackRock's brand travels well through intermediaries; until an attestor signs for JupUSD itself, the cap stays where it is.

u-united-stables.title: Variable Reserve Wrapper
u-united-stables.text: United Stables' U is a BVI-issued dollar whose reserve policy is deliberately flexible: cash, U.S. Treasury bills, and approved fiat-referenced stablecoins may all sit in the basket, and the governing terms permit the mix and its counterparties to change without notice. That flexibility is operationally convenient and analytically useless, because the live feed reports one aggregate balance. There is no composition to score, only an envelope, which is why backing is the weakest of the three pillars. Pharos does credit the proof-of-reserves path, which resolves to a third-party Chainlink feed rather than an issuer dashboard and is materially better than self-reporting. It does little for the {{grade}} overall grade, because no comparable same-notional exit route is supported, and because the same terms that describe segregated custody on the website state that United Stables need not segregate reserves and that holders hold no preferential, secured, or proprietary claim in insolvency. The marketing page and the contract you actually agree to are not describing the same product. U is trying to be a programmable reserve wrapper; the risk is that the wrapper's discretion is the product.

sources.label: United Stables proof of reserves (Chainlink PoR feed)

reusd-re-protocol.title: Insurance Capital Goes On-Chain
reusd-re-protocol.text: Re Protocol's reUSD is the senior NAV-appreciating tranche of a reinsurance-capital structure, issued from the Cayman Islands to eligible non-U.S. persons. The reserve split is now dominated by the off-chain leg: the live Re Metrics feed for August 2026 puts roughly four fifths of the book in Regulation 114 trust collateral supporting reinsurance contracts, measured only in aggregate, with the on-chain remainder concentrated in sUSDe {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} exposure plus small USDC, USDT, and LP positions. That makes the backing pillar the weakest of the three and sets the {{grade}} overall grade: the trust assets, partner reinsurers, and banking counterparties are not enumerated, and Ethena infrastructure still carries most of the liquid side. The token price is recalculated daily from a blend of the off-chain SOFR-based return and the trailing sUSDe basis rate, so the yield is governance-set rather than passed through. Ten chains of deployment through Chainlink CCIP give reUSD real reach, and the canonical Ethereum token has no holder-freeze path, but a live Safe can pause or policy-block holders on Tempo. Instant {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is liquidity-limited and falls back to a quarterly queue, and The Network Firm's daily transparency dashboard is backed by only one formal report from late 2025. It remains one of the more candid yield products on the market, which is not the same as being simple.

rwausdi-multipli.title: Multipli's KYB-Gated Credit Dollar
rwausdi-multipli.text: rwaUSDi is Multipli's KYB-gated institutional credit class: a UAE-domiciled dollar token whose reserve is described as private credit, structured finance, project finance, asset-backed loans, and market-neutral fund strategies run with counterparties such as Nomura, Fasanara, and Edge Capital, priced periodically at NAV with scheduled rather than instant {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The pitch is that lending protocols cannot individually underwrite hundreds of {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} positions, so rwaUSDi does the aggregation and due diligence and issues one composable token, now native on seven chains including Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Monad. The peg record has been quiet, and stress monitoring has stayed at the calm end of its history. The problem is what the {{grade}} overall grade cannot see: the AFI proof-of-reserves feed verifies only aggregate reserve and liability totals, reporting a collateral ratio well above one, but exposes no itemized holdings, borrowers, funds, weights, or holder seniority, and the issuer publishes no tranche priority or loss waterfall. Pharos therefore scores the backing pillar as the weakest of the three under a limited-evidence ceiling. Economic control is the strongest line on the card even though a shared EOA holds uncapped mint rights and chain-local Safes can force-transfer or burn any holder's balance without a timelock. A trust layer between holder and underlying assets works until someone asks to inspect the trust.

usdm-mega.title: Funding the Sequencer
usdm-mega.text: MegaETH's USDm flips the L2 business model: instead of extracting sequencer fees from users, it uses {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} yield from Ethena's USDtb (itself holding BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}) alongside USDC, in proportions MegaETH does not disclose, to subsidize network operations. The chain gets cheaper as more people hold its native stablecoin. The peg has held, with only brief deviations on record, but the absence of any tracked DEX liquidity means exit routes are limited to the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism. The dependency on Ethena's infrastructure for both reserve management and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} adds counterparty risk that the underlying Treasuries don't carry, and it shows in the grading. The {{grade}} overall grade is weighed down by weak backing and exit pillars, backing the weaker of the two because no current reserve split or independent NAV administrator is published, and the dependency profile inherits USDtb's concentrated mint authority wholesale. The stablecoin's value proposition is inseparable from MegaETH's own traction as an L2. Stablecoin adoption subsidizes network costs, which can drive adoption. The same flywheel can also turn in the other direction.

usdm-monetrix.title: Monetrix's Hyperliquid Delta-Neutral Dollar
usdm-monetrix.text: Monetrix USDM is the base dollar token in a small HyperEVM yield stack: users mint it 1:1 by depositing USDC into the Monetrix vault, and sUSDM is the separate staking wrapper where strategy yield accrues. The USDC does not sit idle. Monetrix deploys the backing into a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} portfolio on Hyperliquid, long spot BTC, ETH, and HYPE against matching short {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} positions, and returns USDC on {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} after a multi-day governance-set cooldown. At the latest check, the issuer's own collateral API reported coverage just above par but marked the breakdown unreconciled, mixing spot, margin, hedge, and buffer accounting with no non-double-counted reserve equation, so Pharos carries the whole reserve as a single unresolved strategy envelope. The {{grade}} overall grade is pinned at the failing line by a binding oracle cap: the price feed and failover behind the hedge book are unpublished. Beneath it, the exit pillar is the weakest of the three, with one chain, a cooldown on redemptions, and no comparable exit route, while a global pause under the access controller can halt every transfer. The peg has held over a short, single-source tracking window. USDM is useful coverage for HyperEVM dollar liquidity; what it is backed by on any given day is a question only Monetrix can answer.

usat-tether.title: Tether Goes Domestic
usat-tether.text: Tether's USA-T is a GENIUS-era U.S. dollar issued 1:1 by Anchorage Digital Bank under an OCC federal charter, backed by cash and {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-collateralized overnight reverse repos with Cantor Fitzgerald {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and monthly Deloitte {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} reports. It is the cleanest regulatory setup Tether has ever assembled. The report card has caught up with the paperwork: the {{grade}} overall grade rests on backing and economic control pillars that lead the card and a peg that has held at par since launch. The attestation leaves the single broker-dealer on the other side of the repo book unnamed, along with the deposit banks. The softest pillar is exit, on a deployment that is still Ethereum-only. The strategic logic is transparent: USA-T is Tether's answer to USDC on US soil, separating the domestic compliance story from USDT's offshore empire, with a 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise through Anchorage. Whether American institutions will trust a Tether-branded dollar after a decade of skepticism remains the open question. The durable constraint is distribution: one chain, one issuer, and a track record still under two years.

yzusd-yuzu.title: KYC-Gated Senior Tranche on Plasma
yzusd-yuzu.text: yzUSD is Yuzu's KYC-gated base dollar on Plasma, minted and redeemed 1:1 against USDT0 by accredited, qualified, or institutional investors, with yield routed to the separate syzUSD wrapper. The token is the senior claim on a pooled strategy book: the yzPP junior tranche absorbs first losses and redemption is gated on a system-wide collateral ratio above 110%. The Accountable dashboard publishes the exposure split, and what it shows is a leveraged stablecoin carry book. Ethena USDe loops are the largest line at close to a third, followed by Sky USDS staking and a spread of Aave, Maple, Agora, Superstate, and PayPal USD loop positions, with a small USDT0 liquidity buffer; nearly every slice is classed high risk. Pharos does not rate yzUSD overall: the reserve composition is not carried into the fixed scoring input and the evidence ceiling is too low to support a letter. Within the pillars, exit is the weakest line and economic control the strongest; issuance runs through forty minter accounts, with upgrades and limit changes behind timelocked Safes. The peg line on the card is strong, but with minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} restricted to eligible investors and no meaningful secondary market, that record reflects who is allowed to sell as much as how the book performs.

nusd-neutrl.title: Paused for a Reserve Review
nusd-neutrl.text: Neutrl's NUSD is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar whose reserves, per the Accountable dashboard's last verifiable snapshot of 13 August 2026, were a little over half liquid stablecoins, with the rest in OTC aggregate positions, Jupiter JLP, protocol-owned liquidity, and an undisclosed other bucket. On that same day Neutrl paused minting, redemptions, and other protocol functions for a reserve-liquidity review; as of 29 August the proposed early-redemption path was still waiting on a new contract, an audit, and legal and financial sign-off. The pause followed a months-long supply contraction in which holders had queued for the exit, with the peg holding cleanly throughout and only a handful of shallow blips on record. The {{grade}} overall grade now reflects an exit pillar that is the weakest of the three, since the KYC-gated redemption queue that was the product's one proven exit is closed until the new process ships, while backing is capped by limited evidence on the OTC and JLP legs. The durable constraint is that until redemptions reopen, the peg rests on secondary-market depth rather than on an issuer exit.

usdgo-osl.title: A Billion in Three Months
usdgo-osl.text: OSL's USDGO has been compounding supply at a pace that makes most stablecoin launches look lethargic, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank under an OCC charter with monthly Deloitte examinations. On-chain liquidity is the bottleneck. The float crossed the ten-figure line in July 2026: OSL says the run from $100 million to $1 billion took three months and placed USDGO among the top six regulated stablecoins by circulating supply. The July 31 Deloitte examination confirmed reserves slightly above a ten-figure liability. The peg record is spotless so far over a short tracking window. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: a single Solana deployment and eligibility-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through the issuer make this an issuer-API exit story rather than an on-chain arbitrage play. The reserve is fund shares rather than bills held outright. At the July examination nearly all of it sat in JPMorgan's and Goldman Sachs' government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}} and BlackRock's tokenized BUIDL fund, with about one percent in bank cash, all in segregated fiduciary trust accounts under Anchorage {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. The BUIDL slice is a tracked dependency in its own right, and the shared Solana Token-2022 program, upgradeable by a multisig with no delay, is a common-mode control Pharos flags across the reserve paths. A billion-dollar float built in months says OSL's institutional pipeline is a durable bid. The remaining issue is whether the on-chain plumbing ever catches up to it.

sources.label: OSL Group: USDGO circulating supply surpasses US$1 billion (July 20, 2026)

fidd-fidelity.title: Fidelity's Chartered Dollar
fidd-fidelity.text: FIDD is Fidelity Digital Assets' OCC-chartered dollar stablecoin backed by cash and short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} at BNY Mellon: a regulatory beachhead from a major asset manager. When Fidelity issues a stablecoin, the signal overwhelms the product, and the product is deliberately boring: a T-bill-heavy reserve with a sizeable cash sleeve at a single bank, a Big Four {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} examined monthly by PwC, and institutional-grade {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped only by time: backing and exit both lead the card, economic control trails by a narrow margin, and under two years of implementation history is the binding limit regardless of reserve quality. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} runs 1:1 through Fidelity Digital Assets platforms, an institutional rail that the card scores as permissionless. The single Ethereum deployment sits behind a UUPS proxy administered by externally owned accounts with no timelock. FIDD's peg record is short and clean, while Fidelity's decision to distribute the token more widely remains unresolved.

sources.label: PwC FIDD Reserve Attestation Report - May 2026

aid-gaib.title: GPU Yield, Dollarized
aid-gaib.text: AID is GAIB's centralized dollar stablecoin, minted 1:1 against USDC and USDT and backed by T-bills and approved stables. Its companion sAID accrues GPU/AI infrastructure financing yield. GAIB's AID is a conventional dollar stablecoin backed by {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and stablecoin reserves, with 1:1 mint and burn. Its entire reason for existing is its companion token sAID, which accrues yield from GPU and AI infrastructure financing deals. The structure neatly separates stable value (AID) from exotic yield (sAID), letting users choose their risk exposure. What the issuer has not published is a reserve split or a retrievable attestation: the transparency page names the categories but not the weights, custodians, or a reconciliation of assets to liabilities, so Pharos carries the whole reserve as one undisclosed envelope and the backing and economic-control pillars are the weakest lines on the {{grade}} card. Whether GPU financing agreements produce reliable enough cash flows to back a yield product is genuinely untested, and until a reserve report is published the stable half of the pair rests on the issuer's description rather than on evidence.

apxusd-apyx.title: Dividends as Collateral
apxusd-apyx.text: apxUSD is Apyx's dollar stablecoin backed by preferred shares of Digital Asset Treasury companies plus a cash and {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} buffer: an experimental collateral type that bets equity dividends from crypto-holding firms can stay near par. Apyx introduced what might be the most creative collateral backing in stablecoins: preferred shares from Digital Asset Treasury companies, publicly traded equity from firms like Strategy that hold large crypto positions. The theory is that variable-rate preferred shares trade near par regardless of crypto price volatility, providing stable collateral for a dollar token. Launched on Ethereum in February 2026 with DeFi Development Corp as an early investor, apxUSD scaled to nine figures fast. Then the theory met June 2026. The answer arrived quickly: as Bitcoin fell, Strategy's STRC preferred traded below par and apxUSD followed it down, first to the $0.90s in early June, then through $0.80 by late month. The token still trades below the dollar, the {{grade}} overall grade is pinned by the active depeg, and backing is the weakest of the three pillars. The issuer calls preferred-share pass-through a feature rather than a bug, which is honest as far as it goes, but a dollar that trades at a structural discount whenever its collateral does is a tracking certificate wearing a stablecoin's clothing. Pharos treats the reserve profile as closer to {{term:rwa}}real-world-asset{{/term}} credit than to a cash-only stablecoin.

jpyc-jpyc.title: The Yen's Licensed Pioneer
jpyc-jpyc.text: Japan's first FSA-approved yen stablecoin occupies an enviable regulatory position: a Type II Funds Transfer license under the Payment Services Act, 100% backing in JPY deposits and Japanese government bonds, and institutional-regulated custody, with circulation still modest. Deployed across several public chains with the JPYC EX platform handling mint and redemption via bank transfer after KYC, the infrastructure is sound but adoption has not followed the license, which shows that regulatory compliance alone does not drive demand. The competitive threat has also changed shape: while everyone watched the Progmat megabank consortium, SBI got there first. JPYSC launched in June 2026 as Japan's first trust-bank yen stablecoin, with trust-law redemption rights, despite being locked inside SBI's own exchange. Pharos's report card tells the fuller story. Exit and economic control are JPYC's strongest pillars, supported by bank-rail redemption and tokens that actually trade on open chains. Backing is the weakest, a gap between the license's promise and the reserve evidence Pharos can verify: the issuer states the deposit-and-JGB envelope but publishes no dated split and no independent attestation. The structural moat is reserves split between bank deposits and JGB {{term:treasury}}treasury bonds{{/term}}, statutory safeguarding of customer funds under the Payment Services Act, institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and bank-rail {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via JPYC EX. First-mover status is still worth something, because unlike its trust-bank rival, JPYC's yen can actually leave the building.

sources.label: Ledger Insights: SBI launches first trust bank yen stablecoin JPYSC

xaut-tether.title: Tether Mints Bullion
xaut-tether.text: XAUT is Tether Gold's claim on LBMA Good Delivery bars vaulted in Switzerland, each token representing one fine troy ounce. The June 2026 BDO Italia reasonable-assurance report records 707,747 ounces against 707,747 XAUT outstanding, reconciled to the blockchain ledgers, and states that the gold is owned by the holders rather than by the issuer, with undivided rights in specified bars. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} is physical only: whole bars, a 430 XAUT minimum, delivery in Switzerland, through TG Commodities under El Salvador's CNAD licence. Pharos rates the card {{grade}} overall, with backing the weakest of the three pillars because of disclosure: the report does not name the custodian, publish the custody agreement, prohibit rehypothecation, or test insolvency treatment. Exit routes share a failure domain, since the XAUt0 representations on fourteen other chains all depend on a LayerZero lockbox on Ethereum. The token owner can block addresses and destroy blocked funds, and under MiCA the asset is recorded as a non-compliant asset-referenced token. The peg record shows a long tail of brief episodes, as expected for a gold token priced against spot. The durable constraint is that holders own the bars on paper while the custodian holding them stays unnamed.

sources.label: BDO Tether Gold Reserves Report - June 30, 2026
Tether Gold FAQ (allocated-bar ownership and physical redemption terms)

paxg-paxos.title: Bar Serials and Bankruptcy Remoteness
paxg-paxos.text: PAXG is Paxos's gold token with the paperwork turned all the way up: one fine troy ounce of allocated LBMA Good Delivery gold per token, Brink's and ICBC Standard Bank vaulting in London, KPMG monthly examinations that reconcile redeemable tokens to ounces, and Paxos trust supervision. In a tokenized gold market where the metal is the easy part, PAXG competes on custody traceability and regulatory comfort rather than chain sprawl, and the {{grade}} overall grade rests on backing, exit, and economic control scoring close together rather than on one standout pillar. The issuer-direct mint path and centralized controls are still there: Paxos controller keys mint under rate limits, an immediate controller-manager key can raise them, and the holder-freeze surface is live. The June 2026 Solana expansion ends the Ethereum-only era, but a two-chain footprint after seven years still tells you who the product is for: allocators who care more about bar serials and bankruptcy remoteness than the latest bridge. The remaining gaps are the ones Paxos does not publish: the ounce split between the two vault providers and the LayerZero route details for the Ethereum-to-Solana path.

sources.label: Paxos PAX Gold: allocation lookup covers Ethereum and Solana wallets
WEEX News: PAXG launched on Solana mainnet (June 2026)

kau-kinesis.title: Gold Claim Behind a Two-Step Redemption
kau-kinesis.text: KAU on this page is KMS Labs' Ethereum ERC-20, backed 1:1 by Kinesis-native KAU held in a segregated reserve wallet, which in turn is a claim on one gram of LBMA-approved allocated gold in ABX vaults. The layering matters: the ERC-20 balance does not accrue the Kinesis transaction-fee yield that native KAU holders receive, and physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is two-step, first back to native KAU through KMS Labs after compliance onboarding, then to bullion through Kinesis Cayman subject to platform terms. Bureau Veritas {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} covers the vaulted metal every six months, but KMS Labs publishes no reconciliation of ERC-20 supply against the native-KAU reserve wallet and names no independent digital-asset custodian, so the backing pillar sits well below what allocated gold would suggest. The exit pillar is the weakest on the card because no score-eligible runtime redemption route is compiled. The representation's minter is uncapped and the native Kinesis issuance path is unresolved, which weighs on economic control as well. Pharos records a long tail of deviations against the gold reference, consistent with a thinly traded representation of an off-chain claim. ABX vault {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backs the metal; the ERC-20 holder's claim runs through KMS Labs first.

xaum-matrixdock.title: Asia's Institutional Bullion
xaum-matrixdock.text: Matrixdock's XAUm is backed by LBMA-certified 99.99% gold bars at Brink's and Malca-Amit in Singapore and Hong Kong, inspected by Bureau Veritas under an assets-only physical {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, with institutional-regulated custody and a minimum redemption of 32.148 XAUm (1 kg) restricted to KYC'd accredited investors. The design is a deliberate Asia-domicile bet against London- and Swiss-vaulted competitors, targeting institutions that prefer regional custody for their gold exposure. The Ethereum-and-BNB-Chain token of its launch year has become a distribution play: a February 2026 Solana deployment and a Stellar launch pushed the footprint to eight networks Pharos tracks, alongside Polygon, Tron, Sui, and Plume. The report card catches the asymmetry: respectable backing and economic control against an exit pillar that reflects eight chains of distribution funneling into a single kilo-bar {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} desk with no runtime route Pharos can score. Whether institutions actually prefer Asia-domiciled custody over the London and Swiss vaults that XAUT and PAXG offer remains the strategic bet.

sources.label: Matrixdock expands XAUm to Solana (PR Newswire, Feb 2026)
Matrixdock Gold Bureau Veritas Audit Jul 2026 (covers XAUm gold and XAGm silver)

cgo-comtech.title: DMCC-Stamped Bullion
cgo-comtech.text: CGO is ComTech Gold's tokenized gold from the UAE, one token per gram of 24-karat 999.9 fineness bullion held in segregated Transguard vaults, with bars registered on DMCC Tradeflow and the issuer licensed under DAFZA. Holders can redeem for physical gold through the ComTech app, but Pharos has reviewed that {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path only on paper: no score-eligible runtime route is compiled, so the exit pillar grades the documentation rather than an observed exit. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three. The sole XDC deployment is minted through a controller whose owner, executor, and minter roles all resolve to one 2-of-4 Safe with no cumulative cap, and reserve evidence consists of self-signed gold-stock letters with issuer DMCC screenshots rather than a third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}; the newest routine custodian audit entry dates from March 2025. The peg record is the strongest line on the card, tracking gold over several years with a long tail of brief deviations. Dubai's clarity on {{term:rwa}}tokenized commodities{{/term}} is a real credential, but the governing {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} agreement and any rehypothecation prohibition remain unpublished, and until an independent reserve report appears the license carries more weight than the evidence.

dgld-gold-token-sa.title: PAMP-Refined Gold Token
dgld-gold-token-sa.text: DGLD is Gold Token SA's tokenized gold, one token per troy ounce of allocated LBMA Good Delivery PAMP bars in Swiss vaults, with the issuer's live registry mapping each chain's supply to named bar serials. Token holders hold Swiss-law co-ownership of the metal under the June 2026 terms, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} sits with MKS PAMP SA, and physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is available from one gram with KYC. That is the strong side. The weak side is that the registry is issuer-maintained and no third-party audit is published, so the backing pillar grades a self-reported record. The exit pillar is the weakest of the three: the physical route is reviewed but no score-eligible runtime route exists, and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects that gap plus the issuer EOAs that hold uncapped mint and proxy-admin roles on Ethereum and Base. The record also carries a scar. In February 2026 the former Ethereum-to-Base bridge allowed phantom deposits and unbacked minting on Base; the path was frozen, balances were migrated one-for-one, and the bridge was closed in June, leaving native issuance on Ethereum, Base, and Solana. The peg score is held back by thin single-source quotes that have produced a long tail of deviations, one of them extreme. Allocated gold qualifies DGLD as a {{term:rwa}}real-world asset{{/term}}; the durable constraint is that its verification chain ends at the issuer.

kag-kinesis.title: Silver Claim Rated on Its Paperwork
kag-kinesis.text: KAG is a claim on one troy ounce of allocated silver, and for most of its life on Pharos it carried the word audited without anyone opening the artefact to see what that word was doing. Someone opened it. Bureau Veritas's April 2026 work is a commodity vault inspection performed under agreed procedures with no opinion expressed, scoped to assets only. It counts metal against vault records and stops there. The sole place tokens are compared to silver is the issuer's own cover letter, signed by a party who heads both Kinesis and the vault operator, which is a reconciliation only in the issuer's own telling. The score moved barely at all, and that restraint is the point: the silver is very likely in the vault and the inspection is very likely competent, but neither fact is the same as an independent party confirming that outstanding KAG is covered by it. Anyone here for the yield should know that the ERC-20 tracked on this page does not accrue Kinesis transaction-fee sharing, which belongs to native balances. Tokenized silver is still a market of approximately one, and its lone resident is now rated on what its paperwork proves rather than what the paperwork is called.

eurq-quantoz.title: The Enterprise Euro
eurq-quantoz.text: EURQ is Quantoz Payments' MiCA-licensed euro stablecoin from a Dutch EMI supervised by DNB, redeemable 1:1 through the issuer and aimed at corporate payments rather than DeFi. The transparency page's latest snapshot reports roughly two thirds of reserves in Dutch, German and US government bonds and one third in cash at Tier 1 European banks, slightly above 100% of tokens outstanding; the {{term:attestation}}disclosure{{/term}} is self-reported and static, names neither the banks nor the bond identifiers, and says nothing about the active custodian set or replacement arrangements. That is why backing is the weakest pillar on the card and the {{grade}} overall grade sits below what the licence suggests. The tape adds a warning the paperwork does not: with a single-source price feed and thin trading across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL and Algorand, EURQ has logged a handful of depeg episodes, including a double-digit discount in mid-2026. Whether the enterprise market wants an on-chain euro remains open; what Pharos can see is a regulated claim with a reserve statement that stops short of proof and a secondary market too thin to hold par under pressure.

deuro-deuro.title: The Oracle-Free Euro
deuro-deuro.text: DEURO is a decentralized euro stablecoin minted from overcollateralized crypto positions using Frankencoin-style auctions instead of price oracles. Born from the same codebase as Frankencoin (ZCHF), dEURO takes the position that price feeds are a point of failure: each {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} position carries an owner-set {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} price that anyone can challenge in an auction, trading capital efficiency for resilience against oracle manipulation. The collateral book is the catch. At Pharos's last read roughly 85% of backing was WFPS, the wrapped Frankencoin pool share, with WBTC most of the rest and cbBTC, kBTC, and WETH as dust, so dEURO's {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} rests on reflexive exposure to Frankencoin protocol equity that would take more than a week to unwind. The core Ethereum contract is immutable with no owner and new minting modules can be vetoed by nDEPS holders, but the Polygon representation sits behind a 5-of-9 Safe that can upgrade it without a timelock. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: the protocol's stablecoin bridges to EURC, EURS, and other euro tokens exist, but Pharos has no comparable same-notional route to score and no usable market price for the token. Backing and economic control grade solidly; the durable constraint is a euro whose collateral is mostly another protocol's equity.

cetes-etherfuse.title: Three Counterparties, One Yield
cetes-etherfuse.text: CETES is Etherfuse's tokenized wrapper around Mexico's {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}, zero-coupon sovereign debt auctioned weekly, NAV-accreting in MXN, held through INDEVAL {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with monthly BHR México reasonable-assurance {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} that fully reconcile assets against liabilities. The structure stacks three dependencies: the peso, the BBB- sovereign, and the issuer. FX risk for dollar-denominated holders never shows up in the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} headline. Deployed across five chains from Solana to Stellar behind KYC-gated minting, it offers genuine on-chain access to Mexican sovereign debt for anyone willing to do the paperwork. But since mid-July 2026 Pharos has held the token in quarantine: none of the permitted market-data sources reports a positive circulating supply or market cap, so live scoring is withheld until usable numbers reappear. A sovereign-debt {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} wrapper with verified reserves and no verifiable circulation is an odd inversion: the backing is currently easier to prove than the float.

zarp-zarp.title: The Rand's Digital Outpost
zarp-zarp.text: ZARP is backed effectively one-for-one by rand cash. The overwhelming bulk sits in an Old Mutual Wealth trust account, with a sliver at Standard Bank. ZARP remains the only meaningfully documented on-chain rand. Kempen's agreed-upon-procedures reports, running from May 2024 through August 2026, qualify as recurring third-party reconciliation, which is why backing and economic control both sit well above the {{grade}} overall grade. Read those reports for what they are, though. They are ISRS 4400 agreed-upon procedures that expressly state they are not an assurance engagement and express no opinion, and the August one leaves a difference of roughly R311,000 between the account balances Kempen verified and the single total management asserts alongside them, unreconciled anywhere in the document. The real drag sits on the exit side: no viable exit path is established and the FSCA CASP licence is still pending, which puts the exit pillar at the bottom of the scale and drags the overall grade down with it. ZARP's problem was never credibility. The constraint is the exit: the reserve is documented, but no route for converting ZARP back into rand at scale has been established.

sources.label: Kempen ZARP agreed-upon procedures report - August 12, 2026

syrupusdc-maple.title: Institutional Lending, Vaulted
syrupusdc-maple.text: Maple's syrupUSDC turns USDC into an ERC-4626 receipt for institutional lending, a tidy way to make private credit look like a composable stablecoin. Maple's own disclosures state the token is not backed by USDC one-to-one and carries no redemption guarantee. Deposits fund overcollateralized fixed-rate loans plus basis and liquidity strategies, value accrues through NAV, and withdrawals are served by a FIFO queue that can run to thirty days, which is why exit is comfortably the weakest pillar here. The Network Firm proof-of-reserves programme was announced in May, but the collateralization report it promised is still marked coming soon, so the transparency page currently serves live AUM where independent verification was implied. No ceiling binds the card, so the {{grade}} overall grade is the plain weighted verdict of its own pillars, with the withdrawal queue holding it below the backing score. A private-credit book denominated in someone else's dollar carries two credit stories: the USDC dependency is scored from independent data, while borrower performance inside the pool rests on Maple's own disclosure.

sources.label: Maple syrupUSDC Product Disclosures and Disclaimers

syrupusdt-maple.title: Maple's USDT Lending Vault
syrupusdt-maple.text: Maple's USDT counterpart to syrupUSDC runs on identical machinery. It is an ERC-4626 vault feeding {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} fixed-rate loans to institutional borrowers, with exits served by a FIFO withdrawal queue rather than the pretense that every lender can leave at once. The old Ethereum-only caveat has expired: the vault now spans Ethereum, Plasma, BSC, Mantle, and Ink, yet it still runs at well under half of syrupUSDC's size, and the non-Ethereum units are Chainlink CCIP lock-mint claims on shares escrowed in one Ethereum lockbox. What actually separates the twins is the dollar underneath. Routing the same private-credit book through Tether instead of Circle, with no published strategy split, leaves the backing pillar well below its sibling's and pulls the overall card down with it. The withdrawal queue keeps exit the weakest pillar for both, and here no comparable redemption route is supported and the exit evidence is limited. On verification the vaults share one asterisk: Maple announced a Network Firm proof-of-reserves programme in May, but the transparency page still serves live AUM figures where the promised independent collateralization report should be. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects Tether backing, a thin exit, and an unpublished loan-strategy split.

yousd-yield-optimizer.title: Fifty Strategies, One Token
yousd-yield-optimizer.text:
A USDC-only yield aggregator on Base whose NAV moves with strategy outcomes rather than tracking a fixed dollar claim.

YO Protocol's yoUSD automates what DeFi power users do manually: rebalancing USDC across 50+ yield sources on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Unichain, ranked by risk scores with per-pool and per-protocol concentration caps. That diversification still leaves holders exposed to venue and allocator risk, which is why backing is the weakest of the three pillars on the {{grade}} card while exit and economic control both grade near the top. The March 22 2026 Resolv exploit produced a reported ~2.95% yoUSD drawdown through Resolv-linked exposure, a useful reminder that NAV-appreciating tokens can also absorb strategy losses. Backed by Paradigm, Haun Ventures, and Coinbase Ventures, yoUSD remains a sophisticated {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} product. The open question is whether the extra yield compensates for the portfolio's tail risk.

ustb-superstate.title: Wall Street's On-Chain Fund
ustb-superstate.text: USTB is a tokenized short-duration government-securities fund managed by Invesco and held at BNY Mellon, with the manners and access limits of a traditional private fund because that is what it is. The share price accrues with daily NAV rather than maintaining a fixed dollar, and qualified purchasers subscribe or redeem in USD or USDC on business days. Public holdings, daily NAV disclosure, and institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} make the underlying {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure unusually legible; the restricted investor base makes open DEX liquidity beside the point. USTB matters less as a consumer {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} token than as collateral other protocols can use without building a BNY Mellon relationship. It is Wall Street's fund wrapper on-chain, which is both the innovation and the disclaimer.

ousg-ondo-finance.title: Ondo's Qualified-Purchaser Treasury Share
ousg-ondo-finance.text: OUSG is Ondo's tokenized U.S. Treasury fund share: a NAV-accreting token whose price has compounded far above a dollar rather than a pegged coin, restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers with on-chain KYC enforcement, so tokens cannot transfer to non-whitelisted addresses. The portfolio is no longer a BUIDL proxy. Ondo's July 2026 position table spreads the fund across State Street's Galaxy SWEEP, BlackRock BUIDL, Franklin BENJI, and Fidelity FYOXX, each with a double-digit share, plus small bank-deposit and USDC sleeves, and Ondo I LP remains among BUIDL's largest single holders. Instant T+0 mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via OUSGInstantManager against USDC makes the exit infrastructure better than most tokenized funds, yet the exit pillar is still the weakest of the three because access is eligibility-gated. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped by a reserve-composition gap: the live Chainlink NAV feed reports the fund as a single NAV row, so Pharos cannot classify the constituents it scores, and the evidence ceiling stays limited. Daily NAV reporting runs through a fund administrator whose reports have moved behind a sign-in wall. OUSG is a tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} that borrowed stablecoin infrastructure, with {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} exposure now diversified across four managers.

slvon-ondo.title: Silver ETF Rails
slvon-ondo.text: SLVon is Ondo Global Markets' tokenized exposure to the iShares Silver Trust, tracked as a {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} NAV asset rather than a $1 stablecoin. The token gives eligible non-U.S. investors economic exposure to SLV on Ethereum, BSC, Solana, and HyperEVM, with Ondo handling the issuer, subscription, and redemption infrastructure. The useful feature is composability for a listed ETF; the tradeoff is that holders own an Ondo GM token, not direct ETF shares or physical silver. Risk therefore lives in the Ondo GM legal structure, collateral attestations, access controls, and secondary-market liquidity.

iauon-ondo.title: Gold ETF Rails
iauon-ondo.text: IAUon is Ondo Global Markets' tokenized exposure to the iShares Gold Trust, modeled as a {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} NAV asset rather than a dollar stablecoin. It is gold-linked through the underlying IAU ETF exposure, with no direct claim on allocated bullion of the kind PAXG or XAUT offer. Ondo's multi-chain issuer rails make the ETF exposure portable across Ethereum, BSC, Solana, and HyperEVM, while eligibility restrictions and issuer controls remain central to the risk profile. The exit pillar is the weakest line on the {{grade}} report card: primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is eligibility-gated, and Ondo discloses the IAU shares and cash in transit behind the token only as an unsplit aggregate verified daily by Ankura Trust. The cleanest way to read IAUon is as tokenized listed-security exposure that borrows stablecoin-style settlement infrastructure.

mtbill-midas.title: Europe's T-Bill Token
mtbill-midas.text: mTBILL is Midas's compliance-first answer to the tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} race: exposure held mainly through BlackRock's IB01 ETF with Swiss {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Maerki Baumann, issued as a Liechtenstein FMA-approved MiFID II instrument and restricted to non-U.S. and non-UK retail. That is the exact bureaucratic architecture required to legally sell T-bill exposure to European professionals. Ankura Trust provides daily on-chain NAV {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, and the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral quality with regulated-entity governance earns institutional credibility that most crypto-native tokenized treasury products lack. The 'not available to U.S. or UK retail persons' restriction is the mirror image of USTB and OUSG's American access gates, carving out a European institutional niche in a market dominated by U.S. issuers. Deployed across five chains, mTBILL functions as infrastructure in Midas's product stack and as stable collateral in third-party structured products. It is the European {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market-fund-like{{/term}} token for protocols that need regulatory certainty over DeFi composability. Pharos still leaves the card unrated: the tokenholder exit route is undisclosed and the reviewed reserve is a single ETF slice with no fund look-through, so the evidence is insufficient for a research rating.

rusd-reservoir.title: Reservoir's Base Dollar
rusd-reservoir.text: rUSD is the non-yielding base asset under Reservoir's savings tokens: mintable and redeemable 1:1 for USDC, USDT, or USD1 through the protocol's {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}, but backed by a protocol balance sheet that also routes capital into lending markets and credit strategies. The live reserve feed makes the dependency stack visible: the August 2026 snapshot puts about a third of the book in Figure-originated HELOC private credit lent through a Morpho market, a further third in USDC positions, and the rest in a fixed-maturity Pendle principal token on USDat, GHO lending markets, and a multi-strategy carry vault. That gives rUSD more transparency than a black-box credit book, and the exit pillar leads the {{grade}} overall grade because the PSM exit is permissionless. Backing is the weakest of the three: the private-credit and carry-vault slices publish no internal allocation, the balance sheet sits in protocol-controlled adapters with no third-party custodian or bankruptcy-remote structure, and reserve re-use is the yield model. The {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise therefore depends on multiple upstream stablecoin issuers, DeFi venues, and a single Reservoir admin key rather than a simple cash account.

wsrusd-reservoir.title: Reservoir's rUSD Savings Wrapper
wsrusd-reservoir.text: wsrUSD is Reservoir's non-rebasing ERC-4626 savings wrapper over rUSD: depositing burns rUSD, withdrawing mints it back, and the share price rises as protocol yield accrues, so the token trades above a dollar by design. Its only direct reserve is that rUSD claim, verified from the wrapper's constructor and pinned contract reads; the T-bill, lending-vault, and basis strategies behind it live on the rUSD entry and are inherited rather than duplicated. That inheritance is the trade-off. Upstream rUSD reserves are actively re-deployed into lending markets and credit, no bankruptcy-remote structure is documented for holders, and rUSD {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is immediate only up to available {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} liquidity. Pharos scores the exit pillar at the floor because no viable exit route is established for the wrapper itself, and a child cannot rate above its parent; together those drive the {{grade}} overall grade. The wrapper contract is immutable, but its manager role sits with a 3-of-5 Safe that an admin EOA can still reassign, and all but one of its tracked deployments are {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} representations, mostly LayerZero OFTs. The durable constraint is that wsrUSD carries every rUSD risk plus its own bridge and liquidity dependencies.

dusd-alto.title: The Isolated Vault Stablecoin
dusd-alto.text: DUSD is Alto's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style dollar. It is minted from isolated Ethereum markets for ETH and LSTs, sUSDe, and Syrup USDC, each ring-fenced with per-asset risk parameters, with a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}-style stability module as the peg backstop. The architecture advertises collateral diversity, but the ledger tells a different story: roughly nine-tenths of the backing now sits in the stability module as frxUSD, with the isolated mint markets contributing only a thin tail of ETH, LST, and sUSDe debt, making it less a kitchen-sink CDP and more a Frax wrapper with an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} garnish. That shows up in the classification: ALTO holders still govern the protocol, but the frxUSD dependency drags DUSD into centralized-dependent territory, inheriting Frax's {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} chain wholesale. The peg record is clean on a small float with limited price coverage, and stress monitoring has mostly sat at the quiet end of the scale, though at this size quiet owes as much to thin markets as to design. The {{grade}} overall grade, with the exit pillar the softest of the three because its routes share a failure domain, sums it up: careful risk engineering. The biggest risk decision, the identity of the dollar backing yours, was settled in Frax's favor.

dusd-dtrinity.title: Chain-Isolated Reserves, Unpublished Weights
dusd-dtrinity.text: dUSD is dTRINITY's dollar stablecoin, minted atomically 1:1 against whitelisted reserve stablecoins and yieldcoins such as USDC, USDT, sUSDS and sfrxUSD, redeemed for a fee of up to 50 bps, with Curve {{term:amo}}AMOs{{/term}} pre-minting dUSD into pools and buyback operations retiring it when it trades at a discount. Each deployment on Ethereum, Fraxtal, Katana and Sonic keeps its own isolated reserve with no cross-chain collateral sharing. The {{grade}} overall grade rests on what is not published: the protocol exposes eligible assets and vault accounting, but no dated attestation and no weighted reserve table across chains, and on Ethereum the vault is dominated by AMO accounting receipts rather than itemised Curve legs, so backing is graded on an undisclosed composition. Economic control fares no better: six contracts hold minter roles across the four tokens, the token has no supply cap, and Sonic's proxy admin sits under a small Safe with no timelock. The exit pillar is nonetheless the weakest of the three, and a governance pause role can halt all transfers globally. The peg score is the strongest line on the card, with a long tail of brief episodes and one sharp discount in March 2026, and the binding terms disclaim any fiduciary, custodian or recovery obligation to holders. Until dTRINITY publishes a reconciled reserve balance sheet, that gap is the constraint.

sdusd-dtrinity.title: The dUSD Lender Receipt
sdusd-dtrinity.text: sdUSD is dTRINITY's yield-bearing wrapper for dUSD deposits in dLEND, so the token is best read as liquid dUSD lender exposure rather than a separate reserve asset. The wrapper is chain-isolated like dUSD itself: Ethereum sdUSD and Fraxtal sdUSD use separate deployments and are not fungible across chains. Yield comes from dLEND supply APY and accrues through the vault's NAV, while exits depend on available dUSD liquidity in dLEND or secondary-market depth. The important dependency is direct: sdUSD inherits dUSD reserve, peg, exploit, and dLEND bad-debt risk, with an extra strategy-vault layer on top. Pharos therefore treats sdUSD as a tracked {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} NAV variant of dUSD.

thbill-theo.title: Treasury Basket, Weights Undisclosed
thbill-theo.text: thBILL is Theo's NAV-accreting tokenized Treasury product. Its reserve is now a basket of two institutional funds, Wellington/Libeara ULTRA and Fidelity International FILQ, held through tokenised wrappers, with Theo managing the allocation and publishing no current weights. FILQ may hold asset-backed commercial paper as well as government securities, so Pharos treats the whole basket as an opaque fund-share exposure rather than direct T-bill ownership. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars because of that missing composition and because Theo publishes no dated, independently administered NAV or basket-to-supply reconciliation. Mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are KYC-gated and limited to institutional and non-U.S. accredited investors, settled in USDC with underlying collateral on a T+4 timeline, which keeps the exit pillar in the lower half of the card. The contract side is cleaner: the canonical token is an ERC-4626 vault with no privileged raw mint, governed by a two-day timelock under Theo's 4-of-6 Safe, and LayerZero carries it to four other chains. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects a structure whose underlying assets are institutional but whose disclosure stops one layer above them. The durable constraint is that holders own a wrapper on a wrapper, with no published look-through.

sources.label: Theo thBILL product page (ULTRA + FILQ basket)

usdp-parallel.title: Parallelizer Basket Dollar
usdp-parallel.text: Parallel USDp is the liquid base dollar for a system built around the Parallelizer, a governed basket module rather than a single issuer bank account. The collateral list is a greatest-hits compilation of other stablecoin risks: frxUSD and sfrxUSD, USDe and sUSDe, USDS and sUSDS, plus USDC-linked Avalanche exposure. That makes the peg mechanics elegant and dependency analysis ugly, because overcollateralized basket issuance does not erase the fact that several upstream coins have their own governance, custody, and collateral assumptions. sPRL governance sets accepted collateral and exposure limits, so the real safety control is parameter discipline. USDp is useful as a liquid routing token, but it is a committee-managed index of other people's dollars rather than a clean dollar.

usdpt-western-union.title: Settlement Dollar, Now Spendable
usdpt-western-union.text: USDPT is Western Union's attempt to turn agent and treasury settlement into an on-chain dollar rail without pretending to be a DeFi-native coin. Anchorage Digital Bank issues it on Solana, with reserves almost entirely in a JPMorgan Treasury money-market fund plus a sliver of bank deposits, examined monthly by Deloitte under a regulated U.S. banking setup. The distribution thesis stopped being theoretical on August 4, 2026, when Western Union and stablecoin-payments firm Rain launched Stablecard, a USDPT wallet paired with a Visa card, live in 37 markets at launch. The product bolts consumer spend onto the physical agent network most issuers would pitch as a 2030 roadmap slide. Mint and redemption remain centralized issuer operations, and on-chain circulation is still pilot scale, a rounding error next to Western Union's remittance flows. In V9 terms that reads as strong backing behind a locked door: reserve quality grades near the top of the class while the exit pillar is the weakest of the three by a wide margin, because a holder's real exit is the issuer and the card rather than the market. The card widens where USDPT can be spent, while redemption stays an issuer operation for eligible parties.

sources.label: crypto.news: Western Union launches USDPT Visa card with Rain

roughrider-bnd.title: State-Owned Banking Goes On-Chain
roughrider-bnd.text: North Dakota's Bank of North Dakota, the only state-owned bank in the US, cleared its biggest hurdle on March 25 when the Industrial Commission unanimously approved the bank-to-bank use case for Roughrider Coin. Ten local banks have already expressed pilot interest, CEO Don Morgan rates the risk as 'low to moderate,' and the project is expected to be cost-neutral to the state. The coin runs on Solana via Fiserv's infrastructure, backed by USD reserves and 93-day {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} notes under the GENIUS Act's state-issued stablecoin exemption. It won't be publicly tradeable. This is pure interbank settlement plumbing, voluntary for ND banks and credit unions. September 2026 remains the target, pending Fiserv contract finalization. As the second US state stablecoin after Wyoming's FRNT, Roughrider represents an emerging pattern: state treasurers discovering that blockchain settlement is cheaper than correspondent banking.

fiusd-fiserv.title: The Payments Stack Play
fiusd-fiserv.text: FIUSD is Fiserv's pre-launch Solana dollar stablecoin built on Circle and Paxos infrastructure: a payments-rails play with four-partner coordination risk. Fiserv wants to make stablecoins just another rail in the infrastructure it already runs for roughly 10,000 financial institution clients and six million merchant locations, so FIUSD is less a single stablecoin and more a platform: Paxos handles issuance, Circle provides ecosystem interop, PayPal enables interoperability, and Mastercard connects the payments network. The centralized-dependent classification captures this architecture accurately; FIUSD depends on an entire constellation of {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} partners, any of which could become a {{term:bridge}}bottleneck{{/term}}. After the original end-of-2025 target slipped, CEO Mike Lyons said at June's Bernstein conference, "FIUSD goes live in July." July has now come and gone without a public launch confirmation, leaving Pharos still tracking the token as pre-launch. The interbank settlement pilot with Huntington and Bank of North Dakota remains the opening act, with the white-labeled Roughrider Coin queued behind it. The real test is whether four fintech giants can ship on one timeline.

sources.label: Payments Dive: Fiserv stablecoin arrives next month (June 3, 2026)
CoinDesk: Fiserv joins stablecoin fray with Circle, Paxos, PayPal (June 2025)

gelt-tether.title: Georgia's Lari, Tether's Rails
gelt-tether.text: GEL₮ is Tether's pre-launch Georgian Lari stablecoin, announced in May 2026 alongside the Government of Georgia and framed by Tether as the country's 'official' stablecoin. The framing is the story: a sovereign government handing its national currency's digital rails to the world's largest stablecoin issuer, while the National Bank of Georgia runs its own separate digital-lari pilot. The legal scaffolding is real. NBG Order No. 52/04 lets licensed issuers mint Lari-pegged tokens under 100% reserves, full redemption rights, and a GEL 500,000 capital floor, deliberately built for compatibility with the US GENIUS Act. Everything that matters for an assessment is still blank: no chains, no contracts, no reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, no named {{term:custody}}custodian{{/term}}, no launch date. With prime-minister and central-bank endorsements but a non-USD peg Pharos doesn't yet price, this is a flag planted on a map rather than a token you can hold. Whether 'official' means anything more than a sharper logo on a 1:1 Tether liability is the question the missing disclosures will eventually answer.

eur-qivalis.title: Thirty-Seven Banks, One Euro
eur-qivalis.text: QEUR is a pre-launch MiCA-oriented euro stablecoin from a banking consortium that ballooned to 37 institutions across 15 countries by May 2026, up from 12 a few months earlier, targeting H2 2026 issuance under a Dutch EMI license. Qivalis is the European banking establishment's answer to USDC and Tether: a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin now backed by names like BNP Paribas, ING, UniCredit, BBVA, ABN Amro, Intesa Sanpaolo, Rabobank, and Nordea. The reserve design puts at least 40% in bank deposits and the remainder in short-term euro-area government bonds spread across EU countries. It reads like a {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} with a blockchain address. The chain question is settled: Ethereum mainnet first (ERC-20F with a permissioned KYC layer), then Polygon and Base. Only pre-verified participants can hold or transfer the token. This is the consortium's compromise between public-chain liquidity and institutional control. CEO Jan-Oliver Sell (ex-Coinbase Germany) is lining up exchange partnerships, and the EMI license application sits with De Nederlandsche Bank, filed but not granted; Qivalis says it will launch the moment approval lands. The central tension is unchanged and arguably sharper at 37 members: whether dozens of banks that compete fiercely everywhere else can cooperate long enough to ship before Circle's EURC and SocGen's EURCV finish eating the MiCA-compliant euro market. The ticker itself isn't even public yet. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits across consortium banks and 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rights remain pre-launch commitments.

pusd-polaris.title: Immutable CDP, Yield Included
pusd-polaris.text: pUSD is Polaris Finance's pre-launch Liquity-style immutable CDP stablecoin on Ethereum, built by co-founders TokenBrice and 0xLuude as what they call the successor to Liquity's ethos: immutable core contracts, no admin keys, and no off-chain assets. pUSD is minted against pETH collateral via {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}}, and the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} angle comes from protocol revenue: borrowing interest, swap fees, conversion gains, and DEX fees, rather than from depositing reserves into Aave. The public testnet is live on Sepolia with audits still ahead and no mainnet date set, since the team says it prioritises security over speed, which leaves it time to prove that you can ship immutability without sacrificing usability. For a market saturated with centralized fiat-backed tokens and yield products built on leverage, pUSD is a deliberate bet that there's still demand for the Liquity V1 philosophy, upgraded.

pgold-polaris.title: Synthetic Gold, No Vault Required
pgold-polaris.text: Polaris Gold is a pre-launch synthetic gold exposure that shares infrastructure with its sibling pUSD but pegs to gold rather than the dollar, with no physical backing and the protocol risk that comes with a decentralized design. Unlike XAUT or PAXG, which tokenize actual bars in Swiss vaults, pGOLD is minted from the same pETH collateral pool via {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} on Ethereum. This makes it arguably more decentralized than any gold-pegged token on the market, at the cost of carrying all the risks of crypto collateral in a down market. Whether DeFi users want synthetic gold exposure from immutable contracts instead of custodied metal from Tether or Paxos is an experiment Polaris is willing to run.

usg-tangent.title: Productive Collateral, Dynamic Rates
usg-tangent.text: Tangent Finance built USG as an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin for productive DeFi collateral: Curve LP tokens, Pendle PTs, and other {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} or LP positions rather than plain ETH. The peg mechanism borrows from crvUSD's playbook but explicitly skips {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}: Peg Keepers, dynamic interest rates, and reward deductions grow more aggressive as USG weakens, pushing borrowers toward repayment while sUSG, the Yearn v3 savings wrapper, receives 25% of protocol revenue. Read the Etherscan supply line with care: roughly nine-tenths of the contract's total sits preminted in two protocol contracts, Peg Keeper-style, leaving genuine circulation a small fraction of the headline total, and Pharos sizes it from on-chain circulating supply rather than an aggregator listing. The v9 scorecard captures the beta candor precisely: a spotless peg record and mid-tier backing and exit pillars sit under a {{grade}} overall grade, because economic control is the weakest pillar by a wide margin on a multisig-run, centrally dependent system that lists five audit reports, Sherlock, Egis, two Pashov reviews, and Zerocool, beside placeholder site metrics. The design bets that DeFi-native collateral can be more capital-efficient than traditional {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} models, while inheriting the composability risk of every protocol whose tokens it accepts and a {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} surface only as deep as each underlying market.

klarnausd-klarna.title: KlarnaUSD testnet stablecoin on Tempo
klarnausd-klarna.text: Klarna's planned USD stablecoin runs on Tempo through Stripe Bridge Open Issuance, but it remains testnet-only with mainnet timing undecided. Klarna, the Swedish fintech with 114 million customers and $112B in annual GMV, is building the coin through Stripe's Bridge infrastructure on the Tempo L1. Tempo mainnet went live on March 18, 2026 with sub-second finality and fees under $0.001, and its Machine Payments Protocol, co-authored with Stripe, targets autonomous AI agent payments, yet KlarnaUSD was absent from a mainnet launch partners list that included Anthropic, Mastercard, Visa, and Revolut. The regulatory basis is firmer than the timeline: Bridge's conditional OCC national bank trust charter, approved in February, supplies regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and an {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} framework, while the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window is scoped to Klarna's settlement flows rather than open DeFi liquidity. KlarnaUSD remains on Tempo's testnet: Klarna's Q1 and Q2 2026 earnings calls did not mention it, it is absent from Bridge Open Issuance's live issuer list, and the November 2025 announcement remains the only official word.

trusd-tori.title: Ethena's Playbook, Politely Executed
trusd-tori.text: trUSD is Tori Finance's run at the playbook Ethena popularized: a synthetic dollar backed by {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} trading positions ({{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} arbitrage, calendar spreads, hedged money markets) with a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} staked wrapper, strUSD. The launch sequencing was unusually disciplined: Sherlock and Nethermind audits came before deployment, Accountable's real-time proof-of-solvency started on day one, Nexus Mutual covered the pre-deposit vault, and the $50M pre-deposit cap filled in seven days. Accountable now attests a four-bucket split led by hedged money-market positions, and Pharos treats that split as verified. The open questions are the classic synthetic-dollar ones, and Pharos's on-chain review sharpened them: primary NAV mint and redeem are KYC-whitelisted in the contract itself, so the 'no verification' marketing refers only to secondary swaps; the custodian banks holding most of the attested backing are unnamed by policy; and independent tracing of the sole custodian wallet shows collateral flowing to exchange deposit addresses. Mint and redemption quotes are also set by Tori's own backend with no on-chain price feed. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars, which is why the {{grade}} overall grade sits low despite a peg that has held at par since launch. Delphi-backed, Ethereum-only, and single-entity operated, trUSD is a trading desk in stablecoin form, and its track record is still under six months.

sources.label: The Defiant: Tori fills $50M pre-deposit cap before launch (2026-07-27)
Cryip: Tori secures backing from Delphi Ventures (2026-03-25)

ussd-sonic-labs.title: Yield Without the Yield
ussd-sonic-labs.text: Sonic Labs's USSD is a permissionless, zero-fee wrapper around Sonic frxUSD, so the reserve story belongs upstream to Frax rather than directly to a basket of {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} tokens. The design choice remains pointed: the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} yield generated by that upstream backing flows to the Sonic ecosystem as buybacks and incentives, while USSD holders keep a flat dollar claim. That makes USSD less an independent stablecoin than a branded distribution layer over frxUSD, complete with the same reserve dependencies plus omnichain route risk of its own. If it reaches scale, the protocol captures the carry while users supply the non-yielding balance sheet. It is a tidy business model dressed as neutral infrastructure.

pgold-pleasing.title: Pleasing's Partly Assured Gold Token
pgold-pleasing.text: PGOLD is Pleasing International's gold token: one PGOLD is intended to represent one troy ounce of LBMA-standard 99.99% bullion held with undisclosed qualified custodians in Hong Kong, with KYC-gated physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through the Pleasing platform. Arbitrum is the only native issuance chain; Ethereum, Pharos, and ApeChain are Chainlink CCIP and LayerZero representations. The assurance picture improved in June 2026 when VISTO CPA published a limited-assurance report, but the report physically observed about half of the claimed bullion, relied on issuer assertions for the rest, excluded weight, purity, and valuation, and covered only the Arbitrum liability, so Pharos treats the audited composition as stale against its freshness bound. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the economic-control pillar, the weakest of the three: a single EOA can mint directly on Arbitrum, a separate EOA-owned ProxyAdmin can replace the mint logic with no delay, and no active vault, custodian, insurance schedule, or anti-rehypothecation term is published. The exit pillar is nearly as weak because physical redemption is documented but no score-eligible same-notional route exists. For Pleasing's existing gold corridor clients, PGOLD may serve as a convenient tokenized rail; for everyone else, the {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} remains unverifiable and the admin keys remain unbounded.

sources.label: PGOLD live Reserve Report (VISTO CPA assurance report, 2026-06-25)

ggbr-goldfish-gold.title: Gold Token on a Mining Claim
ggbr-goldfish-gold.text: GGBR is Goldfish Gold's gold-tracking token, priced at 1/1000 of a troy ounce against the LBMA spot price and minted and redeemed through issuer-controlled contracts on Ethereum. The backing is where it parts company with XAUT or PAXG: the issuer's collateral disclosure describes 1,000,000 troy ounces of in-situ gold in the Happy 2 mining claims in Arizona, held by a GGBR Trust for holders and pledged through a lien on mineral rights, with a designated on-chain wallet holding a related-party ION.au token balance as the real-time proof. That is a claim on unmined ore and on an affiliate's security. The disclosure cites a qualified-person resource estimate for the ore but does not name the trustee, the custodian, or the segregation terms, and nobody independently attests the gold quantity against token supply. Pharos scores the {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} as institutional and unregulated, with no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: physical redemption is described only through precious-metals dealers and no score-eligible runtime route is compiled. Mint authority rests with a single issuer key, and a 2-of-3 Safe controls the token's upgrades. The peg has tracked gold with a short tail of brief episodes; the durable constraint is that the token references gold in the ground, and the trust chain runs through Goldfish alone.

gldt-gold-dao.title: NFT Gold, Fungible Wrapper
gldt-gold-dao.text: GLDT is Gold DAO's fungible wrapper over GLD NFTs, each token standing for a hundredth of a gram of gold in Swiss vaults, minted when NFTs are locked in a swap canister on the Internet Computer and carried to Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum through a single-operator lock-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}. Gold DAO's own terms state that GLDT is not legal ownership of gold and that redemption is not guaranteed; a holder must first reverse-swap into a GLD NFT, which alone is described as a deed to a bar. The evidence trail stops in September 2025. KPMG SA Neuchâtel signed a Swiss Auditing Standard 920 report of factual findings, expressly neither an audit nor a review and restricted in use, counting 7.9 kilograms of gold at a Loomis vault in Kloten and reconciling it to GLD NFT certificates issued by Bity Tokenisation; GLDT supply itself was not reconciled. No successor report has appeared, so the composition falls outside Pharos's freshness window and the card carries no overall grade: NR here means insufficient evidence for a rating, with backing and exit both sitting at the bottom of the pillars while economic control still grades. The gold is probably still in Kloten; what the record can no longer show is that anyone checked recently, or ever checked against the token you actually hold.

sources.label: Gold DAO audit reports (KPMG SA Neuchatel)

axcnh-anchorx.title: The Offshore Yuan
axcnh-anchorx.text: AnchorX's AxCNH is a centralized offshore-yuan stablecoin backed by CNH cash reserves and issued under a Kazakhstan AFSA license. The product gives on-chain access to offshore Chinese yuan exposure, which is structurally interesting precisely because the onshore currency remains capital-controlled and politically delicate. Pharos now treats the custody model as institutional-regulated, but the trust stack is still almost entirely issuer-side: AnchorX manages minting, redemption, and reserve reporting, while Ethereum and Conflux mint surfaces depend on multisig-controlled issuer machinery. The issuer describes the reserve as CNH cash and its public feed shows circulation matching reserves to the unit, but the asset classes, custodian, and account terms are undisclosed and the Kreston procedures reports sit behind a sign-in wall, so Pharos carries the whole reserve as an unresolved envelope and the evidence falls short of what a research rating requires. AxCNH is less a DeFi primitive than a regulated corridor for a currency everyone wants near but not too near.

idrt-rupiah-token.title: Indonesia's Digital Rupiah
idrt-rupiah-token.text: Rupiah Token's IDRT is backed 1:1 by IDR bank deposits held by PT Rupiah Token Indonesia and issued natively on Ethereum, BSC, and Polygon, with a dormant legacy Harmony representation, making it one of the more broadly distributed local-currency stablecoins. The proof story has inched forward: the issuer now publishes accountant-prepared AUP reports, a form of {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} that confirms bank balances without expressing assurance, and the July 2026 report reconciled deposits to circulating supply at 1:1 without naming the banks. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} remains institutional and unregulated, and the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path still depends entirely on the issuer honoring KYC-gated fiat exits. The regulatory gray area is closing without IDRT in the room: OJK passed a rival rupiah-stablecoin issuer through its regulatory sandbox in June 2026, opening a formal registration path that turns self-defined compliance from a market condition into a choice. The {{grade}} report card splits sharply: economic control is the strongest pillar because the token is a plain non-upgradeable ERC20 under one 4-of-6 Safe on each native chain, while backing and exit are both weak on undisclosed custody and an eligibility-gated route out. The peg holds only loosely, with a long tail of recorded deviation events across a seven-year operating life. The durable constraint is that IDRT's compliance stays self-defined until it enters the registration path OJK has now opened.

sources.label: OJK June 2026 board meeting press release

tryb-bilira.title: Quarterly Examined Lira Token
tryb-bilira.text: TRYB is BiLira's Turkish-lira stablecoin, issued natively on nine networks, and the product itself has not changed: issuer-held TRY cash in Turkish bank accounts and centralized mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. BiLira's reserve reports come from Corpus Denetim as a genuine examination with full asset-and-liability reconciliation, materially better paperwork than most regional fiat tokens produce. The August 2026 examination found lira balances exceeding tokens outstanding, and Pharos anchors composition to that examined date. The catch is cadence: on a quarterly cycle an honest examination goes stale between filings, so the backing pillar rises and falls with the calendar rather than with the reserve. The banks holding the cash are not named, and the auditor's notes on custody sit outside the assurance opinion. Exit is the weakest of the three pillars, because there is no comparable same-notional route out of the position beyond the issuer. That is what holds the {{grade}} overall grade down while economic control, run through 2-of-3 and 3-of-6 Safes, scores well. The peg record carries a long tail of episodes, tracked on a fallback price source. TRYB is useful infrastructure with a disclosure-cadence problem, and that distinction matters most when the lira itself is under pressure.

sources.label: Corpus Denetim independent TRYB assurance report - August 17, 2026

ebusd-ebisu.title: Exotic Collateral, Orderly Exit
ebusd-ebisu.text: Ebisu's ebUSD was a Liquity V2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with one of the most eclectic collateral baskets Pharos tracked: sUSDe, WBTC, LBTC, stcUSD, and weETH mixed into {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} branches deployed natively on Ethereum and Plasma. The mechanism was sound; the market never showed up. Supply peaked near $815K and had bled below $25K by the time the team announced a wind-down on July 29, 2026: minting paused, users asked to close Troves and pull Stability Pool and DEX deposits, and the frontend slated for deprecation at the end of October.
