Stablecorp's live balances API gives Pharos real-time supply and reserve totals, which is better than the monthly PDF treasure hunt some issuers still call transparency. The tradeoff is scale and centralization: minting and redemption run through Stablecorp or authorized partners, with Safe-controlled token ownership and upgrade paths rather than permissionless plumbing. For a non-USD stablecoin, QCAD is useful because it is boring in the right places and still small enough that liquidity remains the unglamorous part of the story.

usdxl-last.title: Last USD in Wind-Down
usdxl-last.text: Last USD (USDXL) is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style synthetic dollar minted on HypurrFi, an Aave V3 fork on HyperEVM operated by Last, drawn against HYPE, HYPE LSTs, {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} BTC, and ETH collateral with {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} as the only peg defense and no public holder {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rail. Its issuance venue is now in wind-down: HypurrFi announced that its Legacy and Pooled markets would close by July 15, 2026, raised USDXL borrow rates to 30% to force repayment, and suspended new pooled borrows, leaving the token's access-control roles empty and a 2-of-2 proxy-admin Safe as the only remaining upgrade power. Neither Last nor HypurrFi publishes a dated collateral inventory across the market, flash-loan, and USDT0 PSM facilitator paths, so backing is scored on an undisclosed allocation. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the control pillar, the weakest of the three, with a single-source oracle topology, a missing comparable exit route, and a supply too small to clear the peg floor stacked on top. Peg tracking shows a run of brief deviations from par. The asset spans HyperEVM and Hyperliquid spot through a platform-native representation, and whatever remains outstanding is a claim on a market that is closing rather than growing.

bnusd-balanced.title: The Dollar Left Behind
bnusd-balanced.text: bnUSD is Balanced's cross-chain decentralized dollar, borrowed against {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} positions with a Stability Fund swapping USDC and USDT 1:1 to support the peg. It began life in 2021 as ICON's flagship CDP stablecoin, and that era formally ended on April 7, 2026, when Balanced v2 launched as a cross-chain money market powered by SODAX: the v1 app now exists only for withdrawals, and current issuance runs against a SODAX-wrapped collateral basket spanning Treasury-bill vaults, stablecoins, and a long tail of bridged crypto. Pharos still tracks the legacy ICON-hub deployments, and the {{grade}} report card reads accordingly: backing is the strongest pillar, while exit and economic control both sit at the bottom of the scale, exit because no comparable route is established for the tracked supply and control because a single EOA owns the Governance SCORE that can raise the debt ceiling and upgrade mint logic. Secondary liquidity has followed the protocol to its new home, leaving the tracked supply technically solvent and practically stranded. The tracked feed's price coverage is limited, so a clean peg print says little here: a stablecoin can hold a dollar on paper while the market that would let you realize that dollar packs up and leaves.

dusd-fluid.title: The Oracle Went Quiet
dusd-fluid.text: Fluid Finance's DUSD was designed as an Arbitrum stablecoin backed by safeguarded bank cash, with an issuer oracle capping minting at the reported off-chain balance. That was a neat bridge between bank reconciliation and smart-contract supply control; it is not the same thing as current proof that the bank accounts, oracle, or redemption rail still operate. Pharos could not verify a recent reserve report, active banking counterparties, live balance publication, or a working {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route, so the old 'verifiable 24/7' pitch now reads more like historical architecture than present-tense assurance. Single-chain simplicity removes bridge risk but offers little comfort when the evidence path itself has gone quiet. DUSD is a useful reminder that an oracle-enforced ceiling is only as current as the entity still publishing the number.

iusd-initia.title: Initia's AUSD-wrapped ecosystem dollar
iusd-initia.text: iUSD is the native dollar on Initia, the young Move-based Cosmos L1: a single-chain wrapper backed 1:1 by Agora's AUSD bridged in via LayerZero, so the ultimate reserve trace is Agora's short-dated U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}, repos, and cash custodied at State Street under VanEck management. Unlike standard fiat-backed stables, the reserve yield is redirected by Initia into ecosystem incentives that fund Echelon lending, liquidity programs, and Cabal vaults rather than paid to holders. Supply remains tiny and Initia publishes no attestation for the wrapper itself, so the backing pillar leans on Agora's AUSD transparency and holds up reasonably. The exit pillar fails outright because getting out means a LayerZero {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} hop before Agora's USD {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window even applies, and that trapped exit is what pins the overall grade at {{grade}} despite a spotless peg record. Holders therefore depend on the LayerZero bridge and Agora's redemption window for any exit, and on Agora's reserve {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} for the asset itself.

usdcx-movement.title: Movement's native USDC-backed dollar
usdcx-movement.text: USDCx is Movement's native dollar, issued through Circle's xReserve contract: deposit USDC, mint USDCx one-for-one, and move it back out via CCTP and Gateway without a third-party {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}. The issuer is the key distinction. Movement's own team issues USDCx rather than Circle, so this is partner-issued plumbing whose solvency is borrowed from Circle's reserves and Circle's {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} rather than owed by Circle to the holder. The report card reflects that borrowing directly. Backing and economic control both sit at the top of the scale, because the sole reserve is USDC locked in a Circle-deployed contract and the Movement token exposes no local free-mint path. The exit pillar is the weakest of the three and holds the {{grade}} overall grade well below its parent: a single-chain deployment, one issuer-native burn-and-mint route back to Ethereum, and an implementation launched in March 2026. A child cannot rate above the asset it wraps, and USDCx cannot rate above USDC. Circle can freeze the USDC in reserve, and the Movement module is upgradeable by a 4-of-6 multisig with no timelock, so holder-level controls could be added later. Reconciliation against the reserve contract is observable on-chain, but no independent party is documented as checking it. The durable constraint is that USDCx is only ever as good as the wrapper, the route, and the parent underneath.

usdh-hubble.title: Solana's original crypto-backed CDP stablecoin, now dormant
usdh-hubble.text: Hubble's USDH was Solana's first MakerDAO-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin, launched in January 2022 and minted against {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} vaults of SOL, mSOL, BTC, and ETH with Stability Pool {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}}. That is the history; the present is a much smaller and mostly different asset. At the latest on-chain read, about ninety-four percent of outstanding USDH was issued through the {{term:psm}}Peg Stability Module{{/term}} against deposited USDC, with the CDP branch a sub-material remainder led by mSOL and SOL. Backing therefore inherits Circle, and it is the strongest pillar on the card. The {{grade}} overall grade sits near the bottom because the other two pillars fail: the borrowing program is upgradeable through a DAO council where three of seven votes clear the threshold with no hold-up, and exits depend on a thin single-chain market with negligible secondary volume. The token itself is clean, with no freeze authority and no holder blacklist. Circle can freeze the PSM's USDC; it cannot touch a wallet's USDH. The team has pivoted its development energy to sister protocol Kamino Finance; no formal sunset has been announced and the borrow app remains live, but USDH is structurally dormant rather than growing. The 'USDH' symbol is shared with Native Markets and Hermetica, three distinct issuers with three distinct collateral models.

zkusd-goal3.title: Goal3 zkUSD, Reserves Unevidenced
zkusd-goal3.text: zkUSD is an issuer-controlled token on ZKsync Era minted through Goal3's lockdrop portal, originally the in-house dollar of the Goal3 sportsbook. The verified portal code accepts owner-configured stable tokens, forwards deposits to a treasury address, and mints the return token through a vesting flow. That is the whole evidenced mechanism; 1:1 USDC {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, reserve coverage, and a peg-maintenance route are not established. The only reserve-adjacent address Pharos could identify, the portal treasury, held no USDC or USDC.e at the reviewed block, and explorer history shows its USDC.e moved out in tranches through October 2024 to addresses no source identifies. Goal3's documentation site, main site, and X account no longer resolve. The reserve is therefore carried as fully unknown, the token and portal are UUPS proxies owned by a single EOA with no upgrade delay, and no primary exit exists, which is why every pillar and the {{grade}} overall grade sit at the bottom of the scale. The peg line rests on a single price source; with no evidenced backing and no issuer presence, that record cannot be read as a working dollar.

sources.label: Verified Goal3 portal implementation (zkSync Era explorer)

ist-agoric.title: Sunset by Governance
ist-agoric.text: IST was Agoric's textbook interchain dollar, built as an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} against IBC-bridged ATOM and stATOM with Dutch-auction {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, plus a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} swapping approved stablecoins 1:1. It is now a textbook example of how to shut one down. Agoric governance approved a strategic wind-down in spring 2025, ran a roughly 60-day sunset with liquidation fees zeroed so vault users could repay and reclaim collateral, and completed the shutdown on June 26, 2025; Pharos keeps the entry as a frozen archive because nothing mints anymore. The cause of death was not a depeg but a demand problem: an elegantly engineered mechanism on a chain whose DeFi ecosystem never grew large enough to need it. In a cemetery full of stablecoins that died screaming, IST is the rare one that filed the paperwork, gave holders an orderly exit, and turned off the lights. The shutdown made the constraint clear: IST's mechanism was sound, and the chain's ecosystem never generated enough demand for it.

benji-franklin-templeton.title: The Onchain '40 Act Fund
benji-franklin-templeton.text: BENJI is the on-chain share token for Franklin Templeton's FOBXX, an SEC-registered U.S. government {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} with a stable $1.00 NAV, custodied at JPMorgan Chase with Franklin Templeton as transfer agent and the token as the share record. Yield is distributed by rebasing the holder's share count on-chain rather than letting the price drift, which makes BENJI behave like a par-redeemable dollar even though it is legally a fund share. Fund assets grew sharply in the first half of 2026, passing $2.5 billion by July according to press coverage, with Pharos tracking deployments from Stellar and Ethereum to Solana and Aptos while the BNB Chain and Canton issuances remain unintegrated. The catch is telemetry: reserves run on a curated weekly snapshot of the official factsheet, and since mid-July 2026 Pharos has quarantined the listing and withheld circulating supply and market cap because no permitted runtime source reports a positive figure. A multi-billion-dollar fund the dashboard cannot cleanly count is the tokenisation story in miniature: the assets are real, the rails are registered, and the data still arrives by factsheet.

sources.label: Crypto Briefing: Franklin Templeton tokenized Treasury fund passes $2.5B (July 2026)

wtgxx-wisdomtree.title: WisdomTree's 24/7 Dealer-Traded Treasury Fund
wtgxx-wisdomtree.text: WTGXX is the digital share class of WisdomTree's Treasury Money Market Digital Fund, renamed from 'Government' in late 2025, a Rule 2a-7 '40 Act-registered {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} that received SEC approval in early 2026 to support 24/7 dealer trading at a fixed $1.00 NAV, making it one of the most stablecoin-like tokenized MMFs in market. Subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} are gated to WisdomTree Connect users with USDC dealer settlement and USD-wire alternatives; holdings are short-duration U.S. government obligations: {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}, floating-rate notes, and repos, which are the {{term:rwa}}real-world asset{{/term}} backing. The open problem is visibility: since mid-July 2026 Pharos has held WTGXX in quarantine because none of its permitted runtime sources report a positive circulating supply or market cap, so the token sits ungraded while the fund side keeps publishing its daily NAV. The share token spans seven networks from Ethereum to Stellar, and Chainlink's NAV feed still prices the reserves. Everything about this fund is measurable except how much of it actually lives on-chain. The '40 Act wrapper solved the trust problem; the telemetry problem turned out to be harder.

sources.label: WisdomTree Treasury Money Market Digital Fund (WTGXX), WisdomTree Connect fund page

vbill-vaneck.title: VanEck's Securitize-Administered Treasury Share
vbill-vaneck.text: VBILL is the on-chain share token for VanEck's Treasury Fund, with Van Eck advising the BVI Professional Fund and Securitize handling administration, tokenization, transfer agency, and KYC. The reserve stack is pleasantly dull: mostly short-duration U.S. T-bills with a cash and repo sleeve, while the token targets a stable $1.00 NAV and pays yield as newly issued tokens rather than accreting in price. Primary mint and redemption run through Securitize Markets against USDC, AUSD, or wire rails. Wormhole is the announced interoperability provider, but Pharos found no VBILL-specific Wormhole deployment: the Ethereum, Avalanche, BNB Chain, and Solana supplies are independently issued by the transfer agent under single-key, uncapped mint control on every chain. Pharos tracks the live NAV path through the Chainlink NAVLink feed and keeps the product framed as an institutional Treasury share, not a par retail stablecoin. Exit is the weakest pillar on the card, because the only route out is the institutional-only Securitize window and the issuer publishes no holder loss waterfall. VBILL is the kind of tokenized fund where the boring assets are the feature and the wrapper paperwork is the hobby.

acred-apollo-securitize.title: Private Credit, Not Treasuries
acred-apollo-securitize.text: ACRED is a tokenized, NAV-accreting feeder share into Apollo Diversified Credit Fund, a multi-strategy private credit portfolio combining direct lending, structured credit, performing credit, and dislocated credit. Unlike BUIDL or BENJI, the collateral is illiquid private credit rather than {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, so its risk profile is medium-to-high and closer to syrupUSDC than to a stable-NAV vehicle. Subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run at fund NAV through Securitize Markets for qualified purchasers, with quarterly repurchase offers of at least 5% of shares and an on-demand liquidity pool or secondary-market sales for intra-quarter exits, and RedStone publishes a NAV oracle used by integrations. Pharos tracks the Ethereum issuance plus the Avalanche, Ink, Polygon, Solana, and Aptos representations and flags this asset as a private-credit NAV token rather than a par stablecoin, with the exit pillar the weakest line on the card because no comparable same-notional exit route exists.

eutbl-spiko.title: Europe's First Tokenised T-Bill MMF
eutbl-spiko.text: EUTBL is Spiko's AMF-regulated UCITS short-term {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}} backed by Eurozone {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, the first AMF-regulated UCITS MMF tokenised on Ethereum. The fund holds short-dated Eurozone sovereign T-bills with weighted average maturity under two months, and EUTBL behaves as a VNAV (variable-NAV) share that accretes value as T-bill yield compounds. Primary subscriptions and redemptions settle same-day at fund NAV with a €1k minimum for KYC-allowlisted wallets, and Chainlink CCIP relays issuance across chains including Arbitrum and Polygon. EUTBL is one of Pharos's few EUR-pegged {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} assets and one of the cleanest fits for European institutional users seeking regulatory-grade tokenised cash. The {{grade}} overall grade is held back by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: primary redemption is eligibility-gated to allowlisted investors, so holders outside Spiko's KYC perimeter depend on secondary liquidity rather than the fund's own NAV window.

ustbl-spiko.title: Spiko's USD T-Bill MMF Cousin
ustbl-spiko.text: USTBL is the USD-denominated sister fund to Spiko's EUTBL: the same AMF-regulated UCITS {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} architecture, the same ERC-1967 upgradeable proxy, and the same multi-chain rollout, now spanning Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon, Base, Etherlink, Stellar, and Starknet with Chainlink CCIP announced for cross-chain movement, but holding short-dated U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills instead of Eurozone sovereigns. The VNAV share accretes value as T-bill yield compounds, with $1k minimums and same-day NAV settlement for allowlisted wallets that clear Spiko's KYC. Backed by {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral with CACEIS as custodian, BNY Mellon as sub-custodian, and a PwC statutory audit rather than a published periodic {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, USTBL behaves as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} share rather than a par stablecoin. On the Pharos card the exit pillar is the weakest of the three: subscriptions and redemptions run only through Spiko's transfer agent at a daily cutoff, so a holder outside that allowlist has no issuer-side route out.

jtrsy-anemoy.title: Janus Henderson's Tokenised T-Bill Fund
jtrsy-anemoy.text: JTRSY is the Janus Henderson Anemoy Treasury Fund, a BVI Professional Fund holding short-duration U.S. {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, where Janus Henderson acts as sub-advisor and Centrifuge runs the on-chain ERC-7540 vault. The fund carries an S&P fund credit rating and settles primary subscriptions and redemptions at fund NAV for whitelisted non-U.S. Professional Investors via Centrifuge's issuer rail. Pharos reads the Chainlink JTRSY NAV feed as live reserve evidence; the feed proves the share value but does not reproduce current holdings, cash sleeve, or named custodians, so the backing pillar is held below the level a fully disclosed T-bill portfolio would reach. The exit pillar is the weakest line on the card because redemption is eligibility-gated: a holder outside the whitelist has no comparable open route. The issuer also publishes no loss-recovery procedure for restoring NAV after an economic loss, which leaves the mechanism review bounded. Distribution extends across Centrifuge V3's burn-and-mint share bridge to eight chains, with mint authority resolving to a 4-of-9 Centrifuge protocol Safe. Holdings remain a tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share with permissioned Centrifuge {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and same-day NAV {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for those admitted.

bib01-backed.title: Backed's Dollar Treasury Tracker
bib01-backed.text: bIB01 is Backed Finance's NAV-accreting tracker certificate for the BlackRock iShares $ Treasury Bond 0-1yr UCITS ETF (IB01), registered under the Swiss DLT Act and not pegged to $1: the price drifts upward continuously as the underlying {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} ETF accrues yield, making it a tokenised {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share rather than a payment dollar. Primary mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are KYC-gated through Backed; secondary liquidity is on Uniswap and CoW Protocol. Reserves are proven daily through a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed that reads the ETF share count against Backed's published circulation, but the issuer publishes no product-specific administered NAV method or dated reserve-to-liability reconciliation, which bounds the backing review. bIB01 holds a {{grade}} overall grade and the exit pillar is the weakest of the three, because the primary route is eligibility-gated and the secondary venues do not change that on the card. bIB01 deploys on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Gnosis, and Avalanche using the same contract address pattern that Backed uses across its product line.

bc3m-backed.title: Backed's EUR Govt Bond Tracker
bc3m-backed.text: bC3M is Backed Finance's EUR-denominated, NAV-accreting tracker certificate for the Amundi GOVIES 0-6 Months Euro Investment Grade UCITS ETF, KYC-gated and registered under the Swiss DLT Act, which makes it one of the few EUR-pegged {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} tokens in Pharos and economically the euro analogue of a {{term:treasury}}Treasury-bond{{/term}} tracker. Same framework as bIB01, same KYC-gated primary issuance through Backed and KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, same Uniswap / CoW secondary liquidity surfaces. Reserves are proven daily through a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed that publishes the ETF share count, but Backed does not publish a product-specific administered NAV method or a dated reserve-to-liability reconciliation, which bounds the backing review. bC3M holds a {{grade}} overall grade and the exit pillar is the weakest of the three, because primary redemption is eligibility-gated and the secondary venues do not change that on the card. Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract first; Backed also publishes the asset at the same address on Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis.

ntbill-nest.title: Nest's On-Plume Treasury Vault
ntbill-nest.text: nTBILL is Nest Credit's {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} vault: a NAV-accreting share whose value tracks a curated book of Superstate USTB and Janus Henderson JTRSY positions, plus a small stablecoin liquidity buffer, with primary mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Nest at vault NAV rather than par. Reserves are sourced live from the Nest Credit positions API, both underlying funds publish short Treasury-bill maturities with daily or market-day liquidity, and the economic-control pillar is the strongest line on the card. Pharos tracks nTBILL because it references a dollar base, but the token behaves like a tokenised {{term:money-market-fund}}fund-of-funds{{/term}} share rather than a par-redeemable stablecoin. The card is unrated: the exit pillar is the weakest of the three because redemption is eligibility-gated through a rail shared by five Nest vaults, and Nest publishes no vault-level maturity, assurance, or custody-continuity inputs, so the mechanism review stays bounded and the evidence does not support a research rating. The durable constraint is a strong underlying book behind a single, permissioned exit.

nbasis-nest.title: Nest's Basis-Trade Vault
nbasis-nest.text: nBASIS is Nest Credit's {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} vault: a NAV-accreting share whose book is mostly the Superstate USCC cash-and-carry fund, with a smaller Superstate USTB {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} sleeve and a thin stablecoin buffer, so the {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} and futures carry sits inside the underlying fund rather than being run by Nest directly. Closer in profile to Ethena USDe or Midas mRe7YIELD than to a par stablecoin, the token's value drifts with {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} performance rather than holding $1. Pharos lists it because the strategy references the dollar as its base and the Nest Credit positions API publishes live NAV, but the methodology treats nBASIS as a strategy vault with high collateral-quality risk and a NAV-token notice. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three: primary redemption is eligibility-gated through Nest, five Nest vaults share the same redemption rail, and no margin or liquidation disclosure for the underlying fund is published. The durable constraint is that a Nest share is only as redeemable as Nest's single rail.

nopal-nest.title: Nest's BlackOpal Credit Vault
nopal-nest.text: nOPAL is Nest Credit's BlackOpal LiquidStone II vault: a NAV-accreting share over tokenised private-credit positions, a Brazilian credit-card receivables fund, plus a small nTBILL {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} sleeve and stablecoin liquidity buffer. Like other Nest vaults, primary access runs through Nest at vault NAV, and it is not a par-redeemable stablecoin. Pharos flags nOPAL as a private-credit vault share; the high-risk reserve slice reflects the underlying LiquidStone II credit positions classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent exposure, and the fund's obligor-level receivables, service providers, and any fund-level audit are not public. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by exit and economic control, both at the bottom of the card: redemption is eligibility-gated through a rail shared by five Nest vaults, and issuance is unbounded with no independent whole-supply reconciliation. The durable constraint is a credit book Pharos cannot see behind a single Nest rail.

nwisdom-nest.title: Nest's WisdomTree-Backed Vault
nwisdom-nest.text: nWISDOM is Nest Credit's vault share built around WisdomTree Connect tokenised fund exposure (xCRDYX) with a small nTBILL and stablecoin liquidity buffer, classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent vault exposure rather than a par stablecoin. Yield accretes through the underlying WisdomTree fund NAV; primary mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through Nest at vault NAV against USDC and pUSD. The {{grade}} overall grade is low across all three pillars. The September 2026 positions capture shows almost the entire book in xCRDYX, and the capture publishes no underlying securities, obligors, custody, or holder seniority, so the backing pillar treats that slice as opaque. The exit pillar is the weakest of the three: redemption is eligibility-gated and shares the Nest Credit redemption rail with four sibling vaults, so one operational failure would hit all of them. Minting is issuer-direct with no evidenced supply cap, which keeps the economic-control pillar down as well.

susdc-spark.title: Spark's USDC share class on the vault savings rate
susdc-spark.text: Spark Savings USDC lets USDC holders earn Spark's vault savings rate without first converting into USDS, with idle deposits pulled out and deployed by the Spark Liquidity Layer. Unlike the immutable Morpho vaults it competes with, spUSDC is a UUPS proxy whose mint-critical logic can be replaced through Sky's forty-eight-hour governance pause on Ethereum and through Spark's LayerZero-driven executor on Avalanche. It is visible, delayed on one chain, and still a live upgrade path, which is why economic control is the weakest of the three pillars. Backing sits just above it, because Pharos never credited spUSDC with Circle's reserve in the first place: the slice is scored as an aggregate Spark protocol position whose split between idle USDC and downstream strategies is not published. Exit leads the card, since withdrawals redeem directly from vault USDC liquidity. The {{grade}} overall grade is therefore a verdict on who can change the rules and what the deposits are actually doing.

susdt-spark.title: USDT-denominated Spark Savings vault
susdt-spark.text: Spark Savings USDT is the Tether-denominated version of Spark's savings vault: deposits earn a vault savings rate set by Spark while a permissioned Spark Liquidity Layer taker deploys idle USDT into lending and other strategies. The wrapper gives USDT holders a rising share price, but the risk stack inherits Tether issuer exposure, Spark vault mechanics, Sky governance decisions, and whatever liquidity the vault can actually supply on withdrawal. That is a lot of institutional and protocol trust to package as one tidy ERC-4626 receipt. Pharos treats spUSDT separately from spUSDC because changing the underlying issuer changes the dependency surface, even if the vault interface looks nearly identical. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars: Spark does not publish the current strategy split or the downstream custodian set for this vault, and the Arbitrum deployment holds USDT0, a LayerZero bridge representation of Tether's Ethereum USDT. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects the same savings plumbing, a different centralized dollar underneath, and an unpublished allocation.

sgho-aave.title: Aave's non-slashable GHO savings module
sgho-aave.text:
Aave Savings GHO (sGHO) is an ERC-4626 savings vault on Ethereum whose shares increase in GHO value as yield accrues. Deposits mint shares at the prevailing exchange rate, so one sGHO does not represent a fixed one GHO. The governance-set savings rate accrues on-chain, replacing the legacy sGHO product's separately claimed Merit rewards. Deposited GHO stays in the vault, while the DAO funds yield separately.

The savings vault is non-slashable and distinct from Umbrella stkGHO, whose stakers absorb GHO-market deficits. Shares can be redeemed for GHO without a cooldown, subject to the vault's pause controls. Pharos records GHO as the wrapper's single backing asset, so the savings layer adds no collateral diversification. Holders remain exposed to GHO's underlying collateral and peg risk, alongside the vault's smart-contract controls and governance decisions over the savings rate.

gtusdcp-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet's curated USDC MetaMorpho V2 vault
gtusdcp-gauntlet.text: Gauntlet USDC Prime is the V2 line: three immutable Morpho vault deployments on Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum that turn USDC into curated exposure over permissioned Morpho Blue markets backed by blue-chip crypto and real-world asset collateral. Immutability is the strongest thing on the card. Each vault mints shares only against its chain-local USDC, the share-gate setters on the Ethereum V2 vault have been abdicated so the curator cannot switch on transfer gating, and the parameter Safes steer allocations and nothing else. The {{grade}} overall grade is held back by age rather than by structure: the binding cap is the implementation's short track record, with the USDC parent ceiling close behind. Backing and exit both lead the card, and economic control trails only narrowly because the allocation Safes remain concentrated. Share price appreciates on borrower interest, and withdrawals still depend on Morpho market liquidity and on the curator not having optimised the book into a queue at the wrong moment. Freeze exposure is inherited from Circle's authority over the USDC beneath the shares. The durable constraint is that the vault can never rate above the dollar it wraps.

sources.label: Morpho: Gauntlet USDC Prime V2 vault

gtusdc-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet's conservative USDC MetaMorpho vault
gtusdc-gauntlet.text: gtUSDC is the Ethereum-only V1 Morpho Prime vault curated by Gauntlet, an ERC-4626 wrapper compounding {{term:yield-bearing}}lending yield{{/term}} across vetted USDC markets on Morpho Blue. It is deliberately the conservative end of what a curated lending book can look like, and Pharos tracks it apart from the V2 vault at a different address. The {{grade}} overall grade is bound by its parent: a child cannot rate above the USDC it holds, and the card sits at that ceiling. Backing and exit both lead the card because the vault is immutable, mints shares only against USDC deposits, and redeems into whatever USDC liquidity the underlying Morpho markets can return. Economic control is the lowest of the three pillars, though only narrowly: the Gauntlet 4-of-7 Safe steers fees, caps, timelocks, and market allocation, and nothing else, with no holder-transfer gating anywhere in the verified source. The residual exposures are inherited rather than local. Circle can freeze the USDC beneath the shares, and withdrawals can queue when the curated markets are fully utilised. Share price appreciates on borrower interest, so the token trades above par by design, and the durable constraint is that its safety can never exceed Circle's.

sources.label: Morpho: Gauntlet USDC Prime V1 vault

yvusdc-yearn.title: Yearn USDC Vault
yvusdc-yearn.text: yvUSDC-1 is the canonical Yearn v3 USDC vault: an ERC-4626 {{term:yield-bearing}}share token{{/term}} whose price appreciates as Yearn's allocator rotates capital across governance-whitelisted strategies. The whitelist is broader than the book. Funded allocation has narrowed onto the Sky ecosystem with the Morpho leg revoked, so diversification here is a governance option rather than a present fact. Minting is deposit-only, the mint review closed out cleanly, and exits still queue against aggregate strategy liquidity, which matters in a drawdown. The interesting fact is the one that never moves: the {{grade}} overall grade is a ceiling rather than Yearn's own arithmetic, the rule that a child cannot rate above the parent it requires. Every pillar on this card scores above the grade the card is permitted to carry, which is the dependency graph doing exactly what it exists to do: hold a wrapper and you hold the wrapped thing's rating, on someone else's schedule.

aa-falconx-mev-capital.title: FalconX Credit Vault
aa-falconx-mev-capital.text: AA_FalconXUSDC is a Pareto credit-vault tranche: not a Falcon Finance stablecoin and not a MEV Capital strategy token, despite the naming fog. The underlying exposure is USDC lent into FalconX institutional credit lines through a Pareto credit vault curated by M11 Credit, and Pareto sends deposited USDC directly to the borrower, so the vault's asset is the FalconX receivable and the real risk is private-credit performance and monthly exit timing rather than peg arbitrage. The mint path is bounded: the tranche cannot mint itself outside the IdleCDO deposit path, and the CDO's upgrade authority sits behind a one-day timelock. The {{grade}} overall grade is held down by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three, since monthly redemptions through the vault credit line offer no comparable route out at the same notional, while the backing pillar is flagged because the reserve review covers only part of the envelope: no source publishes obligor or instrument weights for the underlying book. This is a lender's balance sheet tokenized, and the word USDC in the symbol should not lull anyone into reading it as cash.

vndc-jade-labs.title: VNDC Quarantined VND Token
vndc-jade-labs.text: VNDC spent years as the only VND stablecoin with material market presence, which makes its 2026 collapse into quarantine the more instructive. Vietnamese authorities arrested ONUS/VNDC-linked executives in March 2026 in a fraud and money-laundering investigation, with local reporting describing platform withdrawal disruptions, so {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and reserve claims moved from weakly attested to actively suspect. The disclosures had already shifted under holders' feet: VNDC 2.0 describes USDT/USDC smart-contract collateral pools rather than the VND bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} of the original pitch, self-reported by an issuer whose own website has been unreachable on repeated checks. Pharos quarantined the listing on 2026-07-15 because no permitted runtime source still reports a positive circulating supply or market cap. The aggregator figures that once diverged from on-chain supply now simply are not there. A dong rail that cannot prove its own existence is only a claim, and the people behind it are answering to prosecutors.

hkdr-rd-technologies.title: Missed the First Wave, Still in the Race
hkdr-rd-technologies.text: HKDR is the pre-launch HKD stablecoin from RD Technologies, a Hong Kong fintech founded by former HKMA chief executive Norman Chan, in the HKMA sandbox since 2024 but absent from the April 2026 first licence cohort. Its subsidiary RD InnoTech was in the first July 2024 cohort admitted to the HKMA stablecoin issuer sandbox, where it tested digital-asset trading rails and cross-border trade payments; the firm has been positioning for licensing under the Stablecoins Ordinance that took effect August 1 2025. On April 10 2026 the HKMA gazetted the first stablecoin issuer licences (FRS01 and FRS02) to Anchorpoint and HSBC, with RD InnoTech absent from that cohort. RD remains a credible later-license contender. A $40M Series A2 round in July 2025 and a memorandum of understanding with ZA Bank both point to a serious operational build-out, but the regulatory window has shifted to a slower queue: in June 2026 the HKMA said the remaining applications stay under review with no timetable for further grants. The entry remains pre-launch until licence issuance is confirmed. The eventual product still routes through HKMA-mandated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a regulated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window.

brd-volpon.title: Selic-Linked Yield, In a Token
brd-volpon.text: BRD is a Brazilian real stablecoin announced January 6 2026 by Tony Volpon, a former deputy governor of the Central Bank of Brazil, through his company CF Inovacao. The distinctive structural choice: BRD is backed by Brazilian National {{term:treasury}}Treasury bonds{{/term}} and explicitly designed to pass the Selic-linked yield, around 15% at announcement, back to holders rather than retaining it as issuer revenue. That is the same model Crown's BRLV already operates in institutional channels; Crown raised $13.5M from Paradigm in December 2025, but BRD is positioning as the first to make {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-sharing{{/term}} the primary product framing rather than a niche feature. The competitive set in Brazilian BRL stablecoins is small but real: Transfero BRZ, BBRL, BRL1, plus cREAL on Celo. The harder gate is Brazilian regulation: BCB's FX-classification regime took effect February 2 2026 and final Consulta Publica 111 output is still pending, which is why Volpon has not published a launch date alongside the announcement.

sources.label: CoinDesk: Former Brazil central bank official unveils real-pegged stablecoin with yield sharing

krw1-bdacs.title: Korea's First Bank-Backed Won Stablecoin, Stuck in PoC
krw1-bdacs.text: KRW1 is BDACS's KRW-backed stablecoin, developed with Woori Bank as the reserve custodian and launched on Avalanche in September 2025, but it remains in a proof-of-concept phase rather than public circulation. The structural advantages are real: real-time banking-API reserve attestation through Woori, KISA's endorsement of Avalanche for public-sector reliability, and a February 2026 Plume partnership that positions KRW1 as the Korean institutional settlement rail for tokenized RWAs (Plume hosted roughly $645M in tokenized assets at the time). The commercial gating is Korea's still-pending Digital Asset Basic Act framework, where BDACS is explicitly trying to make KRW1 the technical standard. The strategic weakness is distribution. BDACS is a B2B custodian without a consumer app or retail footprint, which makes KRW1 likely to win on the institutional side and lose to bank-led or super-app issuers if Korea's eventual framework favours retail surfaces. Real-time banking-API {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} runs through Woori Bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with KRW1 positioning itself as the settlement rail for Korean institutional {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} flows and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} routed through regulated banking channels.

rusd-revolut.title: Revolut Dollar Precedent From EURR
rusd-revolut.text: Revolut's USD stablecoin is still unannounced, and the August 2026 launch of its euro sibling made the shape of any dollar token considerably clearer, mostly by invalidating the assumption everyone was working from. The legal substrate looked settled: a MiCA CASP licence from CySEC in October 2025, plus Revolut's Bank-of-Lithuania EMI supplying the e-money-token issuer foundation MiCA Title IV requires. Then Revolut shipped EURR on August 26 and the issuer of record turned out to be Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg entity of Stripe-owned Bridge, under a CSSF licence, with Revolut Digital Assets Europe merely distributing. Revolut, holding every licence it needed to issue in-house, chose to rent the issuance instead. That reframes RUSD: the nearest live precedent for a Revolut dollar is a third-party regulated-issuer relationship, which trades balance-sheet control and reserve-disclosure ownership for speed to market. The counterparty question for RUSD therefore shifts to whether Revolut is content to have Stripe's infrastructure sitting between its 65 million users and their {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rights. Revolut's US path runs separately through an OCC charter application targeting a 2027 launch with stablecoin services from day one: third-party tokens, not confirmed own issuance. Ticker, chain, issuer entity, and reserve and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} disclosure model for a USD token all remain unannounced, and the euro launch suggests that reserve disclosure and custody will be the key uncertainties.

sources.label: FinTech Futures: Revolut launches euro-backed stablecoin EURR
Blockhead: Revolut launches EURR as it cuts off Tether across Europe

brl-itau.title: Brazil's Biggest Bank Waits for the Rulebook
brl-itau.text: Itau Unibanco, Brazil's largest private bank by assets, confirmed in April 2025 that it is evaluating its own stablecoin, with peg currency and design pending BCB regulation; Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes told a Sao Paulo industry event the bank is 'always open to understanding whether it makes sense for our clients to have a stablecoin, even one in real, within Itau'. The peg-currency choice (BRL or USD) is explicitly undecided and gated on the final shape of Brazil's regulatory framework via BCB Consulta Publica 111, especially the open self-{{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} question that Antunes flagged as a major design constraint. Itau already participates in the DREX wholesale CBDC pilot, providing distribution-rail experience but also a competing institutional product that may shape final positioning; primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} would presumably run through Itau's bank network. The placeholder is BRL-denominated because Brazil's retail base and Itau's franchise make a real-denominated launch the most likely first design, while Itau has not ruled out a USD-denominated option.

sources.label: CoinDesk: Brazil's largest bank Itau Unibanco mulls its own stablecoin

moveusd-cfx.title: CFX's Solana Deposit Dollar
moveusd-cfx.text: MoveUSD is a CFX-issued dollar settlement instrument on Solana with a DefiLlama supply feed and a live price path. The token is best read as tokenized-deposit infrastructure rather than a permissionless DeFi-native stablecoin: minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through the issuer for approved customers, while the SPL mint gives Pharos a concrete on-chain supply anchor. Reserves are described as U.S. dollar deposits held 1:1 in beneficiary accounts at an FDIC-member bank that CFX does not name, and no dated independent reserve report is public. The mint and freeze authorities sit with a program-controlled address, so issuance is concentrated and unreconciled, and backing and economic control both sit at the floor of the card. The detail page carries a tokenized-deposit caveat so users do not confuse the market cap with open retail redemption coverage.

hlusd-hela.title: HeLa's Native Runtime Dollar
hlusd-hela.text: HLUSD is the HeLa ecosystem's centralized dollar stablecoin and the chain's native gas token, admitted through CoinGecko because the HeLa chain is not yet a supported Pharos contract platform. CoinGecko reports a price and market cap, but contract-level supply and issuer reserve telemetry remain outside the supported chain set. HeLa's documentation states that HLUSD is fully backed by custodial USDC held at a licensed financial institution in Australia, which it does not name, and publishes no dated attestation or reserve-to-liability reconciliation. Issuance runs through on-chain MintProposer and MintVoter roles under an Admin that sets the quorum, the same role model can blacklist holders, and the upgrade authority is unknown. The asset is therefore classified as a centralized RWA-backed USD coin with an explicit unsupported-chain notice, and the exit pillar is the weakest line on its {{grade}} report card. Until the issuer publishes a verifiable {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and discloses {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path remains the dominant unknown.

xmd-metal-dollar.title: A Stablecoin Basket on XPR Network
xmd-metal-dollar.text: Metal Dollar is Metallicus's basket-backed dollar token on XPR Network, minted and redeemed 1:1 against whitelisted reserve stablecoins held in the xmd.treasury contract. Issuer materials describe a USDC, PYUSD, and Paxos-dollar basket, but Pharos' August 2026 on-chain read of the treasury tells a narrower story: about 96% is XUSDC, a Metallicus bridge wrapper over Circle's USDC, and the remaining roughly 4% is MPD, a Metallicus-issued dollar token that no public disclosure mentions and that carries no published backing. XMD is therefore a proportional claim on that two-asset basket, and its safety leans almost entirely on Circle plus the bridge wrapper's undisclosed upstream {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Control sits with a 2-of-4 Metallicus operator multisig that owns both the token and treasury contracts and can change the basket, and XPR Network's block producers can blacklist an account at the protocol level. Pharos admits the asset through CoinGecko's price and market-cap path because XPR Network is not a supported contract chain. Redemption is eligibility-gated, and exit and economic control both trail backing on the card. No dated independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} exists: the treasury is visible on-chain, but the wrapper reserves behind it are not.

sources.label: XPR Network: What is Metal Dollar (XMD)

vusd-virtue.title: IOTA-Backed CDP Dollar
vusd-virtue.text: Virtue USD is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on IOTA Rebased, minted by borrowing against {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} IOTA-family positions with {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} as peg defense, and a canonical wrapped copy on IOTA EVM through the network's native bridge. Pharos now reads the vaults directly: at the July 2026 capture, stIOTA made up roughly 97% of collateral, with small IOTA, vIOTA, and iBTC slices, so peg defense rests almost entirely on one liquid-staking derivative of a volatile Layer-1 and on single Pyth price feeds with no fallback. The package is immutable and no freeze or blacklist function exists, but an AdminCap held by a single address gates supply limits and module versions, which is why economic control is the weakest pillar on a card where exit also sits at the floor: no comparable exit route is supported and redemption depth is undisclosed. The peg itself has held on thin, single-source pricing. Sound {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics on a small chain still leave holders exposed to one collateral, one oracle path, and one admin key.

stusd-stoneyield.title: StoneYield BNB Chain Yield Wrapper
stusd-stoneyield.text: StoneYield USD is a BNB Chain yield wrapper over USDC and Venus-linked strategy positions. The reserve model points to USDC routed through StoneYield's StrategyRouter into a Venus-integrated vault, so stability depends on both the underlying stablecoin and the strategy wrapper doing what it says on the label. Pharos marks stUSD as yield-bearing and NAV-style because the holder is accepting vault mechanics, admin controls, and withdrawal liquidity risk in exchange for the yield path. The exit pillar is the weakest line on the card, since no comparable redemption route is disclosed. The token's admin role sits with a single delegated account that also owns the wrapper that issues it. StoneYield's site claims audited contracts but names no auditor, and no proof-of-reserves or {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} over the reserve path is published, so the {{grade}} overall grade rests on issuer documentation plus verified contract sources. CoinGecko supplies the market row; an independent reserve feed would make the entry less dependent on issuer-side framing.

lvusd-leverup.title: Monad Perps Collateral in Stablecoin Form
lvusd-leverup.text: LeverUp USD is a small Monad stablecoin tied to LeverUp's liquidity layer for perpetuals and margin trading; it is minted inside the trading engine when positions open against USDC collateral, so {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and reserve depth depend on a trading system rather than a bank balance sheet. CoinGecko reports a live price and market cap, and the Monad contract is included because Pharos already has a Monad chain entry. The risk profile is not comparable to a cash-backed issuer coin: the single transparency vault holds USDC, but trading gains or losses can change coverage, no legal custodian or segregation terms are disclosed, and public reserve depth is still thin. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the card, with effective minting scored as unbounded because issuance is gated only by the engine contract behind a 3-of-5 Safe, and the exit pillar fails for want of a comparable redemption route. Pharos therefore treats lvUSD as a notice-heavy crypto-backed stable asset rather than a conventional dollar reserve token.

nusd-nexus.title: Legacy Synapse Bridge Liquidity
nusd-nexus.text: Nexus USD is a legacy Synapse {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}-liquidity stable asset backed by a pool of DAI, USDC, and USDT, closer to bridge routing infrastructure than to a standalone modern issuer. It is included because DefiLlama still returns both a current price and circulating supply. Fixed-block reads of the Ethereum nexus pool in August 2026 put USDT at more than half of the basket with DAI and USDC splitting the rest, so the upstream reserve basket gives NUSD inherited freezability and stablecoin dependency risk. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that split: the economic-control pillar leads the card because the LP token and pool are fixed clones with no holder freeze path, while the exit pillar is the weakest of the three because no comparable same-notional redemption route is disclosed. The thirteen reviewed deployments are one native Ethereum LP token plus twelve bridge representations, so the Synapse bridge machinery carries the cross-chain risk.

brlm-mento.title: Mento's Brazilian Real Rail
brlm-mento.text: BRLm is Mento's oracle-priced Brazilian real on Celo, minted and burned against USDm through the Mento Broker at the BRL/USD SortedOracles rate and backed by the shared, diversified Mento reserve rather than by a BRLm-specific trove. Unlike the Mento {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} rows, this entry uses the reserve-wide Mento feed because the CDP trove API only covers GBPm, JPYm, and CHFm. The reserve is diversified but still a mix of AUSD, sUSDS, CELO, USDT, EURC, USDC, stETH, and smaller assets, so Pharos classifies collateral quality as mixed rather than fiat-reserve grade. The exit pillar is the strongest line on the {{grade}} card, since the Broker swap is permissionless, while economic control is the weakest: the binding cap is an oracle finding, because the BRL/USD feed has a single reporter with a 360-second window and no fallback, and the two-day Mento timelock can change the token's broker and upgrade the contracts. BRLm is small in absolute supply, but strategically useful because it adds another BRL rail from an already-modeled issuer family.

kesm-mento.title: First Kenyan Shilling Stablecoin Coverage
kesm-mento.text: KESm is the first Kenyan shilling-denominated stable asset in Pharos, admitted through DefiLlama's price and circulating-supply path. The token runs on Celo and is issued and retired through Mento's oracle-priced USDm/KESm Broker pool against the shared Mento Reserve, the same reserve-backed mechanism as the newer Mento local-currency suite. Because KES does not yet have a dedicated Pharos peg category, the asset is grouped under OTHER. The reserve risk remains driven by the Mento mix, especially CELO exposure and upstream centralized stablecoins. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the card, and the binding cap is the oracle: the Broker prices swaps from a single SortedOracles reporter with a six-minute expiry window and no second feed or failover. Mechanically KESm is reserve-backed inventory rather than a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}: there is no borrower trove or {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} path, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} means swapping back to USDm through the Broker at the oracle rate.

copm-mento.title: Mento's Colombian Peso
copm-mento.text: COPm is Mento's oracle-priced Colombian peso stablecoin on Celo, minted and burned through the Mento Broker against the shared Mento Reserve rather than fiat held in a bank. That reserve is a mixed basket of other stablecoins with a CELO wildcard: AUSD and sUSDS are the largest slices, USDT, EURC, and USDC sit behind them, and CELO plus a little stETH and ETH make up the volatile tail, all readable live from the Mento reserve API. The backing and exit pillars both grade well on that visibility, and the token contract itself has no blacklist, freeze, or pause function. The {{grade}} overall grade is capped by the oracle: the USDm/COPm exchange prices off a single SortedOracles reporter with a 360-second expiry and no second feed, which Pharos treats as a binding single-source topology. Economic control is the weakest of the three pillars, with the Broker and token upgrade path sitting behind a two-day Mento timelock. Pharos has limited price coverage for the asset, so the peg line rests on thin observation. COPm is a small first Colombian peso reference; the durable constraint is that one reporter stands between the reserve and the price.

cadm-mento.title: Mento's Canadian Dollar Rail
cadm-mento.text: CADm is Mento's oracle-priced Canadian dollar stablecoin on Celo, issued and retired against USDm through the Mento Broker at the CAD/USD SortedOracles rate and backed by the shared Mento reserve rather than Canadian bank reserves. It was added mainly for ecosystem completion rather than market size, and circulating supply is small next to the Canadian-issued CAD stablecoins Pharos tracks. The collateral story is therefore Mento reserve exposure: a basket of AUSD, sUSDS, CELO, USDT, EUROP, EURC, USDC, stETH, and ETH held in the on-chain reserve under Mento governance, which Pharos classifies as mixed rather than fiat-reserve grade, so resilience depends on Celo, Mento governance, and that {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} basket. The {{grade}} overall grade is driven by exit, the weakest of the three pillars: {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps rather than fiat off-ramps, and Pharos has not established a viable exit path for the tracked supply. Economic control is also capped by an oracle finding, since the CAD/USD feed has a single reporter and no failover. Backing is the strongest line on the card, which says more about the shared reserve than about CADm's own market.

audm-mento.title: Mento's AUD Completes Another Local Rail
audm-mento.text: AUDm is Mento's crypto-backed Australian dollar on Celo, minted by depositing USDm as Liquity-v2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral against the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} Mento reserve mix. It is distinct from the already tracked Macropod AUDM despite the shared ticker style. It is admitted through DefiLlama and a verified Celo contract, with live reserve visibility through the shared Mento dashboard. The supply is small, so the value is mainly comparative: users can now see Mento's AUD rail beside larger AUD issuers and the rest of the Mento FX set. Reserves remain mixed and on-chain rather than an Australian-dollar banking stack.

ghsm-mento.title: Mento's Cedi Stable
ghsm-mento.text: GHSm is Mento's Ghanaian cedi stablecoin on Celo, swapped into and out of existence through Mento's broker pool against USDm and backed by the shared Mento Reserve, a mixed basket of tracked stablecoins such as AUSD, sUSDS, USDT, and EURC alongside CELO and staked ETH. GHS does not yet have a dedicated Pharos peg category, so like KESm and COPm the token is grouped under OTHER. What the card shows is a reserve-backed FX stable whose exit pillar leads, with permissionless swaps back to USDm through the broker, while backing and economic control trail it: the token sits behind a Mento timelock with the veMENTO governor as sole proposer, and Mento's published plan keeps GHSm on the older V2 pool while GBPm and others move to the borrower-CDP model. The {{grade}} overall grade also carries a short track record. The durable constraint is upstream: GHSm is only as sound as the Mento Reserve basket and the oracle rate that prices cedi against it.

zarm-mento.title: Mento's Rand Stable Asset on Celo
zarm-mento.text: ZARm is Mento's South African rand stable asset on Celo, issued and retired through an oracle-priced USDm/ZARm Broker pool rather than against rand bank collateral. Its backing is the shared Mento Reserve: a basket of AUSD, sUSDS, USDT, EUROP, EURC, and USDC alongside CELO, stETH, and ETH, self-custodied in protocol contracts under a 48-hour governance timelock. Reserve quality is therefore the Mento basket's quality, and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} risk sits on that basket rather than on the South African banking system. Pharos already tracks a larger ZAR issuer; ZARm mainly lets readers compare Mento's local-currency model across regions. The {{grade}} overall grade is driven by the exit pillar, which sits at the bottom of the scale: no viable exit path is established for the token, and Mento governance is winding down the V2 Broker pools with per-token trading limits capped at outstanding supply plus 10%. Backing and economic control both grade far higher, so the constraint is the exit route rather than the reserve. The peg line on the card is strong, but price coverage is limited and the token has one Celo deployment with no cross-chain route.

sources.label: Mento stable assets on Celo (protocol documentation)

wbrl-ripio.title: Ripio's Wrapped Brazilian Real
wbrl-ripio.text: WBRL is the Brazilian real token in Ripio's wFIAT suite, natively issued on Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis at one deterministic address, with Celo and HyperEVM deployments added in September 2026, and moved between chains through Ripio's first-party burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail. It gives Pharos a second BRL rail from a Latin American issuer alongside larger BRL assets already tracked. Reserve evidence is a single sole-practitioner certification as of 31 March 2026 that reconciled about 719,000 outstanding wBRL to roughly R$810,000 in an unnamed Brazilian bank account, expressly not an audit, with nothing newer published since. The weak point has shifted from missing evidence to concentrated control: one Ripio key holds mint, upgrade, and pause roles across the original six deployments, with unbounded and unverified reconciliation, so economic control is the weakest pillar on the card even though secondary exit scores well. Ripio's materials also conflict on whether ordinary holders have any direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right, leaving exits to secondary markets and Ripio's own on/off-ramp. Local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at one undisclosed bank is the durable constraint.

sources.label: Independent public accountant certification for wBRL - March 2026

wclp-ripio.title: First Chilean Peso Runtime Row
wclp-ripio.text: WCLP is Ripio's wrapped Chilean peso token and gives Pharos active CLP exposure even though the peg still sits under the broader OTHER bucket. The product is issuer-managed local-currency infrastructure: Chilean-peso cash and liquid instruments behind a 1 WCLP = 1 CLP target, deployed across the same EVM footprint Ripio uses for its wFIAT suite. The useful part is runtime coverage through DefiLlama price and circulating value plus consistent contract addresses across supported chains. The weak part is reserve transparency, because public materials describe custody and redemption in broad terms without a reliable per-token attestation feed. WCLP expands the map, but it does not yet make the reserve evidence any less local and issuer-shaped.

wcop-ripio.title: Ripio's Colombian Peso wFIAT Token
wcop-ripio.text: WCOP is Ripio's Colombian peso wFIAT token, added through DefiLlama's price and supply coverage with verified native deployments on six EVM chains. It overlaps thematically with Mento COPm but uses a different issuer model: off-chain local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing and issuer-native issuance on each chain, linked by Ripio's own burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail, rather than Celo's Mento reserve. COP is still grouped under OTHER pending broader peg-currency support. Reserve evidence has improved but stays thin: a March 2026 accountant certification reconciles outstanding wCOP to a Colombian bank statement, yet it is expressly not an audit, the bank is unnamed, and ordinary holders have no documented direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} right. One Ripio key also holds mint and upgrade roles on every deployment, which is why economic control is the weakest of the three pillars on the card.

sources.label: Independent public accountant certification for wCOP - March 2026

wpen-ripio.title: Peruvian Sol Coverage from Ripio
wpen-ripio.text: WPEN adds Peruvian sol exposure to Pharos through Ripio's local-currency wFIAT suite, extending Latam fiat coverage across six EVM chains without a per-token reserve attestation. DefiLlama supplies price and circulating-supply data, and Ripio's same-address deployment pattern lets Pharos track native issuance on Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis, linked by Ripio's own burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail. PEN is grouped under OTHER because it does not yet have a dedicated peg category. Reserve transparency is the limiting factor: Ripio's attestation archive publishes certifications for wARS, wBRL, wCOP, and wMXN but none for wPEN, so the backing model is described under issuer {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with no {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} public enough to verify {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} capacity. A single Ripio key also holds mint and upgrade roles on each of those six deployments, which leaves economic control the weakest of the three pillars.

jaaa-janus-henderson-anemoy.title: AAA CLO Exposure as a Tokenized Fund
jaaa-janus-henderson-anemoy.text: JAAA is a NAV-accreting Janus Henderson AAA CLO fund share issued through Anemoy and Centrifuge rails, permissioned and KYC-gated rather than a $1 redeemable stablecoin. Pharos treats the Chainlink NAV feed as live reserve evidence, while the reserve-risk model stays conservative because even AAA CLO tranches are structured credit rather than cash or Treasury bills, and the feed proves the share value without publishing security-level holdings. The token has multi-chain contract coverage, but the exit pillar is the weakest line on the card: primary-market access is whitelisted, so no comparable open exit route exists for a holder outside it. Mint authority runs through Centrifuge's ward system to a 4-of-9 protocol Safe, which keeps the economic-control pillar well short of the top of the range. The fund share is {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} structured-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}, with Centrifuge {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and permissioned {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at NAV rather than open par exit.

acrdx-anemoy-apollo.title: Apollo Credit Through Anemoy
acrdx-anemoy-apollo.text: ACRDX is a permissioned, NAV-accreting share token from Anemoy and Centrifuge giving on-chain access to Apollo's diversified private credit strategy, not a par stablecoin or cash-like asset. ACRDX packages Apollo Diversified Credit Fund exposure into an Anemoy tokenized share class. The backing spans private corporate direct lending, asset-backed lending, performing credit, and opportunistic credit sleeves, so Pharos classifies the reserves as high-risk {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} credit rather than cash-like collateral. Chronicle proof-of-asset coverage provides useful NAV visibility, but {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} remains a permissioned fund process.

stac-securitize.title: CLO Fund Access on Securitize
stac-securitize.text: STAC is a Securitize-issued tokenized fund share for a BNY-advised AAA CLO portfolio, which makes it dollar-denominated without making it a dollar. The token is priced by fund NAV and investor access runs through Securitize's qualification, transfer-control, and primary-market process, so there is no open $1 redemption backstop hiding behind the ticker. Chronicle proof-of-asset coverage improves transparency around the fund exposure, but Pharos still treats the collateral as high-risk structured credit rather than cash-like reserves. Backing is the strongest pillar; exit and economic control are both weak, because the Solana leg that holds most STAC liabilities is not separately attested and its program upgrade authority is a single key with no timelock, shared with the controller that mints VBILL. The distribution story has broadened: the fund expanded to Solana in June with Ethena committing $250 million, and issuer Securitize is now a public company. Its Cantor SPAC merger closed in early July and the stock trades on the NYSE as SECZ after raising roughly $400 million. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that a AAA label on the portfolio does not answer the question a stablecoin dashboard has to ask, which is whether holders can exit when they need to.

sources.label: Securitize expands STAC to Solana with $250M Ethena allocation (PRNewswire, 2026-06-12)
Securitize lists on NYSE as SECZ as $400M SPAC deal closes (Bitcoin.com News)

hlscope-hamilton-lane.title: Hamilton Lane Private Credit Rail
hlscope-hamilton-lane.text: HLSCOPE is Hamilton Lane's Senior Credit Opportunities Fund tokenized through Securitize as a feeder LP interest for qualified purchasers, priced at fund NAV rather than $1. Subscriptions are monthly and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs on demand at the previous quarter's NAV through Securitize's permissioned rail, so the asset belongs in the NAV-token cohort rather than among open-liquidity stablecoins. Reserve risk is high because the backing is a single slice of feeder exposure to floating-rate senior secured private loans, valued monthly by Hamilton Lane's own valuation team with no independent reserve audit. The exit pillar is the weakest line on the {{grade}} report card: access is eligibility-gated and the issuer publishes no fund-specific default workout or recovery waterfall. Economic control is the strongest pillar, reflecting the regulated fund structure with Brown Brothers Harriman as depositary, though issuance and upgrades on the four EVM deployments run through one owner key shared across chains. Distribution now spans Ethereum, Polygon, Optimism, Plume, and Tron, with Wormhole interoperability advertised but no HLSCOPE-specific bridge controller yet verified. This is an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share on {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} rails, and the qualified-purchaser gate is its durable constraint.

pc0000031-tradable.title: Tradable Rent-Financing Term Note
pc0000031-tradable.text: PC0000031 is a KYC-gated Tradable senior secured term note on a North American rent-financing platform, tokenized on zkSync and contract-priced at $1.00 note par with no liquid secondary market. Pharos tracked it as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} private-credit note ({{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure) with CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage but zero reported volume, no reliable public APY or cashflow feed, and no {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop, because there is no public primary redemption route comparable to issuer stablecoin redemption. Minting runs through Tradable's permissioned DealManager, where two EOAs hold immediate mint permission and one of them also controls the shared token and DealManager beacons. Pharos delisted the entry in July 2026 as out of scope: a permissioned, deal-specific private-credit ownership note priced at contractual par is not a transferable stable-value monetary instrument.

pc0000033-tradable.title: Par Value, Private Credit
pc0000033-tradable.text: PC0000033 is a Tradable senior secured term-note token backed by APAC consumer-financing receivables, including line-of-credit and BNPL exposure, with the notes issued by Victory Park Capital Advisors. It is contract-priced at note par and not defended by a liquid secondary-market peg: while tracked, CoinGecko showed a par price and market cap with zero 24-hour volume. Minting is permissioned through Tradable's zkSync deal machinery, where two EOAs hold immediate mint permission and one also controls the shared token and DealManager beacons, and no public yield source has been identified. Pharos delisted the entry in July 2026 as out of scope: a permissioned, deal-specific private-credit ownership note priced at contractual par is not a transferable stable-value monetary instrument. The token is private-credit infrastructure whose value rests on note servicing and repayment.

pc0000101-tradable.title: Legal Finance at Par
pc0000101-tradable.text: PC0000101 is Tradable's tokenized exposure to a Victory Park senior post-settlement legal-financing facility for a U.S. law firm. The token is priced at $1 note par by contract and issuer servicing rather than by a liquid market defending a payment-stablecoin peg. While listed, Pharos treated the CoinGecko price as a private-credit reference point and flagged zero reported volume rather than implying deep exit liquidity. The reserve is a single high-risk legal-finance receivables slice, minted only through Tradable's permissioned zkSync issuance path. Pharos delisted the token on 15 July 2026 as out of scope: a permissioned, deal-specific private-credit ownership note priced at contractual par is not a transferable stable-value monetary instrument. It remains a securitized receivable wearing dollar notation, useful if you want that risk and misleading if you wanted cash.

pc0000089-tradable.title: Residential Credit, Tokenized
pc0000089-tradable.text: PC0000089 is a Tradable token for a Latin American residential-lending senior secured term-loan note, issued through Victory Park and represented on zkSync. The $1 reference is contract par rather than a market-cleared stablecoin peg, and Pharos keeps that distinction visible because private credit does not become cash by wearing two decimal places. The collateral is a single high-risk LatAm residential credit exposure with centralized issuer controls and permissioned minting through Tradable's DealManager, where two issuer EOAs hold immediate mint permission. While listed, CoinGecko reported a $1 price and market cap against zero volume, and no public yield row was ever integrated, so the dashboard never presented it as liquid or income-transparent. Pharos delisted the token on 15 July 2026 as out of scope: a permissioned, deal-specific private-credit ownership note priced at contractual par is not a transferable stable-value monetary instrument. It remains a credit note first and an on-chain asset second.

asusdf-astherus.title: Astherus Yield Wrapper
asusdf-astherus.text: asUSDF is Aster's staked wrapper over USDF, so the wrapper share accrues yield while the base stablecoin risk remains USDF's Ceffu, Binance, and MirrorX strategy stack. Deposits mint asUSDF against USDF, and exits return USDF only after Aster's documented waiting period, which is not quite the same thing as instant dollar liquidity no matter how smooth the UI feels. Pharos captures the reserve dependency as 100% wrapped USDF rather than pretending the wrapper has an independent balance sheet. The extra yield comes from delta-neutral and funding-fee strategies upstream, meaning asUSDF is best read as USDF plus queue risk, role-controlled wrapper minting, and a little more patience demanded from anyone leaving.

mf-one-midas.title: Fasanara F-ONE tokenized strategy certificate
mf-one-midas.text: mF-ONE is a Midas tokenized certificate over Fasanara's F-ONE strategy, spanning fintech receivables, SME lending, real-estate-backed credit, and digital-asset strategies. That makes it a permissioned NAV product, not a bank-reserve stablecoin, and the daily price story comes from strategy valuation rather than a hard $1 redemption floor. Pharos gives it a live valuation route through the Midas transparency setup, while still marking the collateral as high-risk because private credit plus digital-asset strategy exposure is not the conservative end of the menu. Issuance and redemption run through Midas rails, with upgrades and admin rights concentrated behind the Midas control stack. The product is sophisticated, but its centralization and portfolio opacity remain material constraints. Those constraints matter more than the strategy's packaging when assessing the token's NAV exposure.

mglobal-midas-fasanara.title: Receivables, With Rails
mglobal-midas-fasanara.text: mGLOBAL is Midas's tokenized certificate over Fasanara's global private-credit strategy, largely short-dated trade receivables and digital invoices from SMEs. It accrues NAV through issuer-priced portfolio performance, so it is not a fixed $1 payment stablecoin. Pharos models the reserve as a single high-risk Fasanara strategy slice and surfaces the contract-priced strategy-token warning because secondary-market volume is thin. The Midas attestation engine provides daily NAV and proof tooling, but primary issuance and redemption remain permissioned through Midas rails, and the exit pillar is the weakest line on the card. Utility improved in June when mGLOBAL went live as collateral on Aave's Horizon RWA market, giving the certificate its first serious borrowing venue. The appeal is access to an asset-backed lending portfolio; the cost is issuer discretion, private-credit opacity, and a 1-of-3 admin Safe that can rotate mint operators immediately.

sources.label: Midas: mGLOBAL is now live on the Aave Horizon RWA market

mhyper-midas.title: Hyperithm Market-Neutral Certificate
mhyper-midas.text: mHYPER is a Midas tokenized debt instrument tracking Hyperithm-managed market-neutral stablecoin strategies across on-chain markets and institutional execution venues. The mechanism is daily NAV appreciation, not a fixed $1 peg, and tokenholders hold a subordinated claim against Midas rather than ownership of the underlying assets. Pharos can value it through the Midas attestation stack and Chainlink-verified NAV route, but the reserve is still one high-risk strategy sleeve held under Fordefi MPC custody with issuer-admin controls. Primary mint and redeem access is permissioned for greenlisted users, with instant exits relying on Midas Staked Liquidity rather than an unconditional cash floor. The strategy label is market neutral; the holder's exposure is to Midas as obligor and to venues it does not name, and with the position book and the primary exit route both undisclosed, Pharos leaves the card unrated.

mmev-midas.title: Strategy Wrapper, New Driver
mmev-midas.text: mMEV is a Midas NAV token whose original strategy manager no longer runs it: Midas ended its MEV Capital partnership in February 2026 and handed strategy and risk oversight to RockawayX. The token accrues through NAV appreciation and mints or redeems through Midas rails rather than through an open par redemption path built for payments. Daily self-reported Midas transparency gives Pharos a valuation route, but the underlying strategy remains a high-risk, dynamically allocated DeFi book whose current positions, venues, and custodians are not disclosed, and the live reserve feed still carries the MEV Capital label while the post-RockawayX allocation is unverified. The primary exit route is undisclosed, so the card is unrated for insufficient evidence. Mint operators sit behind 1-of-3 admin Safes with immediate rotation rights and two-day timelocked upgrades on each of three native chains. The wrapper survived its manager; what it has not yet produced is a position inventory under the new one.

mapollo-midas.title: Apollo Crypto Strategy via Midas
mapollo-midas.text: mAPOLLO is the Midas liquid-yield wrapper for an Apollo Crypto managed strategy, distinct from the Apollo credit fund and from a transactional stablecoin. Its value follows NAV appreciation through permissioned Midas mint and redeem rails, while the reserve risk is high because the backing is digital-asset strategy exposure rather than cash or bills. Pharos keeps the self-reported Midas transparency and NAV route in view, but that does not make the underlying strategy any less manager-dependent. The signed final terms describe a market-neutral mandate across spot, lending, arbitrage, derivatives, and token rewards without publishing the current positions, venues, or custodians, and the primary exit route is undisclosed, so Pharos leaves the card unrated until that evidence appears. Tokenized strategy access is the product; a published position inventory and a comparable exit route are what it still lacks.

safo-spiko-usd.title: Spiko Smart Cash USD Share Class
safo-spiko-usd.text: SAFO is the USD share class of Spiko and Amundi's Smart Cash exposure, built around fully collateralized overnight total-return swaps rather than direct T-bill ownership. Pharos classifies the reserve as medium-risk RWA strategy exposure because the holder is exposed to fund structure, the swap counterparty (currently BNP Paribas), collateral packages, and regulated NAV mechanics. The AMF/UCITS context and the CACEIS depositary help. PwC's statutory opinion does not exist yet because the fund's first financial year has not closed, and none of that turns a fund share into a simple par-redeemable stablecoin. Primary market access remains permissioned through Spiko rails, with subscriptions and redemptions happening at fund NAV. The token is issuer-minted natively on seven chains under Spiko's permission manager, so no third-party bridge carries the claim. The {{grade}} overall grade is held back by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three, which is where that eligibility-gated primary market shows up. SAFO is conservative by DeFi standards and still a fund share, and the ticker does not change that.

spkcc-spiko.title: Regulated Cash-and-Carry Fund Share
