spkcc-spiko.text: SPKCC is the dollar share class of Spiko's Digital Assets Cash & Carry Fund, a French professional-fund vehicle whose NAV comes from BTC and ETH {{term:basis-trade}}basis trades{{/term}} rotated against short-duration T-bills. It is a fund share carrying a stablecoin's ticker rather than a dollar promise. The institutional plumbing is unusually complete for crypto carry: Marex as sole strategy counterparty, Coinbase for spot {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, CME for cleared futures, and CACEIS Bank as depositary striking a daily NAV. Pharos read the fund prospectus and the AMF's register of authorised management companies directly; together they establish prudential supervision through the manager and a recurring, independently administered reconciliation. Two caveats travel with that. The prudential hook is the AIFM, depositary, and distributor, since the FPS vehicle itself is not AMF-authorised, and reporting is annual with the first financial year closing in December 2026, so PwC's statutory opinion does not yet exist. Meanwhile the reserve side remains one unsplit strategy envelope; Pharos knows the fund is doing carry and knows nothing about the current spot, margin, or venue weights. Exit is the weakest pillar because primary access is eligibility-gated at NAV, which is what holds the {{grade}} overall grade back, and regulated sophistication does not close the transparency gap on the reserve side.

eursafo-spiko.title: EUR Smart Cash Through Spiko
eursafo-spiko.text: EURSAFO is the euro share class of Spiko and Amundi's Smart Cash fund, an AMF-authorized UCITS structure that behaves like a NAV-accreting fund token rather than a bank-deposit stablecoin. The reserve is fully collateralized overnight total-return swap exposure with a tier-1 bank counterparty, currently BNP Paribas, with CACEIS Bank as depositary, so Pharos treats it as medium-risk RWA strategy exposure instead of pretending it is a plain euro cash account. Regulated French fund status helps, but the independent check is still prospective: PwC is the statutory auditor and the fund's first financial year has not closed, so no audit certification exists yet, and subscriptions and redemptions run through KYC-gated Spiko rails. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that split: backing and economic control lead the card, while exit, gated by eligibility, is the weakest pillar. It is conservative by crypto standards and still absolutely a fund share, which is the sort of nuance stablecoin tickers tend to flatten on contact.

eurspkcc-spiko.title: Euro Carry, Fund First
eurspkcc-spiko.text: EURSPKCC is the euro share class of Spiko's Digital Assets Cash & Carry Fund, a French FPS alternative investment fund rather than a euro payment token: NAV accrues from fund performance and primary access is KYC-gated through Spiko's transfer rails, so it reads as a fund share with euro accounting. The {{grade}} overall grade rests on two artefacts: the fund prospectus naming CACEIS as daily administrator and depositary, and a dated AMF register export confirming the manager's portfolio-management authorisation. The euro side's own disclosure is thin. Its live share-class feed publishes a single undifferentiated cash-and-carry line with no constituent weights, and its NAV travels through one permissioned administrative valuation path rather than a redundant feed, which is why economic control and exit both sit near the bottom of the card. The assurance cadence is annual and still prospective: PwC is the appointed statutory auditor, but the first financial year does not close until December 2026, so the only recurring independent check is the depositary's daily NAV rather than an audit opinion. Regulated packaging around crypto {{term:basis-trade}}basis{{/term}} exposure is useful; the exposure underneath remains a crypto strategy whose positions Spiko does not itemise.

uktbl-spiko.title: Sterling T-Bills, Gated
uktbl-spiko.text: UKTBL is Spiko's GBP-denominated UK Treasury-bill money-market fund share, not a dollar product and not a retail payment stablecoin. The backing is dull by crypto standards: short-dated UK T-bills with a settlement cash buffer, run as an AMF-authorised UCITS short-term VNAV money-market fund with PwC as statutory auditor, though the audit reports are available on written request rather than published. The tradeoff is access, because subscriptions, transfers, and redemptions are KYC-gated through Spiko fund rails at NAV rather than settled by permissionless on-chain arbitrage, which is why exit is the weakest of the three pillars behind the {{grade}} overall grade. Pharos treats the collateral as low-risk tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure while keeping centralized issuer controls, blacklistability, and the single-key minter accounts on Starknet and Stellar visible. The reserves are boring in the best possible way; the operating model is fund administration with a token attached.

sources.label: Spiko SICAV prospectus (PwC statutory auditor, art. 24)

gbpsafo-spiko.title: GBP Smart Cash Share Class
gbpsafo-spiko.text: GBPSAFO is the GBP share class of Spiko's AMF-authorized UCITS Amundi Smart Cash {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}}, a permissioned NAV share that accretes value from a fully collateralized overnight total-return swap. The reserve description follows the same swap structure as the USD and EUR SAFO classes, so the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} risk model is medium: returns depend on a swap counterparty and a collateral basket marked daily, with a UCITS depositary in between, and the fund's first financial year has not closed, so no auditor certification exists yet. The {{grade}} overall grade is set by the exit pillar, the weakest of the three by a wide margin: subscriptions and redemptions are KYC-gated through Spiko's transfer rails at published NAV, no comparable same-notional route is disclosed for secondary holders, and the token has only a short implementation history. The token is best understood as a permissioned fund share for onboarded investors, and its constraint is access: outside Spiko's KYC perimeter there is no documented way out at NAV.

eur0-usual.title: Usual's Euro Treasury Wrapper
eur0-usual.text: EUR0 is Usual's euro stablecoin, minted on Ethereum against tokenized Eurozone T-bill collateral, in practice Spiko's EUTBL, through Usual's collateral module, with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} swapping EUR0 back into that collateral through the dApp. The reserve thesis is a {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-bill fund dependency rather than a euro bank-deposit account: on-chain reads show the EUR0 collateral treasury holding EUTBL and nothing else, with supply reconciled against it, so EUR0 is an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-backed dependency token whose backing rests on Spiko's fund and its undisclosed depositary. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects three pillars clustered in the middle of the range, and economic control shows the sharpest concentration: two Usual modules hold the mint role, but the same 8-of-15 Safe can add minters and replace the token implementation, and the token carries an admin-managed blacklist. Market coverage is thin, with a single-source price feed and no depeg episode on record, and the token is recorded as a MiCA non-compliant e-money token. What Pharos shows is a fully reconciled one-asset reserve sitting behind an issuer that can expand minting at will.

emxn-telcoin.title: Telcoin's Mexican Peso Cash Token
emxn-telcoin.text: eMXN is Telcoin's centralized Mexican peso stablecoin on Polygon, extending the Digital Cash model from eUSD into peso settlement with reserves that are issuer-reported and carry no public per-token feed. The issuer framing is bank-style payment infrastructure rather than a permissionless {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}, so reserve confidence depends on Telcoin's off-chain controls and reporting: the terms describe segregated accounts at regulated financial institutions but name no institution, and the monthly attestations Telcoin says it will publish had not appeared in the reviewed materials. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits with the issuer and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Telcoin's wallet rails, at 1:1 for verified account holders with a 0.15% fee, a $2,000 per-transaction cap, and one to three business days to settle. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects that gap: the exit pillar is the weakest on the card, backing is graded on an undisclosed composition, and no depeg episode is on record across more than two years of tracking, though price coverage is single-source.

hchf-hedera-swiss-franc.title: Hedera's Small CHF Experiment
hchf-hedera-swiss-franc.text: HCHF is HLiquity's Swiss-franc synthetic on Hedera, minted against overcollateralized HBAR troves in a Liquity-style design rather than issued from a regulated franc account. Borrowers create HCHF from HBAR positions at a 110% minimum collateral ratio, undercollateralized troves are liquidated through the Stability Pool, and face-value redemptions against collateral are the peg-defense mechanism. The upside is unusually clean on-chain control: the Hedera token has no admin, freeze, wipe, or pause key, every mint-critical contract has renounced ownership, and Pharos marks governance as immutable-code rather than issuer discretion, which is why economic control leads the {{grade}} report card. The downside is equally plain: collateral is volatile HBAR priced through Pyth with a Supra fallback, liquidity is tiny, and the exit pillar is the weakest of the three. Anyone expecting the comfort of a Swiss bank attestation will not find one; the durable constraint is that the franc claim is only as good as HBAR and the pools that hold it.

eurot-token-teknoloji.title: Token Teknoloji's Euro Token
eurot-token-teknoloji.text: EUROT is Token Teknoloji's centralized euro stablecoin issued from Turkey, deployed on Ethereum, Avalanche and Polygon and described as backed 1:1 by euro bank reserves at Ziraat Participation Bank and Akbank. The reserve evidence is thin: the proof-of-reserves page is shared across seven tokens, the bank letters it links are bare balance certificates dated 2024, and no current balances, bank split or {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} feed are published, so backing is graded on an undisclosed composition. The {{grade}} overall grade is pulled down further by exit, the weakest pillar: holders can trade through Bitlo, but no direct redemption route is disclosed and no comparable same-notional exit exists on record. Economic control is the strongest of the three pillars, though issuance sits with single externally owned accounts that can mint without an on-chain cap, and the contracts carry an issuer-controlled external transfer rail whose counterparts are unidentified. The peg has no episode on record over three years of tracking with single-source coverage. EUROT gives Pharos long-tail euro coverage; what it does not give is a dated reserve statement or a modeled way out.

mxne-real-mxn.title: Brale and Etherfuse's MXN Rail
mxne-real-mxn.text: MXNe is a Mexican peso token issued by Brale in partnership with Etherfuse, deployed on Base, Solana, and Stellar with issuer-managed mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Brale onboarding. The backing is the Etherfuse CETES Stablebond, a token over short-duration Mexican federal Treasury bills held at regulated Mexican {{term:custody}}custodians{{/term}}, mostly BBVA Mexico, through INDEVAL. BHR Mexico publishes monthly reasonable-assurance {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} reconciling CETES tokens in circulation to backing assets, but that examination covers Etherfuse's whole CETES program rather than an MXNe-specific ledger, so Pharos records the backing category without an MXNe balance claim. The {{grade}} overall grade reflects an exit pillar that is the weakest of the three, with redemption gated to onboarded customers, and a backing pillar held back by limited evidence. Control risk is concrete: on each chain a single issuer-controlled key holds all mint and admin rights, and the Base contract is an upgradeable proxy under that key. The durable constraint is that the reserve assurance belongs to Etherfuse while the token liability belongs to Brale.

sources.label: BHR Mexico reasonable-assurance report dated July 24, 2026

wmxn-ripio.title: Ripio's Mexican Peso wFIAT Token
wmxn-ripio.text: wMXN completes the tracked Ripio wFIAT set with a Mexican peso asset deployed across the same EVM footprint as WBRL, WCLP, WCOP, and WPEN. DefiLlama provides the live price and circulating-supply path, while Ripio's local-stablecoin page describes 1:1 local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing and on/off-ramp {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, with Ripio's own burn-and-mint {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} rail between deployments. Reserve evidence is thin rather than absent: a March 2026 accountant certification reconciled outstanding wMXN to a Mexican bank statement, but it is expressly not an audit, the bank is unnamed, and holders have no contractual on-chain redemption right. The same Ripio key holds mint and upgrade roles on every native deployment, which is why economic control is the weakest of the three pillars on the card.

sources.label: Independent public accountant certification for wMXN - March 2026

jpyt-dephaser.title: A High-Risk Yen Synthetic
jpyt-dephaser.text: JPYT is Dephaser's yen-pegged token on Base and Optimism, minted against locked USDT or USDC priced through an FX oracle, with thin liquidity and high-dependency collateral. The locked stablecoins are routed into Aave rather than held directly, making the reserve view dependency collateral rather than a cash yen reserve. Price and market-cap coverage are present, but the supply is small and the peg depends on Dephaser's mechanism, USDT collateral quality, and thin secondary liquidity. Economic control is the weakest pillar on the card: a single EOA per chain administers the mint role and can grant itself unbounded minting, and the deposit managers holding the collateral are upgradeable by Dephaser's own admin keys. The mechanism is closer to {{term:algorithmic}}algorithmic{{/term}} FX synthesis than fiat backing, with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} returning the locked USDT or USDC collateral rather than yen cash.

euro3-3a-dao.title: A Tiny Overcollateralized Euro CDP
euro3-3a-dao.text: EURO3 is 3A DAO's {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} euro {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin on Polygon and Linea, minted against whitelisted crypto and stablecoin collateral in user-owned vaults and burned when borrowers repay or redeem. The {{grade}} overall grade is driven by one pillar: exit is the weakest of the three by a wide margin because no viable exit path is established, with negligible market depth and a redemption route that depends on protocol conditions being met. Backing is comparatively the strongest of the three pillars: a live read of both vault factories valued total collateral in the tens of thousands of euros, the bulk of it Mendi meUSDC receipts on Linea with WETH and WBTC making up most of the rest, so the collateral is real but small and leans on a single lending market wrapped around freezable USDC. Economic control sits between the two: the token contracts are immutable with no freeze or blacklist hook, but the minter registry is owned through a proxy by a single externally owned account with no multisig, and every collateral price runs through one Chainlink EUR/USD denominator with a 24-hour staleness bound and no fallback. The peg record shows no episode, which says more about the absence of trading than about the design. Until depth exists, EURO3 is a working mechanism without a market.

xofm-mento.title: Mento's CFA Franc Stable
xofm-mento.text: XOFm is Mento's West African CFA franc stablecoin on Celo, minted and burned through the Mento Broker: a USDm-to-XOFm swap burns the incoming USDm and mints XOFm at the XOF/USD oracle rate, the reverse burns XOFm back into USDm, and every swap passes spread, trading-limit, freshness, and circuit-breaker checks. There is no trove, health factor, or {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} path; the claim sits on the shared Mento Reserve, a diversified basket that at the July 2026 read was roughly a quarter AUSD, a quarter sUSDS, a sixth CELO, and the rest USDT, EURC, USDC, stETH, and ETH. That composition is the trade-off. The swap path is permissionless and the token contract exposes no blacklist or freeze, with governance changes gated by a two-day timelock, which is why exit and economic control lead the card. Backing is the weakest of the three pillars because a material share of the reserve is volatile CELO and ETH exposure, and Pharos records a bounded unresolved reserve exposure on top. The durable constraint is that XOFm's franc peg is only as good as an oracle feed and a crypto-heavy shared reserve.

xnk-kinka.title: Japanese Gold Bullion Token
xnk-kinka.text:
Kinka's XNK represents one fine troy ounce equivalent of 99.99% Japanese-brand physical gold bullion, issued on Ethereum and Cardano against centralized issuer custody.

The whitepaper places the bars with Loomis International under Gold Management LLC, and the reserve model treats the backing as physical gold with centralized custody and issuer-controlled exchange terms. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} into physical bars is possible only through the documented KYC process and size thresholds, and no dated XNK-specific reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} was located in the issuer's published materials. On 18 August 2026 the issuer announced final exchange trading suspensions and set 30 October 2026 deadlines for buyback and gold-exchange requests, and Pharos delisted XNK the same day. What remains is a wind-down window in which holders must act through the issuer's buyback or gold-exchange process before the deadline passes.

sources.label: Kinka Gold issuer delisting and wind-down notice

gynusd-gyndore.title: The cbBTC-Only CDP
gynusd-gyndore.text: gynUSD is a pre-launch CDP stablecoin built around a single, blunt proposition: cbBTC is the only collateral. By focusing exclusively on Bitcoin through Coinbase's wrapper, Gyndore sidesteps the generalized risk models that force multi-asset lending markets into conservative LTV ratios. It then passes the capital efficiency benefit directly to borrowers, with a 110% minimum collateralization ratio enabling up to 90.91% LTV. Seventy percent of borrow fees flow to Stability Pool depositors, removing the idle-liquidity drag that burdens pool-based lending markets. The governance story has two possible endings depending on launch conditions: the protocol can either start with a bootstrapping admin key and transition to GYND token governance once the fee switch triggers, or mint GYND from day one if pre-launch capital formation is sufficient. The Pareto Controller constrains GYND voters to ±10bps rate adjustments and requires 80% consensus. This governance behaves more like a thermostat than a parliament. The cbBTC dependency is the structural asterisk: Coinbase custody sits at the base of every loan, so the trust-minimized pitch has a ceiling.

tgld-tenbin.title: Synthetic Gold Debt-Note
tgld-tenbin.text: tGLD is Tenbin's tokenized gold note, but unlike PAXG or XAUT it holds no vaulted metal. Each token is a Tenbin AssetCo (BVI) debt-note representing the U.S.-dollar value of one troy ounce of gold, collateralized by USDC and hedged with CME gold futures rather than allocated bullion. Mint and redemption are KYC-gated through a Controller and a backend signer that holds the on-chain minter role, and redemptions settle in a USD stablecoin instead of physical metal. Launched on Ethereum mainnet in February 2026 after a $7M Galaxy Ventures-led seed and four security audits, it remains in private beta with a small float, its only public market a near-dormant Uniswap V4 pool and no independent proof-of-reserves attestation. In May 2026 Tenbin retired LayerZero and moved tGLD's cross-chain messaging to Chainlink CCIP; a staked yield variant (stGLD) and testnet FX siblings (tBRL, tMXN) round out the roadmap. Pharos lists tGLD as pre-launch until its public price feed updates frequently enough to clear the gold pricing-freshness gate.

sources.label: CoinDesk: Galaxy Digital leads $7M investment in Tenbin

ejpy-jbfd.title: The Trust-Bank Yen That Skips the Cap
ejpy-jbfd.text: EJPY is Japan Blockchain Foundation's pre-launch yen stablecoin, and its whole pitch is a legal classification: a trust-type Type III electronic payment instrument that escapes the ¥1M-per-transaction ceiling JPYC has spent years working around. JBFD, the consortium operator behind Japan Open Chain, would be the settlor, with reserves parked in a licensed trust bank that, as of the May 2026 announcement, it is still negotiating with and has not named. That gap is the tell: trust-segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and statutory {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rights are the entire value proposition, yet the trustee, the reserve mix, and the launch date are all blank. The plan is to issue on Japan Open Chain first and Ethereum next, sometime within fiscal 2026 (which runs through March 2027), aimed squarely at B2B settlement rather than retail DeFi. EJPY is a credible institutional play in a market suddenly crowded with yen-stablecoin contenders. JPYSC, JPYC, and a megabank consortium all circle the same FSA framework. Right now, this is a decision to issue, not a token you can hold.

aed-rakbank.title: The First Commercial-Bank Dirham
aed-rakbank.text: AED-RAKBANK is RAKBank's pre-launch dirham stablecoin, notable less for what it is than for who is issuing it: the first conventional commercial bank to win CBUAE in-principle approval for an AED payment token, as opposed to the digital-bank and sovereign-wealth vehicles (Zand AED, AE Coin, the FAB/ADQ/IHC effort) that got there first. The January 2026 nod arrives under the UAE's Payment Token Services Regulation, which permits payment use only for dirham-backed tokens and demands a published white paper plus full reserves. RAKBank's plan ticks the regulatory boxes: it calls for 1:1 dirhams in segregated regulated accounts, full par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, audited contracts, and real-time reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. However, 'in-principle' is doing heavy lifting: no ticker, no chain, no issuing subsidiary, and no launch date have been disclosed, and the regulation may force RAKBank into a separate licensed issuer it hasn't confirmed. Pharos tracks the AED peg as OTHER until dirham support is built. A pilot is promised 'in due course,' which in regulatory dialect means watch this space.

bils-bitsofgold.title: Israel's First Regulated Shekel
bils-bitsofgold.text: BILS is the first shekel stablecoin to clear an Israeli regulator, and unlike most entries on this list it is approved rather than merely announced; Bits of Gold spent two years in a sandbox before the Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority signed off in April 2026. The conditions are unusually concrete for a pre-launch asset: 1:1 New Israeli Shekel backing held in segregated bank accounts inside Israel (foreign custody explicitly barred), an Ernst & Young audit, Fireblocks issuance infrastructure, and QEDIT zero-knowledge privacy, all on Solana via token extensions. Reach is limited: the regulator required a deliberately gradual, small-scale rollout, and Bits of Gold announced in July 2026 that the pilot was complete and BILS was moving to wide distribution, with roughly 100,000 BILS minted on Solana by early August. That throttled debut, plus a peg Pharos doesn't yet price (tracked as OTHER until shekel support lands), is exactly why it sits in pre-launch rather than the live table. Note the regulatory lane: the approval is under the CMISA rulebook, while the broader Israeli Stablecoin Law is still stuck in draft. A real, audited, regulator-blessed shekel, just not one you can buy in size yet.

sources.label: Bits of Gold announces move to wide distribution of BILS
CoinDesk: Israel approves its first regulated stablecoin (2026-04-28)

autousd-auto-finance.title: An Autopool Dollar Wrapper
autousd-auto-finance.text: autoUSD is Auto Finance's USDC autopool share token on Ethereum: holders own a vault receipt rather than a fiat-reserve stablecoin, and the share price is expected to rise as strategy earnings auto-compound. The protocol documentation describes autopools that rebalance across eligible DeFi destinations in search of stronger risk-adjusted returns, so the dollar anchor comes from USDC as the vault asset while the extra risk comes from destination selection, liquidity, and controller operations. Pharos reads the Ethereum contract directly for supply and price, and Royco Dawn's senior/junior tranche market wraps the same vault token. The overall grade is {{grade}}, with backing the strongest of the three pillars and exit the weakest. Pharos records no established viable exit path; withdrawals redeem shares for USDC subject to autopool liquidity and destination unwinds rather than through an issuer's redemption desk. The economic control pillar is little better: any of four emergency-pauser accounts can halt every holder transfer, and a 6-of-11 Safe governs the proxy upgrade path. The durable constraint is structural: this is a strategy wrapper over USDC rather than a redeemable issuer dollar.

eearn-ember.title: Ember's Royco-Listed Vault Share
eearn-ember.text: eEARN is Ember's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} USDC vault share on Ethereum, an ERC-4626-style token whose value follows the vault's USDC share price rather than a flat par claim; Royco Dawn wraps the same token into senior and junior tranche vaults. The card behind the {{grade}} overall grade splits sharply. Backing and economic control lead the card: on-chain reads confirm the vault's only asset is USDC, the pause flags are off, and withdrawal fees are zero. The exit pillar is the weakest of the three by a wide margin, because withdrawals go through an operator-batched request queue with no proven settlement bound and no fixed redemption window. Issuer control is real but narrow: the protocol config can blacklist accounts at deposit, withdrawal, and queued-settlement time, and the implementation can be replaced through a timelock whose proposer, executor, and canceller roles each sit with a single externally owned account behind a one-day delay. The vault's current strategy holdings, custody terms, and any independent reconciliation are not disclosed, and upstream USDC freeze exposure passes straight through.

dusd-dialectic.title: Dialectic's Book, Tokenised
dusd-dialectic.text:
DUSD is a USDC-accounted Makina strategy share whose price follows Dialectic's marked AUM per share rather than a fixed dollar claim. The portfolio rotates through DeFi venues under an approved instruction set, and Pharos can read first-party live accounting for its allocations, debt, supply, and NAV.

The exit route now has a live same-block capacity bound, calculated as idle Ethereum USDC minus the liability of DUSD already locked in the queue. That backlog-adjusted number is a conditional liquidity proxy and carries no reserved buffer or funding promise. The reviewed contract processes request IDs sequentially and currently charges no redemption fee, while the Machine Terms grant neither a contractual redemption right nor queue priority; finalization has no maximum SLA, requests may remain unfilled indefinitely, and the operator may cease the Machine without notice. That queue is why the exit pillar is the weakest of the three and why the {{grade}} overall grade sits where it does. Custody is equally blunt: Dialectic owns deposited and deployed assets outright, holders receive no trust, proprietary, priority, or bankruptcy-remote claim, and the optional Security Module carries no contractual backstop obligation. DUSD itself has no reviewed local freeze path, but upstream USDC can still be frozen; Recovery Mode cannot move Circle-frozen funds, and wallet or request-NFT transfers remain subject to verification and discretionary fill, leaving thin DEX liquidity and the issuer queue as two versions of the same exit problem.

ousd-open-standard.title: The Everything-Consortium Dollar
ousd-open-standard.text: Open USD is what happens when 140-plus of the biggest names in payments and banking, including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Stripe, BlackRock, BNY Mellon, and Coinbase, decide they would rather split reserve income among themselves than hand it to Circle. Announced June 30, 2026 and operated by an independent company, Open Standard, whose board is drawn from its own partners, OUSD promises fee-free minting, no volume limits, and most of the reserve yield routed back to the businesses that adopt it. The pitch is GENIUS Act compliance and neutral, shared governance; the reality, still, is a launch announcement with no mainnet contracts, named custodian, or attestation. Markets took it seriously anyway. Circle's stock fell roughly 15-17% on the news, even though some OUSD backers such as BlackRock and BNY are also core partners in Circle's own ecosystem. The unresolved question is the one that has dogged every mega-consortium before it: 140 partners are easy to announce and very hard to align. Launch is promised 'later in 2026,' natively on Solana, with Stellar and Plasma named as launch partners. As of mid-August, the token still isn't live.

sources.label: Blockhead: Visa, Stripe, BlackRock among 140 firms backing Open USD

rd-rai-dollar.title: RAI, Finally Pinned to a Dollar
rd-rai-dollar.text: RAI proved a stablecoin could be steered by an on-chain controller rather than a committee, and the market followed the redemption price faithfully; that price was not a dollar, and most of the market could not get past it. RAI Dollar keeps the machinery and pins the target. RD is an immutable CDP stablecoin on Ethereum where a PI controller reads a 24-hour TWAP of the market price and moves one system-wide borrow rate, bounded to 0.25-50% APY around a 2% bias, until supply and demand pull the price back to $1, with Liquity's redemption arbitrage as the floor. The par lever RAI made famous survives, bounded to $0.75-$1.30 and moving no faster than a tenth of a cent an hour, held for the extremes rather than left to float. Collateral sits in eight isolated branches: WETH, wstETH, rETH, weETH, WBTC, tBTC, sUSDS, and PAXG, each with its own troves, stability pool, and shutdown path. The question Liquity V2 left open is answered by routing a slice of healthy-branch fees to repair an undercollateralized branch rather than convening a vote. Borrowers who dislike the redemption queue can pay a floating Redemption Shield surcharge that funds a matching discount for everyone who does not. All of it is still theoretical: no contracts are deployed, the address registry reads TBD, the core repository is private, and the audits, part-funded by an August 2026 Ethereum Foundation subsidy, are still in progress. Immutability cuts both ways, and whatever ships is what runs, permanently.

sources.label: RAI Dollar docs: How it stays stable

eurr-revolut.title: The Neobank That Rented Its Own Coin
eurr-revolut.text: EURR is live, and Pharos tracks it pre-launch anyway. Revolut launched it on August 26 2026 as the first product of a stablecoin programme long assumed to be arriving in dollars or sterling, phased into Denmark, Poland, and Portugal with the rest of the EEA promised later in the year. The structural surprise is the issuer: Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg arm of Stripe-owned Bridge, holds the EMI licence and MiCA authorisation from the CSSF, while Revolut Digital Assets Europe distributes under its CySEC permission and Revolut's own Lithuanian EMI stays out of issuance. Europe's biggest neobank built the distribution and outsourced the balance sheet: the same Bridge Open Issuance model behind MoneyGram's and Deel's tokens, now wearing a consumer brand with 80 million customers behind it. The timing is not subtle either: EURR arrived as Revolut finished pulling Tether's USDt from European retail on August 31, so the euro rail it removed and the euro rail it added are the same shelf. Supply went from a few hundred tokens at launch to more than a million within two weeks, which is a rollout rather than adoption. MiCA does not force reserve composition, custodians, or {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence into public view; all remain undisclosed, and no accepted price source resolves the token, which is why it sits here rather than in the tracked set. A stablecoin distributed by a bank, issued by a payments company, and priced by nobody is a fair snapshot of where regulated euro tokens currently are.

sources.label: FinTech Futures: Revolut launches euro-backed stablecoin EURR
Blockhead: Revolut launches EURR as it cuts off Tether across Europe
